title: fix: enforce complete tenant isolation with API tokens only for WPP endpoints
body:
fix: enforce complete tenant isolation with API tokens only for WPP endpoints

SECURITY FIX - Prevents tenant impersonation vulnerability

Before this fix:
- /wpp/* endpoints accepted both JWT and API tokens
- tenantId from request body could override token's tenant
- Tenant A could perform operations as Tenant B by specifying different tenantId

After this fix:
- All /wpp/* endpoints ONLY accept X-API-Key header (API tokens)
- JWT Bearer tokens are rejected with clear error message
- tenantId is ALWAYS extracted from API token, body parameter ignored
- Complete tenant isolation: one token = one tenant, always

Changes:
- whatsapp.controller.ts:
  - Replaced JwtOrApiTokenGuard with ApiTokenGuard (28 endpoints)
  - Removed @Roles decorators (no longer needed)
  - Simplified getTenantId() to only use req.tenantId
  - Removed redundant tenantId validation checks
  - Cleaned up unused imports (JwtOrApiTokenGuard, Roles)

- api-token.guard.ts:
  - Improved error messages with specific hints
  - "X-API-Key header is required" instead of generic error
  - "Invalid or expired API token" with helpful hint
  - Added req.authType = 'api-token' for future use

Impact:
- Admin users must create tenant API tokens to perform WPP operations
- Maintains backward compatibility (body tenantId silently ignored)

**Trade-offs**:
- ✅ Simpler build (no compilation issues)
- ✅ Faster build time (~40s vs ~5min with tsc)
- ✅ Consistent dev/prod behavior
- ⚠️ Slightly higher memory usage (ts-node + deps)
- ⚠️ Transpilation overhead at startup (~1-2s)

fix: clear orphaned Redis locks on worker-session startup

Added automatic cleanup of session locks in boot-restore to prevent
reconnection failures when worker-session is restarted.

Problem: When worker-session crashes or is rebuilt, distributed locks
in Redis are not released, causing boot-restore connects to fail with
"failed to acquire lock, session may be owned by another worker".

Solution: Clear all `session-lock:*` keys from Redis before enqueuing
boot-restore connects. This ensures clean startup and automatic device
reconnection.

- --flag=value (used by npm scripts and workflow)
- --flag value (space-separated)

This ensures the full tag (production-719baa566...) is correctly parsed
from workflow arguments and used consistently across build, push, and deploy.

```typescript
export interface CreateActionDto {
  ...
  deviceId?: string;
  name?: string;
}
```

Adiciona sistema completo de autenticação via API tokens para acesso programático à API, permitindo testes de eventos sem OAuth do Google.

## Funcionalidades Implementadas

### Sistema de API Tokens
- Geração segura de tokens com SHA-256 hashing
- Formato: `tok_{prefix}_{secret}` (64 chars de entropia)
- Tokens exibidos apenas uma vez na criação
- Validação via Authorization header: `Bearer tok_...`
- Suporte a expiração configurável
- Tracking de último uso (lastUsedAt)

### Autenticação Dual (JWT + API Token)
- Guard global unificado: JwtOrApiTokenGuard
- Suporta tanto JWT (Google OAuth) quanto API tokens
- Detecção automática pelo formato do token
- Suporte ao decorator @Public() para rotas públicas
- Logging detalhado para debugging

### Arquitetura
- ApiTokensModule marcado como @Global para DI em toda aplicação
- JwtModule configurado e exportado para uso por guards
- Guard substituído globalmente em main.ts
- Removidos guards redundantes de controllers (usando global)

### Segurança
- Tokens nunca armazenados em texto plano (apenas hash SHA-256)
- Validação de expiração automática
- Tokens podem ser revogados (campo active)
- Rate limiting aplicado em endpoints sensíveis

### Integração com Workflows
- WhatsappService usa API tokens de devices
- Workflows executam ações usando tokens configurados
- Mensagens enviadas via SDK com autenticação por token

feat(worker-session): Phase 1 - WhatsApp ban prevention with exponential backoff

Implements critical fixes to prevent mass reconnection incidents and WhatsApp bans (statusCode 405).

## Changes

### Prisma Schema
- Add DeviceStatus enum: connecting, qr, open, closed, reset, **banned**
- Add Device.lastError field to store ban/error messages
- Applied with `prisma db push` (development)

### SessionManager (apps/worker-session/src/session.ts)

**New Properties:**
- `reconnectAttempts: Map<string, number>` - Track retry count per tenant
- `lastReconnectTime: Map<string, number>` - Timestamp of last attempt
- `bannedTenants: Set<string>` - Set of banned tenant IDs

**Constants:**
- MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 5
- BASE_BACKOFF_MS = 3000 (3 seconds)
- MAX_BACKOFF_MS = 300000 (5 minutes)
- CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RESET_MS = 3600000 (1 hour)

**New Methods:**
- `getBackoffTime(tenantId)` - Calculates exponential backoff: 3s → 6s → 12s → 24s → 48s
- `shouldAttemptReconnect(tenantId)` - Circuit breaker pattern with auto-reset after 1 hour

**Connection Handler Updates:**
1. **405 Ban Detection** (line 353-382):
   - Detects WhatsApp ban (statusCode 405)
   - Marks device as 'banned' in database
   - Updates lastError field
   - Adds to bannedTenants set
   - **STOPS reconnection immediately**
   - Logs clear intervention instructions

2. **Exponential Backoff** (line 427-450):
   - Replaces fixed 3s timeout with progressive delays
   - Increments attempt counter
   - Logs detailed backoff info (attempts, backoff time, next attempt)

3. **Circuit Breaker** (line 427):
   - Checks shouldAttemptReconnect() before scheduling
   - Opens after 5 failed attempts
   - Auto-resets after 1 hour of inactivity
   - Logs clear message when open

4. **Counter Reset** (line 453-457):
   - Clears reconnection counters on successful connection
   - Removes from bannedTenants set
   - Clears lastError in database

## Behavior

### Scenario 1: Temporary Connection Failure
- Attempt 1: Fail → wait 3s → retry
- Attempt 2: Fail → wait 6s → retry
- Attempt 3: Fail → wait 12s → retry
- Attempt 4: Fail → wait 24s → retry
- Attempt 5: Fail → wait 48s → retry
- Attempt 6: **Circuit breaker opens** → stops trying
- After 1 hour: Circuit breaker resets automatically

### Scenario 2: WhatsApp Ban (405)
- Detects statusCode 405 immediately
- Device status → 'banned'
- lastError → "WhatsApp ban detected (statusCode 405)"
- **Stops reconnection immediately** (no backoff attempts)
- Requires manual intervention: POST /admin/wpp/tenants/{tenantId}/reset
- Recommended: Wait 30-60 minutes before resetting

### Scenario 3: Successful Connection
- Resets all counters (reconnectAttempts, lastReconnectTime)
- Removes from bannedTenants
- Clears lastError in database
- Normal operation resumes

## Testing

✅ Docker build successful (no-cache)
✅ Container starts without errors
✅ QR codes generating normally
✅ Prisma Client regenerated with new schema
✅ No type errors or runtime crashes

**Validation pending**:

- Circuit breaker opens after 5 attempts (requires sustained failures)
- 405 detection stops reconnection (requires actual ban)

- docs/PROGRESS.md - Phase 7 completed
- docs/PREVENTION_PLAN.md - Phase 1 implementation details
- docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md - Issues #1-4 addressed

## Impact

🔴 CRITICAL: Prevents infinite reconnection loops
🔴 CRITICAL: Stops ban worsening with immediate 405 detection
🟢 IMPROVEMENT: Progressive backoff reduces WhatsApp spam detection
🟢 IMPROVEMENT: Auto-recovery after 1 hour (circuit breaker reset)

**Erro**: `Nest can't resolve dependencies of the DispatchEventHandler (?)`

**Causa**: Multi-stage Dockerfile gera Prisma Client no Debian (glibc) mas executa no Alpine (musl)

- `native` (Debian/glibc para build)

pinging WhatsApp devices from painel-cliente.

- SDK ping() required tenantId parameter in URL: /wpp/ping/:tenantId

- API token already identifies the tenant (embedded in token)

4. When 515 follows pairing: immediate reconnect without counting as failure
5. When 515 without pairing context: treat as normal failure

feat(events): implement dual-phase event emission system for WhatsApp callbacks

Implement comprehensive event emission system that emits events at two stages:
1. Immediate emission when webhook callback is received
2. Processed emission after data is persisted to database

This enables workflows to react to both raw WhatsApp events and processed events
with database consistency guarantees.

Changes:

**CallbackController** (`callback.controller.ts`):
- Inject WebhookEventsService for event emission
- Emit raw WhatsApp event immediately after saving to WhatsAppEventLog
- Events include original payload and metadata (source, deviceId, headers)
- Allows workflows to react in real-time to all WhatsApp events

**EventProcessorService** (`event-processor.service.ts`):
- Inject WebhookEventsService for event emission
- Emit 'message.processed' event after successfully saving Message/Chat/Lead
- Includes structured data (messageId, chatId, leadId, text, etc)
- Provides database consistency guarantee for workflows

**Event Types** (`event-types.ts`):
- Add WhatsApp raw event types (messages.upsert, connection.update, etc)
- Add processed event types (message.processed, chat.processed, etc)
- Add descriptions for all new event types

**Benefits**:
- ✅ No event duplication (original vs .processed are different event types)
- ✅ Workflows can choose raw (immediate) or processed (consistent) events
- ✅ All WhatsApp events trigger workflows, not just processed ones
- ✅ Error detection: missing .processed event indicates processing failure
- ✅ Complete event traceability through system

**Event Flow**:
```
/wpp/callbacks → WhatsAppEventLog → emit(messages.upsert)
    ↓ (1 minute later)
EventProcessor → Message/Chat/Lead → emit(message.processed)
```

**Root Cause**: Baileys library emits messages.upsert events with fromMe=false
for group messages even when the participant is the device's own LID.

**Investigation Results**:
- Database: Messages with participant=deviceLid had fromMe=false ❌
- EventLog: Baileys raw events showed fromMe=false for device messages ❌
- Webhooks: Filter service correctly extracted fromMe but value was false ❌

**The Fix**:
1. Detect when msg.key.participant === sock.user.id (device LID)
2. Override fromMe to true for database persistence
3. Apply correction to Redis Pub/Sub events (webhooks, SSE, workflows)
4. Add debug logging when correction occurs

**Impact**:
✅ Webhooks with fromMe=true filters now trigger for device group messages
✅ Workflows with fromMe=true triggers work correctly
✅ Database accurately reflects message ownership
✅ Advanced webhook filtering works as expected

**Files Changed**:
- apps/worker-session/src/session.ts:602-686
  - Added deviceLid detection in messages.upsert handler
  - Corrected fromMe for database persistence

- EventListener → DISABLED → no duplicate execution

deep copy of all related entities.

  - Deep copies all actions (preserves execution order)
  - Does NOT duplicate executions (historical data)

**Frontend (painel-cliente)**:
- Added `duplicate()` method to workflowsApi.ts
- Added "Duplicar" button with FiCopy icon in workflows table menu
- Added `handleDuplicate()` handler with success/error toasts
- Auto-refreshes workflow list after duplication

**Key Implementation Details**:
- Workflow name appended with " (cópia)" to avoid confusion
- Trigger statistics reset (totalExecutions, successCount, failureCount)
- Action `order` field preserved to maintain execution sequence
- Uses Prisma `$transaction` to ensure all-or-nothing duplication
- Permission check ensures users only duplicate their own workflows

**Example**: Duplicating a workflow with 3 triggers and 5 actions
creates a complete copy with all configurations intact.

body:
fix(worker-session): only reconnect devices with valid credentials in bootRestore

Previously bootRestore would enqueue connect jobs for ALL tenants,
causing infinite QR generation cycles for unpaired devices.

Now it:
- Queries devices with their WaAuth count
- Only reconnects devices with >1 WaAuth records (paired)
- Or devices with status='open' and at least some auth
- Skips devices in 'qr' or 'closed' status without valid credentials

This prevents unnecessary resource consumption and improves stability
when new devices are added to the system.

feat(ai-assistant): implement AI Assistant module with multi-provider support

Implements a complete AI Assistant module for the Panel Client with:

**Architecture:**
- Multi-provider LLM abstraction (Claude, extensible to Groq/OpenAI)
- Hybrid strategy (fast model for simple queries, smart model for complex)
- Factory pattern for easy provider switching via environment config

**Features:**
- 30+ tools covering Leads, Workflows, WhatsApp, Analytics
- Tools executor using Panel SDK (respects ACL, reuses existing APIs)
- Session management with Prisma (persistent conversation history)
- Type-safe TypeScript implementation end-to-end

**Backend Components:**
- `ai-assistant.module.ts` - NestJS module
- `ai-assistant.service.ts` - Main orchestrator
- `ai-assistant.controller.ts` - REST API endpoints
- `providers/` - LLM provider abstraction layer
  - `llm-provider.interface.ts` - Base interface
  - `llm-provider.factory.ts` - Factory with hybrid strategy
  - `claude/claude.provider.ts` - Claude implementation (Sonnet + Haiku)
- `tools/` - Tool execution layer
  - `tools-registry.ts` - 30+ tool definitions
  - `tools-executor.service.ts` - Executes via Panel SDK
- `sessions/` - Session management
  - `session.service.ts` - Prisma-based persistence
- `dto/` - Request/Response DTOs
- `prompts/system-prompt.ts` - AI context and behavior

**Database:**
- `AIAssistantSession` - Conversation sessions
- `AIAssistantMessage` - Message history
- `AIAssistantToolLog` - Tool execution logs

**Configuration:**
- Environment variables for provider selection
- Hybrid strategy with complexity detection
- Rate limiting support

**API Endpoints:**
- POST /ai/chat - Send message to assistant
- GET /ai/sessions - List user sessions
- POST /ai/sessions - Create new session
- DELETE /ai/sessions/:id - Delete session
- GET /ai/sessions/:id/messages - Get session messages
- GET /ai/stats - Usage statistics

**Tools Available:**
- Leads: list, get, create, update, delete, assign
- Workflows: list, get, execute, toggle, stats, executions
- WhatsApp: list chats, send messages, manage devices
- Analytics: dashboard stats, message stats, events
- Navigation: suggest URLs for visual tasks

**Benefits:**
- ✅ Respects ACL (uses user JWT for all operations)
- ✅ No business logic duplication (all via Panel SDK)
- ✅ Extensible (easy to add new providers/tools)
- ✅ Type-safe (TypeScript end-to-end)
- ✅ Cost-optimized (hybrid strategy)
- ✅ Production-ready (comprehensive error handling)

**Next Steps:**
- Frontend implementation (React/Chakra UI components)
- Add Groq provider for free tier option
- Implement streaming responses (SSE)

title: fix(database): prevent PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion
body:
fix(database): prevent PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion

## Problem
- CallbackController created new PrismaClient on each webhook request
- Each PrismaClient creates ~10 connections by default
- Under load (100+ webhooks/min), this caused connection exhaustion
- Production was at 82% capacity (41/50 connections)

## Solution
- Convert ad-hoc PrismaClient to singleton pattern in CallbackController
- Use double-checked locking to prevent race conditions
- Add connection_limit=3 for the singleton client
- Implement OnModuleDestroy for proper cleanup

## Additional fixes
- Update Dockerfiles to remove local .env files during build
- Fix deploy script build args for VITE_* variables
- Add proper env var handling for frontend builds

## Multi-tenant safety
- Singleton is safe because PrismaClient is stateless
- Each query always filters by tenantId explicitly
- No data cached between requests - only connection pool reused

title: fix(security,perf): implement critical security hardening and memory leak fixes
body:
fix(security,perf): implement critical security hardening and memory leak fixes

## Security Improvements

### CRITICAL Fixes
1. **CORS Security** (main.ts)
   - Replaced `origin: true` with explicit whitelist
   - Added CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS env var support
   - Production requires explicit configuration (throws if not set)
   - Development defaults to localhost origins

2. **Session Secret Requirement** (main.ts)
   - Production requires SESSION_SECRET (min 32 chars)
   - Production requires JWT_SECRET
   - Warns if REFRESH_TOKEN_SECRET not set
   - Added validateSecurityConfig() function

3. **Cookie Security** (main.ts)
   - Added sameSite: 'strict' for CSRF protection
   - Custom session name 'painel.sid' (avoids fingerprinting)
   - Proper httpOnly and secure settings

4. **API Token Encryption** (whatsapp-devices.service.ts)
   - Encrypts API tokens before database storage
   - Decrypts on retrieval
   - Backward compatible with plain-text tokens
   - Uses existing EncryptionService

5. **Admin Email Config** (auth.service.ts)
   - Moved hardcoded email to DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAILS env var
   - Supports comma-separated list
   - Case-insensitive matching

6. **Refresh Token Security** (auth.service.ts)
   - Added getRefreshTokenSecret() with proper fallbacks
   - Requires secret in production

### HIGH Priority Fixes
7. **Rate Limiting** (app.module.ts, auth.controller.ts)
   - Multi-tier throttling (short/medium/long)
   - Global ThrottlerGuard via APP_GUARD
   - Strict limits on auth endpoints (login, forgot-password, reset-password)
   - Health endpoint exempted

## Architecture Improvements

8. **Event Listener Memory Leak Fix** (session.ts)
   - Added sessionCleanupFunctions Map to track cleanup
   - Created registerListener() helper with auto-tracking
   - Added cleanupSessionListeners() method
   - All 16 event listeners now properly cleaned up
   - Called in resetSession() and disconnectSession()

## New Tests (29 tests)

- main.spec.ts (8 tests): CORS, cookies, security validation
- auth.service.spec.ts (10 tests): tokens, admin email, secrets
- whatsapp-devices.service.spec.ts (11 tests): encryption, decryption

## New Environment Variables

```env
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://panel.wpp.bb.catalisa.app
DEFAULT_ADMIN_EMAILS=admin@company.com
SESSION_SECRET=<min 32 characters>
```

- POST /agents/:id/duplicate - Clone agent
- GET /agents/available-tools - List builtin tools
- GET/POST /agents/:id/tools - Manage agent tools
- POST /agents/:id/chat - Chat with agent
- POST /agents/:id/test - Test agent without persistence
- GET /agents/:id/conversations - List conversations
- GET /agents/:id/stats - Usage statistics
- GET /agents/:id/executions - Execution logs

## Services
- AgentsService: Main CRUD operations
- AgentExecutorService: LLM + tool execution

title: fix(workflows): correct conditional branch skipping in workflow execution
body:
fix(workflows): correct conditional branch skipping in workflow execution

Bug: When viewing workflow execution history with IF-ELSE conditionals,
both branches were showing as executed (green) even when only one branch
should have run.

Root cause:
1. Backend: The execution.service.ts relied on `branch.targetActionId` in
   the action config to determine which branches to skip. But the frontend
   saves branch targets in the layout edges, not in the config.
2. Frontend: The loadHistoricalExecution function was adding ALL action IDs
   to executionOrder, including skipped actions.

Fix:
1. Backend: Now reads branch targets from layout edges (sourceHandle: "branch-N")
   instead of depending on config. Also creates WorkflowActionLog with status
   'skipped' for actions that are not executed.
2. Frontend: Filters out skipped actions from executionOrder so edges don't
   highlight incorrectly.

the change automatically.

with an optional version input for rollbacks.

title: fix(workflows): fix DAG cascading skip + default branch resolution in execution engine
body:
fix(workflows): fix DAG cascading skip + default branch resolution in execution engine

Two bugs in the branch-gating logic of the DAG execution engine:

1. Cascading skip: when a CONDITIONAL action was itself skipped (because
   it depended on a non-taken branch of a parent CONDITIONAL), actions
   depending on its branches would see `undefined` in the
   conditionalBranchTaken map and proceed to run instead of being skipped.
   Now checks the skipped set and propagates the skip.

2. Default branch resolution: the `:default` branch suffix only matched
   `takenBranch === -1` (no branch matched). But when the last branch is
   explicitly matched by name, takenBranch is the actual index (e.g. 1),
   not -1. Now resolves `default` to the actual last branch index.

Validated by 26/26 E2E tests (24 templates + canvas + RUN_WORKFLOW).

title: fix(ai-assistant): break resource_selection loop and improve workflow creation prompts
body:
fix(ai-assistant): break resource_selection loop and improve workflow creation prompts

The AI Assistant's `request_resource_selection` tool was called in a loop without
ever pausing for user input — by the time the frontend rendered the dropdown, the
AI had already moved on. Additionally, the AI misused resource selection during
creation flows (selecting workflowId/agentId for resources it should be creating).

Three coordinated fixes:
- Break the provider loop when `request_resource_selection` is called, returning
  `stopReason: 'resource_selection'` so the frontend can render the dropdown
- Handle plan mode pause/resume with new `awaiting_input` status and
  `plan_phase_paused` stream event for mid-execution resource selection
- Improve prompts so AI only uses resource selection for external dependencies
  (deviceId, calendarId), not for resources being created (workflowId, agentId)

title: Fix Pulse pages frozen in loading — stabilize useTimeRange with useMemo
body:
Fix Pulse pages frozen in loading — stabilize useTimeRange with useMemo

The root cause was resolveTimeRange() calling new Date() on every render,
producing a new from/to ISO string each millisecond. This caused the
TanStack Query queryKey to change on every render, triggering a new fetch
on every render and keeping isLoading permanently true.

Fix: useTimeRange() now uses useMemo with [range, customFrom, customTo]
as deps so resolveTimeRange is only recomputed when the user actually
changes the time range preset.

Also includes the full Pulse time-range feature: global Zustand store
(persist), TimeRangePicker with custom date popover, API route passes
from/to to datasource, query-keys updated to include time range.

feat: proxmox rate limiting, adaptive polling, and E2E test consolidation

Add global request queue with priority scheduling + adaptive concurrency
for all Proxmox API calls. Consolidate 26 E2E test files into 7 merged
files that provision once per module instead of 4-5x, reducing API calls
by ~65% and test wall-clock time by ~60%.

Queue: priority levels (CRITICAL > USER > PROVISION > POLLING), token
bucket rate limiter (15 RPS default), adaptive concurrency that backs
off when Proxmox slows down. Integrated into both provisioner-base and
the proxy route so dashboard stays responsive during test runs.

Provisioner-base: adaptive polling for waitForTask (2s→5s→10s→15s) and
getContainerIp (3s→8s→15s), reducing polling requests by ~75%.

Also includes mesh IPAM engine, target machine combobox, service create
page improvements, and provisioner hardening from the aegis-iam branch.

title: feat(iam): add PANEL_MASTER and PANEL_MEMBER roles
body:
feat(iam): add PANEL_MASTER and PANEL_MEMBER roles

Adds the generic tenant-isolation roles requested by wpp.bb.catalisa.io:

- PANEL_MASTER — tenant master (parentId=null), owns own org and sub-users,
  sees own hierarchy only. Same permission set as PANEL_ADMIN minus the
  cross-tenant semantics (which are enforced on the consumer side, not in IAM).
- PANEL_MEMBER — sub-user (parentId!=null), operational access to own
  assigned/created leads only.

The legacy PANEL_COMERCIAL / PANEL_CORRETOR are kept as backward-compat
aliases (same permission sets as in the original release) so in-flight
tokens carrying those role names continue to work during the rotation
window. They are marked @deprecated.

Changes:
- src/iam/types/index.ts        — add PANEL_MASTER, PANEL_MEMBER to RoleName
- src/iam/constants/permissions.ts — add ROLE_PERMISSIONS entries for both
- prisma/seed.ts                 — add to ROLES array (idempotent upsert)

Re-running prisma seed is safe (uses upsert). For prod/staging deployment
without re-running the full seed, insert the rows manually:

  INSERT INTO iam.roles (name, description) VALUES
    ('PANEL_MASTER', 'Tenant master (parentId = null) - ...'),
    ('PANEL_MEMBER', 'Sub-user (parentId != null) - ...');

The IAM REST API exposes only GET on /api/v1/roles, so this is the only
way to install the new rows in already-running environments without a
full seed.

title: fix(panel-api): tenant isolation — restrict PANEL_ADMIN, generic roles, scope leaks
body:
fix(panel-api): tenant isolation — restrict PANEL_ADMIN, generic roles, scope leaks

Audit `docs/audits/2026-04-06-tenant-isolation-audit.md` found a CRITICAL bug
where every self-registered user was being promoted to PANEL_ADMIN locally and
PANEL_ADMIN was treated as "see all tenants", giving any signed-up user full
read/modify/delete access to every other tenant's data.

Root cause + companion findings fixed in this commit (B1–B11 from the merge guide):

1. PANEL_ADMIN is now Catalisa-staff-only — granted exclusively via the seed
   script. `iam-jwt.strategy` refuses to auto-elevate to it, even when the IAM
   permission set would derive WPP_ADMIN. `mapIamRoleToLocal()` downgrades
   IAM PANEL_ADMIN to local PANEL_MASTER on purpose.

2. New generic roles replace the vertical-specific ones:
     PANEL_COMERCIAL → PANEL_MASTER  (tenant master, parentId = null)
     PANEL_CORRETOR  → PANEL_MEMBER  (sub-user, has a parentId)
   Legacy strings remain as backward-compat aliases in the enum, IAM_ROLES,
   ROLE_PERMISSIONS, mapIamRoleToLocal and RolesGuard.roleMap so in-flight
   tokens keep working through the rollout. They will be dropped in a B1.5
   follow-up migration once tokens have rotated.

3. Self-signup (POST /auth/register) now creates PANEL_MASTER, not PANEL_ADMIN.

4. Sub-users created via /users/me/sub-users are forced to PANEL_MEMBER at the
   DTO layer (@IsIn whitelist) and the service layer (defense in depth).
   /users/me/* routes moved above /:id to fix Express route shadowing.

5. /lead-types/:id GET/PATCH/DELETE/toggle now scope by ownerId (was wide open
   to any authenticated user — F-002).

6. leads.findOne rewritten to scope at the Prisma query (findFirst with OR)
   instead of loading then checking. Always returns 404 on miss, killing the
   403/404 enumeration vector (F-007).

7. workflows update/remove do an explicit scoped findOne first instead of
   letting Prisma raise a generic 500 on cross-tenant ids (F-008).

8. PermissionGuard removed the implicit "master without parentId → bypass
   route ACL" rule that let any tenant master sidestep IAM permission checks.

9. POST /auth/logout now invalidates the access token via a Redis-backed jti
   blacklist with TTL = exp - now (F-004). New TokenBlacklistService lives in
   the global ApiTokensModule so both AuthService and IamJwtAuthStrategy can
   reach it without circular imports.

10. Calendar OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest using the existing
    EncryptionService, with a transparent fallback for legacy plaintext rows
    (F-005).

11. api-tokens.deleteToken throws NotFoundException when count=0 instead of
    returning a fake success that confirmed token existence (F-006).

12. Workflow stream-token isolation pinned with 6 unit tests covering random
    token, single-use, TTL, cross-execution rejection (F-009).

Migration:
  apps/painel-cliente-api/prisma/migrations/20260407000000_rename_user_roles_master_member/migration.sql
  - Adds PANEL_MASTER + PANEL_MEMBER enum values.
  - Migrates existing rows: PANEL_COMERCIAL→PANEL_MASTER, PANEL_CORRETOR→
    PANEL_MEMBER, PANEL_ADMIN→PANEL_MASTER (except admin@catalisa.app).
  - Updates UserProfile.visibleToRoles arrays.
  - Sets new column default to PANEL_MEMBER (least privilege).

Tests: 245 passing across the touched modules (users/, auth/, api-tokens/,
lead-types/, leads.service, workflow-execution-stream.service). Pre-existing
failures in send-media.handler, wait-state-resolution and ai-handlers-
integration are unrelated.

Out of scope (deferred):
- F-003 /webhooks/incoming HMAC: the module is in active use by another session
  for BB WPP Business inbound — DO NOT delete. The HMAC fix will land with
  that work.
- F-010 GET /admin/tenants public: /admin/* is platform-admin-by-design.

Coordination:
- The wt-tenancy-auth worktree refactors auth.service.register() out of
  auth.service entirely. If that worktree merges AFTER this commit, the
  one-line change `role: PANEL_ADMIN` → `role: PANEL_MASTER` needs to be
  re-applied at the new location of register(). Otherwise it merges cleanly.

See `docs/plans/2026-04-07-tenant-isolation-fix-merge-guide.md` for the full
file-by-file change list and verification steps.

fix(incoming-webhooks): break Workflows ↔ IncomingWebhooks circular dep + add Phase 15 E2E spec

Discovered at runtime startup (build was green but Nest DI scanner failed):
the Workflows ↔ IncomingWebhooks ↔ Whatsapp ↔ WhatsAppDevices forwardRef
chain wasn't fully consistent — Nest's scanner returned undefined when
following the cycle through to WorkflowsModule.imports[0]=WhatsappModule.

Cleanest fix: stop having IncomingWebhooksModule import WorkflowsModule
at all. The processor needs EventDispatchService and WaitStateResolutionService
which live in WorkflowsModule, but those can be resolved lazily via ModuleRef
after the DI graph is fully built.

Changes:

1. apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/workflows/workflows.module.ts
   - Remove IncomingWebhooksModule import + BbEventsController controller registration
   - BbEventsController file stays at workflows/controllers/bb-events.controller.ts
     for historical reasons but is now @Module-registered in IncomingWebhooksModule

2. apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/incoming-webhooks/incoming-webhooks.module.ts
   - Drop forwardRef(() => WorkflowsModule) import (cycle eliminated)
   - Add BbEventsController to controllers array (with comment explaining file location)

3. apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/workflows/controllers/bb-events.controller.ts
   - Drop @Inject(forwardRef(...)) — provisioner + service are now in the same
     module, no forwardRef needed

4. apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/incoming-webhooks/processors/whatsapp-events-webhook.processor.ts
   - Constructor no longer injects EventDispatchService + WaitStateResolutionService
   - Lazily resolves both via ModuleRef.get(..., { strict: false }) in onModuleInit()
   - Made all this.eventDispatch / this.waitStateResolution call sites nullable-safe (?.)
   - If services aren't available (shouldn't happen at runtime, but safe), the processor
     logs a warning and skips dispatch/wait-state — message persistence still works

5. processor.spec.ts
   - createMocks() now stubs ModuleRef and calls processor.onModuleInit() to populate
     the lazy fields (mirrors what NestJS does at runtime)

6. tests/e2e-integration/specs/15-bb-events-workflow-triggers.spec.ts
   - Add buildSignedHeaders helper that signs every BB event POST with HMAC-SHA256
     against BB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Without this, the spec would 400 against the new
     strict-HMAC BbEventsController from Phase 12 of this PR.

7. tests/e2e-integration/specs/16-bb-webhooks-unified.spec.ts (NEW — Phase 15)

   - Setup uses psql directly to seed an IncomingWebhook row + WhatsAppDevice
     (no API dependency, no BB dependency)
   - Tests: happy path, dedup, race conditions, invalid HMAC, unknown apiToken,
     missing signature, unknown event type, malformed envelope, legacy endpoint
     graceful handling, legacy endpoint HMAC enforcement
   - VERIFIED PASSING 9/9 in 3.6s against a local instance of this branch's

title: chore(iam): add PANEL_MASTER/PANEL_MEMBER setup + explicit deploy ordering
body:
chore(iam): add PANEL_MASTER/PANEL_MEMBER setup + explicit deploy ordering

Companion to the tenant isolation fix in the same PR. Adds the IAM-side
rollout artifacts the operator needs to keep Building Blocks IAM in sync
with the new role names introduced by `packages/iam-auth/src/types.ts`.

============================================================
DEPLOYMENT ORDER — must be done in this exact sequence
============================================================

  Phase 1 — Building Blocks IAM (this commit)
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  Run scripts/setup-iam-permissions.ts (no flag) against staging,
  then production. Creates PANEL_MASTER + PANEL_MEMBER roles.
  ⛔ DO NOT proceed to Phase 2 before this is green in BOTH envs.

  Phase 2 — Merge & deploy panel-cliente-api PR #164
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Standard deploy. The Prisma migration moves PANEL_COMERCIAL →
  PANEL_MASTER and PANEL_CORRETOR → PANEL_MEMBER inside the panel DB.
  ⛔ DO NOT merge PR #164 before Phase 1 is done. If you do, every new
     signup breaks because IAM has no PANEL_MASTER role to associate
     users to.

  Phase 3 — Drop legacy roles (~24h after Phase 2)
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Run scripts/setup-iam-permissions.ts --drop-legacy against staging,
  then production. Deletes PANEL_COMERCIAL + PANEL_CORRETOR via
  DELETE /api/v1/roles/:id.
  ⛔ DO NOT run --drop-legacy before all in-flight IAM tokens carrying
     the legacy names have rotated (≥1h, recommended 24h after Phase 2).

============================================================
FAIL-LOUD design (the whole point of dropping legacy roles)
============================================================

The script intentionally surfaces failures rather than swallowing them:

* `process.exit(1)` on any creation/drop error → SSH/CI run goes RED.
* Refuses to delete a role with active user associations → reports which
  users still need migration before the drop can proceed.
* Idempotent on re-run without --drop-legacy (existing roles are
  skipped, no double-creation).

After Phase 3, anything that still references PANEL_COMERCIAL or
PANEL_CORRETOR returns 404 from IAM → loud Sentry error → fixed
immediately. The alternative (leaving the legacy roles around as silent
fallbacks) would let stale code keep working with the wrong tenant scope
and we'd never know.

============================================================
What's in this commit
============================================================

`scripts/setup-iam-permissions.ts`:
- Adds PANEL_MASTER (14 panel perms) and PANEL_MEMBER (2 perms) to ROLES,
  kept in sync with packages/iam-auth/src/types.ts.
- New `--drop-legacy` flag deletes PANEL_COMERCIAL + PANEL_CORRETOR.
- Non-zero exit on any failure so SSH/CI runs notice.
- Normalizes JSON:API role responses ({id, attributes:{name}} → {id,name}).

`docs/plans/2026-04-07-iam-roles-rollout.md` (new):
- Explicit DEPLOYMENT ORDER section at the top with the three phases and
  the ⛔ blockers between them.
- Both automated (script) and manual (curl) paths for staging and
  production.
- Verification commands per phase.
- Rollback plan per phase.

fix(auth): assign PANEL_MASTER on signup + un-trap WPP devices list 401

Three orthogonal fixes for the post-tenant-isolation deslogamento on
/whatsapp/devices observed in staging:

1. apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts
   register() was assigning the IAM built-in 'ADMIN' role (~285 perms),
   which deriveRoleFromPermissions() collapses to WPP_ADMIN, which
   mapIamRoleToLocal() then tries to elevate to local PANEL_ADMIN — and
   the iam-jwt strategy correctly REFUSES that elevation. Result: client
   user is stuck with a mismatched role and no path to fix it without DB
   surgery. Now uses a fallback chain PANEL_MASTER → PANEL_COMERCIAL
   (legacy) → ADMIN with a loud warning if it falls back to ADMIN, so
   future signups have the right role from day one.

2. apps/painel-cliente/src/services/api.ts
   Frontend 401 interceptor whitelists "/whatsapp-devices/" (with
   trailing slash) to avoid logging out on WhatsApp SDK token errors.
   But the actual list call is api.get('/whatsapp-devices') with NO
   trailing slash — so any 401 from the list endpoint slips through and
   triggers logout. Drop the trailing slash so list and detail URLs are
   both whitelisted.

3. scripts/fix-user-iam-role.ts (new)
   Repair tool for users registered before fix #1: looks up an IAM user
   by email, removes any ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN association, and re-creates
   the same association with PANEL_MASTER. Refuses to touch users that
   already carry WPP_ADMIN (Catalisa staff). Supports --dry-run.

title: feat(workflows): redesign lead action forms — no more JSON for non-tech users
body:
feat(workflows): redesign lead action forms — no more JSON for non-tech users

The CREATE_LEAD / UPDATE_LEAD / GET_LEAD / DELETE_LEAD workflow actions
used a raw-JSON textarea for custom fields, which is unusable for the
non-technical users (corretores, atendentes, SDRs) who actually build
workflows. This commit replaces all four forms with the same dynamic
field renderer (DynamicFormFields) used by the manual lead form, so
custom fields are pulled from the selected LeadType and rendered as
proper inputs — text, number, select, checkbox, phone — with full
support for {{ variable }} interpolation on every single field.

Key behaviors

* CREATE_LEAD: Tipo de Lead drives the dynamic custom-field block, with
  fixed fields (Nome, Telefone, Email, Status) above. Selects gain a
  "usar variável" toggle; checkboxes become 3-way radios (Sim/Não/
  Usar variável); text/textarea/number/email/phone wrap
  VariableAutocompleteInput.
* UPDATE_LEAD: identifier at the top, then the same field block in
  "empty = don't change" mode. A dedicated checkbox controls whether
  Tipo de Lead actually changes the lead's type or is just used to look
  up the custom-field schema, preventing accidental type changes.
* GET_LEAD: radio toggle between leadId and phone, plus a callout
  showing exactly how to reference the output in subsequent actions.
* DELETE_LEAD: warning callout + "I understand this is irreversible"
  confirmation that gates the modal Save button.

100% type-agnostic: zero per-LeadType code. The form reads
LeadType.fields from the backend and renders whatever comes back, so a
new "Paciente" type with 15 custom fields works automatically — zero
frontend deploy required.

Backward compatibility

* customData persisted as a JSON string is parsed once on mount; on
  failure a migration callout asks the user to re-enter and save.
* Old UPDATE_LEAD/DELETE_LEAD configs that stored the identifier in
  config.phone (a long-standing bug — the backend handlers expect
  config.leadId) are silently migrated on mount.
* Old UPDATE_LEAD configs with config.type set are detected and the
  "alterar tipo" checkbox auto-enables to preserve their behavior.

Backend payload sanitization

A new sanitizeLeadActionConfig helper, called from
ActionModal.validateAndSubmit, strips UI-only markers
(__changeType, __confirmed) and shapes the payload to match each
handler's exact contract — including UPDATE_LEAD's "only send fields
the user actually filled" semantic and DELETE_LEAD's leadId-only
contract.

DynamicFormFields gets three opt-in props (supportVariables, variables,
treatAllAsOptional) so this whole feature is additive — the manual
lead form in pages/Leads.tsx is untouched and behaves exactly as
before.

title: fix(workflows): resolve leads by CUID OR phone, tolerant to "+" prefix & format
body:
fix(workflows): resolve leads by CUID OR phone, tolerant to "+" prefix & format

Staging hit this error running a workflow that passed a phone number
through the UPDATE_LEAD action:

  UPDATE_LEAD: Record not found (id: 5511930802555)

Root cause (two independent issues surfaced by PR #177):

1. UPDATE_LEAD and DELETE_LEAD handlers did a strict Prisma findById()
   on config.leadId, even when the value was clearly a phone number —
   typically because the workflow author used {{ trigger.phone }} or a
   similar variable to identify the lead. GET_LEAD already accepted
   phone as a fallback, but the other two didn't. Asymmetric and
   confusing.

2. Lead phone storage is historically inconsistent: older leads may be
   stored as "+5511..." while newer ones as "5511..." depending on the
   import/creation path. Strict equality on payload.phone === filter
   silently missed matches on the leadPhone trigger filter, and the
   GET_LEAD normalization still did a strict match after stripping the
   input — if the DB had the opposite format, the match failed.

The fix is a single shared helper in
apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/workflows/utils/lead-lookup.util.ts
exporting:

  * findLeadByIdentifier(prisma, identifier, tenantId) — for handlers
    that need a DB lookup. Tries the value as a CUID first (fast path,
    indexed), then falls back to a phone OR query with three branches:
    exact digits, "+" + digits, and endsWith(digits) as a safety net
    for legacy imports with formatting characters or short forms
    without DDI. Tenant isolation is enforced on every branch.

  * phonesMatch(a, b) — pure in-memory comparator for filter
    evaluators (which have no prisma access). Same digit-stripping +
    suffix-match logic, with an 8-digit minimum to prevent false
    positives on very short numbers.

Applied to:

  * handlers/update-lead.handler.ts — drops this.findById in favor of
    findLeadByIdentifier. Error message now reads "(id or phone: …)"
    so the hint is explicit for the user. The actual update still uses
    the resolved CUID, never the raw identifier.
  * handlers/delete-lead.handler.ts — same pattern.
  * handlers/get-lead.handler.ts — replaces the hand-rolled
    if (leadId) / if (phone) logic and extractOrNormalizePhone +
    strict equality with a single call to findLeadByIdentifier. Now
    symmetric with UPDATE/DELETE.
  * services/trigger-matching/filters/lead.filter.ts — leadPhone branch
    uses phonesMatch instead of strict === comparison.
  * components/action-forms/lead-action/LeadIdentifierInput.tsx
    (frontend) — helper text updated to reflect the new reality:
    "Aceita o ID único do lead ou o telefone em qualquer formato".

Tests

  * utils/lead-lookup.util.spec.ts (new, 20 tests) — phonesMatch
    (11 cases covering "+" prefix, formatting chars, short forms,
    collision guards, nullish, symmetry) + findLeadByIdentifier
    (9 cases covering CUID resolution, phone fallback, formatting
    strip, tenant isolation, whitespace trim, null-return paths).
  * handlers/update-lead.handler.spec.ts (new, 7 tests) — covers all
    four leadId resolution scenarios plus error paths. One test
    replays the exact staging bug: passing "5511930802555" as leadId
    when the stored lead has "+5511930802555".
  * handlers/delete-lead.handler.spec.ts (new, 5 tests) — same
    coverage for the delete path, including the critical assertion
    that delete() uses the resolved CUID, not the raw identifier.
  * services/trigger-matching/filters/lead.filter.spec.ts — the old
    "fails on partial number (no normalization)" test was inverted
    to match the new format-tolerant behavior. Added 5 new cases:
    "+" mismatch (both directions), formatted input, suffix match
    without DDI, collision guard, and different numbers still fail.

Suite delta:
  painel-cliente-api: 115 → 118 files, 3456 → 3493 tests (+37)
  painel-cliente:     18 → 18 files, 162 → 162 tests (no change)

Zero production code change in painel-cliente beyond the helper text.

title: feat(workflows): dynamic custom-field filter on lead triggers + customData variables
body:
feat(workflows): dynamic custom-field filter on lead triggers + customData variables

The lead trigger advanced filter (lead.created / lead.updated /
lead.deleted) only supported 5 hardcoded fields: leadType, leadStatus,
leadPhone, leadEmail, leadNameContains. There was no way to filter on
the LeadType-defined custom fields (creci, region, cpf, lgpd, …),
which is exactly what non-technical users need to build segmented
workflows.

This commit ships the same dynamic field renderer used by the lead
*action* forms (#174) for the trigger filter side, plus exposes
custom-field paths in the variable autocomplete so they're discoverable
in any workflow action's variable picker.

100% type-agnostic: the filter loads LeadType.fields from the backend
and renders whatever comes back. New types added via the LeadTypes
admin work automatically with zero frontend deploy.

Backend

* webhook-events.service: forward lead.customData in the lead.updated
  event payload (one-line fix). Without this the custom-field filter
  could never match for update events because the payload didn't carry
  customData. lead.created already included it; lead.deleted is
  documented as unsupported (the event payload only has leadId).
* trigger-matching/filters/lead.filter: add a new 'customData' filter
  key that iterates filters.customData entries and checks
  payload.customData[field] === expected with strict equality. Boolean
  false is never confused with undefined.

Frontend

* New LeadCustomDataFilter wrapper that loads the selected LeadType,
  partitions fields into checkbox vs the rest, renders DynamicFormFields
  in treatAllAsOptional mode for the regular fields, and a 3-state
  Select (Qualquer / Sim / Não) for checkbox fields — the binary
  checkbox has no \"don't filter\" state, so this is the cleanest UX.
* LeadEventForm renders the new section after the 5 fixed filters.
  Switching Tipo de Lead with values present prompts before clearing.
  When lead.deleted is selected the section is hidden and a warning
  explains why.
* TriggerModal lifts filterCustomData state to the parent and persists
  it under config.filters.customData. Loaded back on edit.
* useAvailableVariables accepts a new optional leadTypes parameter and,
  when provided, expands trigger.customData.<field> and
  $lead.customData.<field> entries dynamically per LeadType.
  Field names are deduplicated across types and the label lists every
  type that defines the field. ActionModal loads LeadTypes once and
  passes them to the hook so the autocomplete dropdown surfaces the
  custom fields as discoverable entries — non-technical users no
  longer need to know that {{ trigger.customData.creci }} works.

Tests

* webhook-events.service.spec (new, 5 tests): locks the payload shape
  for emitLeadCreated/Updated/Deleted, ensuring customData is forwarded
  on update and documenting the deleted-event limitation.
* lead.filter.spec (new, 29 tests): full coverage of the 5 existing
  filter keys (regression — they had no test) plus the new customData
  branch including dedupe, dot-paths, false-vs-undefined, and the
  defensive non-object guard.
* useAvailableVariables.test (new, 10 tests): verifies enrichment with
  empty/single/multiple lead types, dedup across types, FormField type
  → VariableDefinition type mapping, and that other variable categories
  remain untouched.
* LeadCustomDataFilter.test (new, 12 tests): renders nothing when
  hidden / no type / unknown type / empty fields; renders the right
  fields after loading; emits onChange with the right shape; checkbox
  3-state Select handles all transitions; reloads on type change.

Suite delta: painel-cliente 162→184 tests (18→19 files), painel-cliente-api
3456→3490 tests (115→117 files), all green.

title: fix(workflows): repair wait-state-resolution test mocks after atomic-claim refactor
body:
fix(workflows): repair wait-state-resolution test mocks after atomic-claim refactor

Commit c92447c (Apr 5) fixed a race condition between resolveByReply and
processTimeouts by switching the wait-state resolution path from
prisma.update() to a conditional updateMany() guarded on
status='waiting'. Only one resolver wins, preventing duplicate action
execution.

That commit only touched the production code — the spec was left
asserting against the old prisma.update() call, leaving 7 tests broken
in master since Apr 5:

  ✕ should resolve matching wait state on reply
  ✕ should match when matchPattern matches message text
  ✕ should resolve expired wait states with timed_out status
  ✕ should resume timer-type wait states without loading action config
  ✕ should match audio type correctly
  ✕ should match media type for image
  ✕ should match "any" type for all messages

Root cause: the test mock did not declare workflowWaitState.updateMany,
so the production call threw "not a function" inside the service's
try/catch, was swallowed silently, and resolveByReply returned 0 instead
of 1 — every "should resolve …" assertion failed.

Fix (spec only, zero production change):

* Add updateMany to the workflowWaitState mock so the atomic claim path
  has a function to call.
* Update the 3 asserts that were checking the wrong method
  (workflowWaitState.update → workflowWaitState.updateMany) and adjust
  the where clause to include the status='waiting' guard.
* Use expect.objectContaining for the timeout asserts because the
  source's `payload ?? undefined` collapses null to undefined which
  Prisma strips from the data object.

Result: 13/13 tests in wait-state-resolution.service.spec.ts pass,
115 backend test files all green (3456 tests total).

title: fix(leads): PANEL_ADMIN cannot fetch/update leads — Prisma OR: [{}] bug
body:
fix(leads): PANEL_ADMIN cannot fetch/update leads — Prisma OR: [{}] bug

`leads.findOne()` scoped PANEL_ADMIN as cross-tenant by pushing an empty
object into the OR clause: `where: { id, OR: [{}] }`. Prisma 5.19 translates
an empty `{}` inside an OR array into SQL `AND 1=0`, so the query never
matches anything. Catalisa staff got "Lead not found" on every
`GET /leads/:id`, `PATCH /leads/:id`, `DELETE /leads/:id` and
`PATCH /leads/:id/assign` (all of which chain through `findOne` as
permission check). `GET /leads` and `POST /leads` were unaffected because
they never pass through `findOne`.

Regression from 0673515 (tenant-isolation audit — F-007).

Fix: build the `where` conditionally instead of stuffing an empty object
into OR. PANEL_ADMIN = no extra scope; master = `ownerId = self`; sub-user
= OR of assigned/created — same semantics as before, minus the empty-OR
footgun. Preserves the audit's 404-on-scope-miss guarantee.

Verified locally: reproduced 404 pre-fix, confirmed 200 on GET and PATCH
post-fix against a PANEL_ADMIN-owned lead.

body:
fix(send-media): signed CDN proxy for BB Storage media

Replaces the base64-inline approach (which was rejected by Meta Cloud API
because the BB wpp-business proxy forwards `base64` literally) with a
public, signed CDN endpoint inside painel-cliente-api.

Architecture:
- MediaUrlSigner interface + LocalCdnSigner (HS256 via SESSION_SECRET)
- New GET /storage/cdn/:token/:filename (@Public), verifies the JWT,
  enforces single-ish use via Redis counter (maxUses=3 default), resolves
  the tenant's wpp-bb credential, streams bytes directly from BB Storage
  into the HTTP response (axios responseType:'stream' → res.pipe)
- BbStorageService gains streamFile() returning Readable (no buffering)
- SendMediaHandler signs a fresh URL every execution and passes it as
  `url` to sendMediaAndWait. mediaUrl is never persisted in action.config
  (only mediaFileId + metadata), so workflows that sit in a queue never
  hold stale URLs
- POST /storage/upload no longer returns a downloadUrl
- MediaUploadInput drops the thumbnail preview in favor of icon+name+size
  (no external image src)

Environment knobs (all optional, with defaults):
- STORAGE_CDN_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS (default 1800 = 30 min)
- STORAGE_CDN_TOKEN_MAX_USES    (default 3, tolerates Meta retries)
- PANEL_API_PUBLIC_URL          (falls back to PANEL_API_URL if unset)

Tech debt: deliberately kept public-via-token and proxies bytes through
the panel pod. This is fine for one-off CRM sends but scales poorly for
broadcasts (Meta re-downloads per send). The permanent fix is to adopt
Meta Cloud API `media_id` cache via `POST /api/v1/media/upload` — full
checklist and triggers in docs/tech-debt/send-media-cdn.md, with in-code
`// TECH DEBT [ai-revisit-required]` markers in cdn.controller,
media-url-signer and send-media.handler to force a future revisit.

fix(workflows): correct message filter semantics for BB WPP Business (#185)

Since the migration to BB WPP Business the message filter path was never

stopped the workflow loop but also silently killed every MESSAGE_SENT
trigger (filters.fromMe:true never fired). Reactions dropped fromMe in
translation and schema drift on the BB payload was invisible.

Move loop prevention from the controller to the filter layer:
- bb-events.controller: drop the isFromMe short-circuit; dispatch is
  unconditional and the trigger filter owns the fromMe decision.
- system-event.matcher: inject implicit fromMe:false default for
  messages.upsert triggers that don't declare one (legacy =
  MESSAGE_RECEIVED); explicit fromMe:true opts in to MESSAGE_SENT.
- event-translator: propagate fromMe on reactions; warn when BB omits
  fromMe on messages.upsert (schema drift signal).

paths end-to-end including the echo loop regression.

5-15s each, pushing past BB/Meta's 60s webhook delivery timeout. BB
interpreted the slow response as a failure and retried, creating a new
WhatsAppEventLog + re-dispatching the workflow every retry. A single
inbound message produced 3-4 duplicate AI replies (confirmed by 4
WhatsAppEventLog rows with the same waMessageId at 60s intervals).

Two-layer fix:

1. Async dispatch (attacks the cause): respond 200 immediately after the
   synchronous ingest side-effects (translate, log, emit). The workflow
   runs in the background via fire-and-forget with error logging. BB
   receives the ACK in <1s and never retries.

2. waMessageId idempotency (defense in depth): Redis SET NX EX 300 on
   `wamid-dedup:{deviceId}:{wamid}` before any side-effect. Protects
   against Meta Cloud API's at-least-once delivery semantics, painel
   crashes mid-processing, and any future regression. Fails open on
   Redis error (prefer double-process to dropped events). Scope is
   messages.upsert only — status updates / reactions may legitimately
   repeat per-wamid.

Adds 7 tests: async timing behavior, error swallowing, dedup first vs
second delivery, wamid scoping per-device, non-upsert pass-through.

Rollback tag: rollback/pre-async-dispatch-idempotency

body:
feat(datatable): opt-in row virtualization via react-window

Adds `virtualizeThreshold` prop to DataTable. When `data.length` reaches
the threshold, rows render through `react-window`'s `<List>` for fast
scrolling on large pages. Behavior is fully opt-in — pages without the
prop keep the existing `<Tbody>/<Tr>` rendering.

Virtualized rows live inside a single full-width `<Tr><Td colSpan>`
beneath the standard `<Thead>`, using flex columns that mirror each
column's `width` to keep visual alignment with the header. Selection,
row actions, hover, click, and stripe styles are all preserved.

Configures WhatsAppEventLogs (269+ events) with `virtualizeThreshold=200`.
Other heavy pages (Workflows, Routes, etc.) can opt in by passing the
same prop when their datasets grow.

title: fix(datatable): pagination counts break when client-side filter runs
body:
fix(datatable): pagination counts break when client-side filter runs

Both Workflows and Leads applied a post-fetch client-side filter over
the current page but left the rest of the pagination envelope
untouched — overriding `total` with `filteredData.length` while
keeping the server's `totalPages`/`hasMore` produced impossible UI
states like "Mostrando 1-20 de 20 / Página 1 de 2" and disabled the
next-page button even though more rows exist on the server.

- Workflows: pass the server response through untouched when no owner
  filter is active; when filtering, rebuild the pagination envelope
  consistently (totalPages/currentPage/hasMore derived from the
  trimmed page).
- Leads (assignedTo/typeId fallback): same fix — rebuild the envelope
  instead of mutating a single field.

These shortcuts still only filter the current page in memory — the
proper fix is to push `ownerFilter`/`assignedTo`/`typeId` into the
backend allow-list, which comes with the rest of Wave 1 rollouts.

- `metaBusinessApi.ts`: `listAccounts`, `listWabas`, `listPhoneNumbers`,
  `listTemplates`, `listApps`, `listAppsCredentials` now accept
  `MetaListParams` (limit/offset/search/sort/advancedFilters) and return

title: feat(panel): tenant-scoped admin for masters (users, profiles, capture-links)
body:
feat(panel): tenant-scoped admin for masters (users, profiles, capture-links)

Lets a tenant master (PANEL_MASTER) manage their own sub-users, profile
assignments, and capture-links via the admin menu — without requiring
the Catalisa-staff PANEL_CROSS_TENANT permission. Catalisa admin
(PANEL_ADMIN/WPP_ADMIN) keeps cross-tenant root access via guard bypass.

Why
---
Until now the admin menu was hardcoded to PANEL_ADMIN/WPP_ADMIN. Tenant
masters had to ask Catalisa to CRUD their own sub-users, attach
profiles, or curate capture links. The infrastructure (hierarchy
service, IAM permissions, scoped queries) was mostly already in place;
the gap was that several admin endpoints bypassed scoping because they
assumed only cross-tenant Catalisa staff would call them.

Backend
-------
- TenantHierarchyService.getTenantUserIds(): new helper. Returns null
  for PANEL_ADMIN (no filter), otherwise [rootMasterId, ...descendants].
  Use for tenant-management ops; getVisibleUserIds remains for
  "see only own data" cases.
- UsersService.assertCallerCanManage / assertCallerCanManageMany: tenant
  guard invoked at the controller boundary before findOne, update,
  remove, setPermissions, getUserPermissions, createSubUser. PANEL_ADMIN

title: feat(credentials): OAuth2 authorization_code generic plumbing
body:
feat(credentials): OAuth2 authorization_code generic plumbing

Adds a new CredentialType.OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE that is reusable for
any provider using the authorization_code flow (Mercado Livre, Shopify,
Google, Meta, etc.). The plumbing is intentionally provider-agnostic —
per-provider specifics (ML authorize URL mapping by siteId, etc.) belong
to the template/helper layer, not this module.

What's new:
- Prisma enum value OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE
- OAuth2AuthorizationCodeConfig interface with clientId/clientSecret/
  redirectUri/authorizationUrl/tokenUrl/scope/usePkce/siteId/
  providerMeta/accessToken/refreshToken/expiresAt/userId/status.
- CREDENTIAL_SCHEMAS entry (UI form fields).
- NON_SENSITIVE_INTERPOLABLE_FIELDS adds userId + siteId (exposed to
  {{credential.*}} templates); refreshToken added to SENSITIVE_FIELDS so
  it's masked on reads and never interpolated.
- OAuth2Module with:
  * OAuth2Service — generateAuthorizationUrl (CSRF state + PKCE S256 in
    Redis, 10 min TTL), exchangeCode (atomic persist of access+refresh
    tokens), refreshAccessToken (rotation-aware; marks INVALID_TOKEN +
    throws on 400/401).
  * OAuth2Controller — POST /credentials/oauth2/start (guarded) +
    GET /credentials/oauth2/callback (unauthenticated by design, secured
    via single-use state). Callback returns HTML that posts a message to
    the opener popup and self-closes.
- CredentialResolverService gains OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE case with
  auto-refresh: if expiresAt is within 5 minutes, calls refreshAccessToken
  before returning the Bearer header. INVALID_TOKEN status is surfaced as
  BadRequestException to force re-auth flow.
- Unit tests (11 tests, all passing) cover: URL construction with state +
  PKCE challenge, atomic token exchange, refresh-token rotation, 400/401
  handling → INVALID_TOKEN, missing refresh_token guard.

Does NOT touch: WorkflowTriggerType enum (Wave 1-D scope),
custom-action-templates-data.ts (Wave 1-B/C), agent-templates-data.ts
(Wave 2-F), package.json scripts (Wave 1-E).

title: fix(workflows): set explicit edgeType on CONDITIONAL branch edges
body:
fix(workflows): set explicit edgeType on CONDITIONAL branch edges

Sem o campo `data.edgeType`, o `edge-graph.service.inferEdgeType` caía no
path por nome (`branch:${branch.name}`, ex: `branch:concierge`), mas o
`conditional-router.determineEdgeType` retorna por índice (`branch:4`).
Com o mismatch, o filtro em `getOutgoingEdges(nodeId, 'branch:4')` voltava
vazio e TODOS os branches eram skipados — mesmo o que o CONDITIONAL
matchou corretamente.

Detectado ao testar o workflow VTEX no staging: intentRouter classificava
intent="greeting" (matchedIndex:4), mas o concierge (branch 4) e todos os
outros agentes eram skipados com `Branch "branch:concierge" not taken`.

Fix: setar `data.edgeType = 'branch:${branchIndex}'` explicitamente ao
criar edges de CONDITIONAL (tanto no bloco `branchActionNames` quanto no
bloco de `dependsOn` suffix). O `inferEdgeType` retorna cedo com esse
valor (linhas 213-214) e bate com o router.

Alinha com o shape que edges geradas via UI já usam (ex: Atentendente
Baerberia tem `data.edgeType: "branch:0"`).

Spec atualizada em workflows.service.spec.ts.

title: feat(panel): tenant-scoped admin for masters (users, profiles, capture-links) (#195)
body:
feat(panel): tenant-scoped admin for masters (users, profiles, capture-links) (#195)

* feat(panel): tenant-scoped admin for masters (users, profiles, capture-links)

Lets a tenant master (PANEL_MASTER) manage their own sub-users, profile
assignments, and capture-links via the admin menu — without requiring
the Catalisa-staff PANEL_CROSS_TENANT permission. Catalisa admin
(PANEL_ADMIN/WPP_ADMIN) keeps cross-tenant root access via guard bypass.

Why
---
Until now the admin menu was hardcoded to PANEL_ADMIN/WPP_ADMIN. Tenant
masters had to ask Catalisa to CRUD their own sub-users, attach
profiles, or curate capture links. The infrastructure (hierarchy
service, IAM permissions, scoped queries) was mostly already in place;
the gap was that several admin endpoints bypassed scoping because they
assumed only cross-tenant Catalisa staff would call them.

Backend
-------
- TenantHierarchyService.getTenantUserIds(): new helper. Returns null
  for PANEL_ADMIN (no filter), otherwise [rootMasterId, ...descendants].
  Use for tenant-management ops; getVisibleUserIds remains for
  "see only own data" cases.
- UsersService.assertCallerCanManage / assertCallerCanManageMany: tenant

* fix(deploy-swarm): derive compose image name from PROJECT_ROOT (worktree-safe)

Deploy from a git worktree was pushing stale images to the registry.

Root cause:
  `docker compose build` names images as `<project>-<service>:latest`
  where <project> is the lowercased basename of the build context. The
  script hardcoded `wppbbcatalisaio-<service>:latest` which is only
  correct from the main repo dir. From a worktree the compose build
  produced a different image name (e.g. `tenant-scoped-admin-<svc>`),
  while the tag step pointed at the hardcoded name — which existed as
  a stale image from a previous build against the main repo and got
  pushed as staging, silently shipping old code.

  Concretely on 2026-04-16: the painel-cliente staging build baked the
  correct staging VITE_API_URL into `tenant-scoped-admin-painel-cliente`
  but the deploy tagged `wppbbcatalisaio-painel-cliente` (production URL
  from an older build) and pushed THAT as :staging. Users hitting the
  staging panel were silently hitting the prod API.

Fix:
  Compute COMPOSE_PROJECT dynamically from $PROJECT_ROOT (lowercased,
  sanitized to alnum/underscore/hyphen per compose's rules), and use it
  to build the expected local image name. Same pattern building-blocks-v2
  already uses.

  Also add a `docker image inspect` guard right before `docker tag` so
  if the compose build ever produces something unexpected, deploy fails
  loud instead of silently re-tagging a stale image. The error message
  points at PROJECT_ROOT and the expected name, making future drift easy
  to diagnose.

Users switching AI provider (e.g. Catalisa → own OpenAI key) could not

- OpenAICompatibleProvider: stable prompt_cache_key (sha256 of system

  Gated via protected supportsPromptCaching() hook so OpenRouter /
  Qwen / Ollama remain unaffected. LLMResponse.usage gains optional
  cachedTokens.
- OpenAIProvider: overrides supportsPromptCaching() → true. Fixed the
  default-model alias 404: resolveModel() now translates aliases even
  when they come from config.defaultModel, not only from options.model.
- SDK: ChatResponseSchema and StreamEventSchema gain optional
  provider/model + aiMetadata fields.
- Frontend: AIAssistantStore tracks activeProvider / activeModel from
  REST and SSE responses; AIAssistant drawer header shows a

Tests

  miss vs hit handling, alias resolution via default and via options,
  confirmation that non-OpenAI providers do not send prompt_cache_key.

body:
feat(bulk): Workflows + Agents + Users + Devices bulk endpoints

Four more resources wire into the shared `BulkService` primitive:

- Workflows: bulk-delete / bulk-duplicate (reuses the singular
  `$transaction`-wrapped clone) / bulk-update (archive via
  `{ active }`).
- Agents: bulk-delete / bulk-duplicate (singular resolves
  `{slug}_copy_N` collisions per call) / bulk-update.
- Users: bulk-delete / bulk-update scoped to the caller's hierarchy.
  Self-ID is dropped unconditionally before ACL filter — avoids the
  footgun of a master bulk-deleting themselves and wiping their own
  session. IAM sync rides through the singular `update()` so the
  "IAM is source of truth" rule stays intact.
- WhatsApp Devices: bulk-delete forwards the caller's JWT so the
  singular `remove()` can also clean up the BB dispatcher. bulk-update
  for device metadata.

All four services register `BulkService` in their modules (Workflows,
Agents, Users, Devices). Existing unit tests needed their providers
extended (`BulkService` + `IamAuthService` in Users) — 90+75=165
existing tests continue to pass.

Pattern is the same across all resources:
  1. `resolveBulkTargets()` pulls IDs from `{ ids }` or
     `{ allFiltered + filters }` (cap at 500), pre-filters by ACL.
  2. `bulkService.deleteMany / duplicateMany / updateMany` fans out
     singular methods per ID. Events, cascades, validation preserved.
  3. `skipped[]` captures ACL drops as `{ code: 'forbidden' }` —
     never distinguishes "not yours" from "not found".

feat(ml-webhooks): inbound webhook endpoint + HMAC + fetch worker + 5 workflow triggers

Wave 1-D of the Mercado Livre integration plan: end-to-end webhook
ingestion for the 4 ML topics we subscribe to (orders_v2, questions,
messages, shipments).

API surface (painel-cliente-api)
  - POST /webhooks/mercado-livre (public, HMAC-protected)
  - MlWebhooksService: validateSignature (timing-safe HMAC-SHA256, accepts
    both 'x-signature' and 'x-hub-signature' with or without 'sha256=' prefix),
    lookupCredentialByUserId (OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE credentials),
    checkDedup (Redis SET NX TTL 24h, fails open), enqueueFetchJob (BullMQ).
  - MlWebhooksController ACKs 200 immediately (ML 22s retry window) and
    enqueues a BullMQ job for async processing. Bad HMAC -> 401;
    unknown seller -> 200 (prevents retry storms); duplicate -> 200 no-op.
  - main.ts: capture rawBody via Express json verify callback so HMAC
    validates against the exact received bytes.

Worker (painel-cliente-worker)
  - ml-webhook-fetch.handler.ts: BullMQ consumer of 'ml-webhook-fetch',
    resolves credential with auto-refresh (rotating refresh_token), GETs
    the ML resource with Bearer token, maps topic -> internal event type,
    publishes on Redis Pub/Sub events:{internal userId}.
    Topic routing: orders_v2 -> ML_ORDER_CREATED vs ML_ORDER_UPDATED via
    per-seller 'seen orders' Redis SET (SADD returns 0 when already seen);
    messages -> ML_MESSAGE_RECEIVED only for buyer->seller (suppress seller
    echoes); questions -> ML_QUESTION_RECEIVED; shipments -> ML_SHIPMENT_UPDATED.
    401 -> refresh + retry once; if still 401, mark credential INVALID_TOKEN
    and stop retrying.
  - main.ts: boot the BullMQ worker alongside the existing Redis Streams
    consumer; shared encryption helpers (AES-256-GCM, same scheme as the
    API's EncryptionService) to decrypt/re-encrypt Credential.config.

title: fix(deploy-swarm): derive compose image name from PROJECT_ROOT (worktree-safe)
body:
fix(deploy-swarm): derive compose image name from PROJECT_ROOT (worktree-safe)

Deploy from a git worktree was pushing stale images to the registry.

Root cause:
  `docker compose build` names images as `<project>-<service>:latest`
  where <project> is the lowercased basename of the build context. The
  script hardcoded `wppbbcatalisaio-<service>:latest` which is only
  correct from the main repo dir. From a worktree the compose build
  produced a different image name (e.g. `tenant-scoped-admin-<svc>`),
  while the tag step pointed at the hardcoded name — which existed as
  a stale image from a previous build against the main repo and got
  pushed as staging, silently shipping old code.

  Concretely on 2026-04-16: the painel-cliente staging build baked the
  correct staging VITE_API_URL into `tenant-scoped-admin-painel-cliente`
  but the deploy tagged `wppbbcatalisaio-painel-cliente` (production URL
  from an older build) and pushed THAT as :staging. Users hitting the
  staging panel were silently hitting the prod API.

Fix:
  Compute COMPOSE_PROJECT dynamically from $PROJECT_ROOT (lowercased,
  sanitized to alnum/underscore/hyphen per compose's rules), and use it
  to build the expected local image name. Same pattern building-blocks-v2
  already uses.

  Also add a `docker image inspect` guard right before `docker tag` so
  if the compose build ever produces something unexpected, deploy fails
  loud instead of silently re-tagging a stale image. The error message
  points at PROJECT_ROOT and the expected name, making future drift easy
  to diagnose.

title: fix(bulk): cast TItem after narrow so prod tsc -p tsconfig.build.json accepts it
body:
fix(bulk): cast TItem after narrow so prod tsc -p tsconfig.build.json accepts it

`BulkService.runPerId` had a runtime guard
  if (result !== undefined && result !== null) items.push(result)
that narrows `TItem | void` at runtime but not under
`tsconfig.build.json`'s stricter `strictFunctionTypes` — the type
kept `void` in the union and the Docker build failed with:

  src/common/bulk/bulk.service.ts(197,26): error TS2345: Argument of
  type 'void | Awaited<TItem>' is not assignable to parameter of type
  'TItem'.

dev's `tsc --noEmit` didn't catch this (less strict config),
so it slipped through PR #197 and only surfaced on the prod deploy.

Cast `result as TItem` after the guard — safe because the guard
already excludes undefined/null, which are the only inhabitants of
`void` in this codebase.

Verified locally with the same command the Docker build runs:
  cd apps/painel-cliente-api && npx tsc -p tsconfig.build.json

body:
fix(agents): strip leaked tool-call XML + allow hyphen in agent slug + rewrite VTEX prompts

Dois bugs detectados no smoke staging do PR #204 (VTEX Commerce Workflow):

1. XML de tool call vazando na mensagem WhatsApp
2. Slug com hyphen criado pelo install rejeitado ao editar via UI

## Fix 1 — XML leak (defense-in-depth: prompt + sanitização)

Claude (Sonnet 4.x) tem prior forte de treinamento pro formato Claude Code
(`<function_calls><invoke name="X"><parameter name="Y">...</parameter></invoke></function_calls>
<function_result>...</function_result>`). Quando system prompts descrevem
tools usando pseudocódigo em backticks (ex: `execute_custom_action({...})`)
e instruem "Chame X", o modelo narra a chamada AS TEXT além de usar o tool_use
nativo. O texto contendo XML entra num bloco `text` legítimo, passa por
`extractTextContent`, e vai pro usuário final.

- Reescreve os 6 system prompts VTEX (triage + 5 specialists) em
  `vtex-commerce-workflow.ts`: remove pseudocódigo, usa linguagem natural,
  adiciona guardrail "## Formato de resposta" proibindo XML/pseudocódigo.
- Adiciona defense-in-depth em `claude.provider.ts#extractTextContent`:
  strip regex de `<function_calls>`, `<function_result>`, `<invoke>`,
  `<parameter>` como última trava (cobre TODOS os agentes, não só VTEX).
- Novo spec `claude.provider.spec.ts` (8 tests) cobrindo os casos de strip.

## Fix 2 — slug aceitar hyphen

Install flow gera slug kebab-case `${template.slug}-${agentDef.slug}`
(ex: `vtex-commerce-whatsapp-vtex-triage`), mas o validator de create/edit
usa regex `/^[a-z0-9_]+$/` que rejeita hyphen. `agentsService.create()`
chamado via service layer bypassa class-validator, então install funciona;
mas edit via UI re-valida e falha.

Hyphens já são padrão em workflow/agent template slugs (kebab-case).
Amplia regex pra aceitar ambos.

- `create-agent.dto.ts:43` — `/^[a-z0-9_]+$/` → `/^[a-z0-9_-]+$/`
- `AgentModal.tsx:313` — mesmo regex, client-side
- `agents/AgentWizardModal.tsx:388` — mesmo regex, client-side
- Todas as messages atualizadas pra mencionar hífens

## Verificação

- 8/8 tests novos em `claude.provider.spec.ts`
- 58/58 tests do escopo (claude.provider + vtex-commerce-workflow +
  workflow-templates.spec + knowledge-router)
- Frontend TSC: 0 erros
- Regressões: nenhuma. 11 erros TSC + 10 testes falhando são pré-existentes
  (tools-executor, OAUTH2/ML, ollama integration) — todos já existiam antes
  deste PR e estão rastreados em outras branches/PRs.

## Referência de memória criada

`reference_iam_jwt_format.md` — documenta que JWT pra panel-cliente-api
requer `sub=IAM_UUID`, não cuid local. Self-signed JWTs com cuid local
criam phantom users. Descoberto ao debugar smoke staging (erro obscuro
de SEND_MESSAGE foi conseqüência de workflow criado sob phantom sem acesso
ao device/credencial do admin real).

body:
fix(ai): unbreak Verification Contracts + restore AI Assistant bubble + tests

Post-validation fixes to the AI Intelligence Layer (a3ef7845) after live
testing revealed four silent bugs that made verification a no-op for the
most common flows. Also restores the floating bubble trigger to replace
the thin docked strip users found hard to discover.

## AI Intelligence Layer — Verification Contracts

- contracts.ts: split `idField` into `resultIdField` (read from tool result
  payload) + optional `verifyParamField` (name expected by the verify tool).
  Previous single field was used for both purposes, so `create_lead` /
  `create_agent` / `create_workflow` / `update_lead` called the verify tool
  with `{ id: ... }` while `get_lead`/`get_agent`/`get_workflow` require
  `{ leadId }` / `{ agentId }` / `{ workflowId }`. Verification never ran
  end-to-end in any of those contracts.
- verification.service.ts: unwrap `{ success, data }` SDK envelope on both
  the tool result and the verify-tool response. Use `'data' in x ? x.data
  : x` instead of `?? x` so `data: null` (resource not found) falls through
  to the FAIL branch instead of being masked by the truthy wrapper.
- openai-compatible.provider.ts: invoke `callbacks.onVerifyTool` after
  tool execution, matching the existing Claude provider. Verification was
  previously Claude-only, so anyone using OpenAI/OpenRouter/Qwen/Ollama
  got nothing.
- tool-format.ts: `toolResultsToOpenAI` / `toolResultsToAnthropic` now
  append `verificationMessage` to the serialized tool result so the LLM
  actually sees the verification outcome (previously the field was set by
  the provider and silently dropped during serialization).

## Unit tests — 34 new + 4 pre-existing

- knowledge-base.service.spec.ts (10): contributor registration, keyword
  scoring, skill filter, maxTokens cap, result composition
- verification.service.spec.ts (13): one test per contract + envelope
  unwrapping + null `data` handling + thrown-error path + no-contract path
- session-compressor.service.spec.ts (11): threshold, preservation of last
  5 messages, summary-message synthesis, provider-error fallback

## Pre-existing test fixes (unrelated regressions surfaced during validation)

- tools-executor.service.spec.ts: SDK `whatsappDevices.list` now returns
  `{ data, pagination }` instead of a bare array (SDK migration the mocks
  hadn't caught up with). Updated 3 failing `add_workflow_trigger` tests.
- ai-conversation-workflow-automation.spec.ts + whatsapp-messaging.spec.ts:
  same SDK envelope migration; updated the shared device mock and the
  inline "devices offline" mock.

router (doesn't use this prompt). Chitchat goes from ~760 to ~820
input tokens. Trade: tiny cost increase for a measurable reduction
in silent outcome bugs across all providers.

title: feat(auth): X-Target-Organization-Id header for PANEL_CROSS_TENANT api keys (#113)
body:
feat(auth): X-Target-Organization-Id header for PANEL_CROSS_TENANT api keys (#113)

* feat(auth): X-Target-Organization-Id header for PANEL_CROSS_TENANT api keys

Allows api keys whose authenticated user has the PANEL_CROSS_TENANT IAM
permission to override the organizationId context on a per-request basis.

Required so the Catalisa platform's shared x-api-key can manage per-tenant
resources (billing accounts, subscriptions, invoices) in the Billing BB
without minting per-tenant JWTs.

Gating:
- Only the api-key auth path honors the header; JWT path ignores it (JWT
  carries its own org context and overrides would be confusing).
- ApiKeyContext has no 'permissions' field on the cached struct, so we
  lazily resolve roles -> permissions via AssociationRepository when the
  header is present. No DB hit on requests without the header.
- Missing PANEL_CROSS_TENANT -> 403.
- Invalid UUID shape -> 400 (short-circuits role lookup).
- No header -> no change (regression-safe).

Tests: 20 unit tests (15 pre-existing + 5 new covering allow / deny-perm
/ deny-uuid / no-op / jwt-path-ignore).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): use Prisma directly instead of AssociationRepository in middleware

AssociationRepository is registered only inside the IAM module's DI
container. Services running in standalone mode (MODULE_SELF=billing etc.)
don't have access to it, so Container.get(AssociationRepository) threw
and turned into the generic 'Failed to resolve api-key permissions' 500.

Since the DB is shared across all BB services (monolithic schema, single
postgres), query the association table directly via Container.get(
PrismaClient) — which is registered by registerCore() for every service.

Tests updated to mock prisma.association.findMany. 20/20 pass.

Adds two admin-scoped PATCH endpoints and the corresponding UI forms so

without going to SQL.

Deferred by design (will land as a Phase 2.5 sub-plan):
- Role change — needs a proper IAM association-update flow. Writing
  directly to the local DB violates `feedback_iam_source_of_truth` and
  gets overwritten on next login by iam-jwt.strategy's role sync.
- Email change — email is the IAM login identifier; changing it locally
  creates drift with IAM.
