- `PATCH /admin/clients/:userId` with AdminUpdateClientDto (name, phone).
  Delegates to UsersService.update. E.164 phone validation.
- `PATCH /admin/clients/:userId/organization` with
  AdminUpdateClientOrganizationDto (name, billingEmail, billingName,
  document). Writes via prisma directly — bypassing
  OrganizationsService.update which scopes to the caller's own org.
  slug, bbOrganizationId, bbBillingAccountId, iamOrganizationId are
  deliberately immutable.
- 9 new Jest cases (27 total) covering staff rejection, empty-body 400,
  missing-org 404, field stripping, and the slug/BB-IDs immutability
  invariant.

title: feat(chats): persist outbound WhatsApp messages in chat history
body:
feat(chats): persist outbound WhatsApp messages in chat history

Outgoing messages sent from the CRM chat UI are now persisted immediately
in the Message table with a correlationId placeholder and deliveryStatus
'pending'. When the BB echo (messages.upsert with fromMe=true) arrives,
MessageProcessor reconciles by swapping the placeholder messageId for the
real wamid and flipping status to 'sent'.

Why: before this, ChatsService.sendMessage/sendMedia only called BB and
returned the correlationId — nothing was written to the Message table.
The row only materialized when the 1-minute EventProcessor cron processed
the BB echo, so outgoing messages disappeared from the chat view. Now the
frontend's existing fetchMessages-after-send call immediately picks up the
pending placeholder, and the reconciled wamid lands seconds later via the
sync echo processing added to BbEventsController.

Key changes:
- Message.correlationId column + index on deliveryStatus (migration)
- OutboundMessagePersistenceService: shared persistence for CRM + future
  workflow paths; emits CHAT_MESSAGE_SENT webhook; meters via
  UsageMeterService with idempotencyHint='outbound-<correlationId>'
- MessageProcessor: reconcile pending placeholders by chatId+fromMe+pending
  (FIFO within 60s window); skip meter for fromMe=true to avoid
  double-billing with the direct save
- BbEventsController: fire-and-forget EventProcessorService.processEventNow
  inline so messages land in DB within seconds instead of 1-minute cron

Unit tests: 4697 passed, 0 failed (includes 12 new tests for
OutboundMessagePersistence + MessageProcessor reconciliation + 4 new
ChatsService send tests).

Deferred to follow-up PRs:
- Workflow SendMessage/SendMedia handlers direct-save (avoids chat
  resolution race with MessageProcessor; sync echo processing already
  eliminates the lag for the current echo path)
- Frontend status indicator (pending/sent/delivered/read checkmarks)

body:
fix(admin-clients): include Masters only (parentId=null), drop STAFF_ROLES gate (#247)

The admin "Gestão de Clientes" list was filtering PANEL_ADMIN out and NOT
filtering sub-users (PANEL_MEMBER / parentId!=null). Two consequences:
- Admins couldn't manage their own plan/overrides via the UI (invisible list row)
- Sub-users leaked into the list, but have no actionable billing surface
  (they inherit org + billing account from their Master)

Align the filter to the real invariant — billing belongs to Masters:

  listClients()   where: { parentId: null }   // was: role notIn [PANEL_ADMIN]
  assertIsClient  rejects sub-users (BadRequest); drops staff-role check

Effect:
- Admin appears in the list alongside other Masters → can change plan +
  apply overrides on themselves through the existing flows
- Sub-users no longer appear → removes dozens of lines of dead UI rows
- Attempts to operate billing on a sub-user now fail early with a clear
  message instead of a mystery 500 from BB

Tests: admin-clients (50) + admin-billing-override (all) green.

body:
fix(bb-calendar): use IAM client_credentials service token instead of user JWT

Root cause of staging 500: user JWTs from panel client-orgs don't carry
CALENDAR_READ/WRITE perms (those are new BB IAM perms, not in the 'ALL
perms' seed for client orgs). Forwarding the user JWT to BB Calendar

500 for the frontend.

Also: the X-Target-Organization-Id header we were injecting is a no-op
on BB today (Part B pending in project_bb_target_org_override_plan). So
the 'shared provider model' needed a different mechanism.

Fix: BbCalendarClientFactory.createForService() — fetches a service token
via IAM OAuth 'client_credentials' grant using CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID +
CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_SECRET (already available in all envs, already used by
BillingClientService). In-memory caching with 60s buffer before expiry +
cache invalidation on 401. All 4 consumers swapped from createWithToken
to createForService:
  - CalendarIntegrationsService (4 call-sites)
  - AdminCalendarProvidersService (1)
  - 6 workflow handlers (6)

Specs updated accordingly. 4818/4818 calendar-related tests pass.

Provider-configs had to be re-registered under the painel-service org
(b0000000-...-000002 in stg) — service token resolves to that org, not
root Catalisa. Legacy configs in root org (c0ff6afd-... + 30c89764-...)
kept temporarily; delete after full validation.

providerType if no isDefault. Fixes the 'Google is default but user
wants Outlook' case.

title: fix(credentials): skip OAUTH2 field validation for BB Calendar proxied creds
body:
fix(credentials): skip OAUTH2 field validation for BB Calendar proxied creds

BB Calendar credentials are a proxied shape: the OAuth app (clientId,
clientSecret, redirectUri, authorizationUrl, tokenUrl) lives in
building-blocks-v2 `CalendarProviderConfig`, not in painel. Painel
only persists the `connectionId` that references BB's `CalendarConnection`.

The generic `OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE` field validator was designed for
ML/VTEX (where painel owns the OAuth app) and required those 5 fields.
That caused `completeOAuth` to fail with "Field 'clientId' is required
for OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE credentials" right after the user consented
at Google/Microsoft — breaking the calendar connect flow in staging.

Fix: `CredentialStorageService.create` and `update` now skip the schema
field check when `serviceName === CALENDAR_BB_SERVICE_NAME`. The BB
shape is still structurally validated by its TypeScript interface
(`CalendarBbCredentialConfig`) and by BB Calendar itself when painel
later calls `listConnections()` / `deleteConnection()`.

- Moved `CALENDAR_BB_SERVICE_NAME` to `shared/bb-calendar/constants.ts`
  to avoid a circular import (calendar-integrations → credentials →
  storage → calendar-integrations).
- +3 unit tests: BB-calendar skip on create, ML still errors without
  clientId (regression guard), BB-calendar skip on update.

Alternatives rejected:
- Placeholder values like `bb-calendar-managed-outlook` (commit
  c832ef80, later reverted in f71a30aa): pollutes DB rows with fake
  fields that imply an OAuth flow painel doesn't run.
- New credential type enum (e.g. `EXTERNAL_OAUTH_CONNECTION`):
  disproportionate for a one-field validator gap; would require
  Prisma schema + UI form updates.

title: fix(ai-assistant): 4 workflow-construction bugs found by stg deep tests
body:
fix(ai-assistant): 4 workflow-construction bugs found by stg deep tests

Bug sweep uncovered by the 6-scenario deep-test battery on stg 1.15.5.
All 4 were pre-existing behaviors, not introduced by PR #249 — they
just become visible once the assistant is actually executing complex
workflows successfully.

1. **DUPLICATE_ACTION_NAME guard** (tools-executor.service.ts)
   Split-turn construction (turn 1 hits MAX_ITERATIONS mid-build, turn 2
   continues) used to silently duplicate actions because the model had
   no visibility of DB state between turns. Stg scenario C produced 12
   actions where 6 were expected (2×RUN_AGENT, 2×UPDATE_LEAD, 3×DELAY).
   Fix: reject when `stepName` matches an existing action; return the
   existing action's metadata + full list, so the model can either skip
   or pick a different name. Adds regression test.

2. **toggle_workflow required by default** (plan-mode prompt rule 7)
   Stg scenarios B and C left workflows at `active=false` because the
   model forgot to activate after `finalize_workflow_diagram`. User
   tests and sees "it doesn't work" — worse than any error. Rule now
   mandates `toggle_workflow(id, active=true)` unless user asked to
   keep inactive.

3. **Pre-check on continuation turns** (plan-mode prompt rule 8)
   In turn-2+ of a workflow-building session, model must call
   `list_workflow_actions(workflowId)` BEFORE `add_workflow_action`.
   Combined with fix #1 this turns silent duplication into a fast,
   deterministic retry loop.

4. **CONDITIONAL nested-actions pattern** (plan-mode prompt rule 9)
   Model was producing two semantically-different patterns: (a) actions
   INSIDE branches[].actions (correct routing), (b) actions top-level
   with dependsOn referencing conditional name (runs ALL branches in
   parallel, not gated). Stg scenario B exhibited (b). Explicit rule
   + reason makes pattern (a) the default.

Also: agent-executor.service.ts gained a "resource-discovery rule" in
its built system prompt — when the user asks for data that could come
from multiple sources and a list_* tool exists, LIST first, don't ask
the user to disambiguate preemptively. Fixes stg scenario E where the
calendar agent asked for an integration ID instead of calling
list_calendar_events.

title: fix(calendar): OAuth return — derive connectionId via listConnections diff

fix(calendar): OAuth return — derive connectionId via listConnections diff

BB Calendar does NOT append any identifiers to the redirect URL (see
building-blocks-v2/src/calendar/services/connection.service.ts#handleCallback
— returns the state-stored redirectUrl as-is). So Agent B/E's flow expecting
?connectionId= in the query param was broken: user got 'Parâmetro
connectionId ausente' on return.

Fix: completeOAuth() now takes only userId + jwt and finds the just-created
connection by diffing listConnections() (via service token) against local
Credentials already claiming a connectionId. Picks newest unclaimed ACTIVE.
Race window (two users finishing OAuth within the same millisecond) is
negligible — human consent takes seconds.

- CalendarIntegrationsService.completeOAuth: drop connectionId arg,
  run listConnections + local findAll in parallel, filter out claimed,
  sort by createdAt desc, take first
- Controller GET /oauth/callback-return: drop @Query('connectionId')

Hardens AI agent executions (invoked from workflows or ad-hoc) against
runaway loops, silent timeouts, and provider degradation. All guard-rails
are inherited by every agent — no per-agent opt-in needed.

**Budget cascade (action > agent > env, default 60s)**
- New `Agent.executionBudgetMs` column (nullable, 10000–600000ms)
- New `config.timeoutMs` on RUN_AGENT actions (same range, per-action override)
- Env `AGENT_DEFAULT_EXECUTION_BUDGET_MS` as fallback
- AbortController wired into agent chat → Claude SDK → tool loop
  so wall-clock exhaustion interrupts in-flight HTTP requests, not just
  next-iteration boundaries

**Per-tool timeout**
- `TOOL_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 30s) wraps each tool in claude.provider
- Returns synthetic `{__toolTimeout: true}` result so LLM can recover
  (pick another tool, respond with partial info) instead of killing the loop

**Error classification + selective retry**
- New `error-classifier.ts`: timeout / rate_limit / network / provider_5xx / client_error
- RUN_AGENT retries once at 50% budget for transient categories only
- 4xx never retries (caller's fault); rate_limit handled inside provider

- Redis-backed state machine (closed / open / half_open)
- Opens after 5 failures in 10min, fast-fails for 5min, then probe

title: fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe) (#261)
body:
fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe) (#261)

PR #260 added the BullMQ workflow-execution queue but didn't pass a
deterministic jobId. With a single api replica that's fine — there's
exactly one Pub/Sub subscriber. Once we scale `wpp_painel-cliente-api`
to 2+ replicas every replica spins up its own EventListener subscriber,
Pub/Sub fans every message out to all of them, and without a stable
jobId each replica enqueues an independent job per matched trigger —
the workflow runs N times.

Fix: pass `jobId = "${eventId}:${triggerId}"` when enqueueing.

- `eventId` comes from the publisher (`event.id`/`event.eventId` set by
  WebhookEventsService.emit, which uuidv4s every emit). For synthetic
  publishes that don't carry an id we fall back to a sha256 hash of
  channel + type + userId + payload — same input on each replica yields
  the same hash, so dedup still holds.
- BullMQ rejects duplicate jobIds across all states (waiting/active/
  completed/failed), so the second enqueue is a cheap no-op and the
  workflow runs exactly once even when N replicas race to add it.

This unlocks horizontal scaling of `wpp_painel-cliente-api` without
risking duplicate workflow execution for tenants with active LEAD_*
or workflow.* triggers.

Tests: 3 new specs in event-listener.service.spec.ts cover the
event.id-derived jobId, the hash fallback for synthetic events,
and idempotency across re-deliveries. All 11/11 spec cases pass.

Bumps painel-cliente-api 1.15.14 → 1.15.15.

title: fix(workflows): async dispatch via BullMQ + AI_HUB_AGENT non-text skip + subscriber resilience (#260)
body:
fix(workflows): async dispatch via BullMQ + AI_HUB_AGENT non-text skip + subscriber resilience (#260)

Three coordinated fixes for the production timeout reports on agent flows
and bulk-import-driven workflows.

1. **BullMQ workflow-execution queue (Frente A)** — `EventListenerService`
   used to `await WorkflowExecutionService.execute()` inline inside the
   Redis Pub/Sub `pmessage` callback. With one api replica, that drained
   one workflow at a time per tenant. Bulk imports of N leads fanned out
   into N `LEAD_CREATED` events that the subscriber processed serially —
   later leads appeared to "time out" because their workflow only started
   minutes after the import.

   New `WorkflowExecutionQueueService` registers a BullMQ `Queue` + `Worker`
   in the same NestJS process. The producer adds a lightweight
   `{ workflowId, payload, triggerId }` job; the worker re-fetches the
   workflow from Prisma (picks up any state change between enqueue and
   execute) and delegates to `WorkflowExecutionService.execute()`. The
   subscriber returns immediately, so backpressure on Pub/Sub is gone.

   Behind the `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_VIA_QUEUE` flag — defaulting OFF for
   now — so prod can flip it on, observe, and roll back via env in seconds
   if anything misbehaves. Concurrency tunable via
   `WORKFLOW_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` (default 5).

   Defense in depth: if `queue.add()` itself throws (e.g. Redis
   unavailable), the listener falls back to inline execution so events
   are never silently dropped.

2. **AI_HUB_AGENT skip on empty message (Frente B)** — Audio, image,
   sticker and other non-text inbound messages interpolate
   `$helpers.getMessageText(...)` to an empty string, which was making
   the handler return `success: false` with
   `'AI_HUB_AGENT requires message in config'`. That bubbled up as a
   workflow failure and polluted Sentry. The CORRETOR tenant logs were
   full of these.

   The handler now returns `success: true` with
   `data: { skipped: true, reason: 'non-text-message' }` when message is
   empty. Downstream actions can branch on `output.skipped` if they need
   non-text-specific behavior; otherwise the workflow keeps running.

3. **Subscriber Redis resilience (Frente C)** — `EventListenerService`'s
   raw `new Redis(...)` call did not match the
   `createResilientRedis` factory used elsewhere, so it didn't recover
   gracefully from DigitalOcean managed Redis ECONNRESET cycles. We
   added a sibling `createResilientRedisSubscriber` (psubscribe-friendly:
   keeps `enableOfflineQueue: true` and `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` so
   the long-running subscribe survives reconnect, while still applying
   `retryStrategy` and `reconnectOnError`) and migrated the listener
   onto it.

Tests: 4 new spec files, 20 unit tests covering producer enqueue,
consumer execute, missing-workflow no-op, AI_HUB_AGENT skip path
(empty/null/undefined), inline fallback when queue throws, legacy
synchronous path. Full painel-cliente-api jest run on touched modules:
2911 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed across 107 suites.

Bumps painel-cliente-api 1.15.13 → 1.15.14.

title: fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe)
body:
fix(workflows): deterministic jobId on workflow-execution enqueue (multi-replica safe)

PR #260 added the BullMQ workflow-execution queue but didn't pass a
deterministic jobId. With a single api replica that's fine — there's
exactly one Pub/Sub subscriber. Once we scale `wpp_painel-cliente-api`
to 2+ replicas every replica spins up its own EventListener subscriber,
Pub/Sub fans every message out to all of them, and without a stable
jobId each replica enqueues an independent job per matched trigger —
the workflow runs N times.

Fix: pass `jobId = "${eventId}:${triggerId}"` when enqueueing.

- `eventId` comes from the publisher (`event.id`/`event.eventId` set by
  WebhookEventsService.emit, which uuidv4s every emit). For synthetic
  publishes that don't carry an id we fall back to a sha256 hash of
  channel + type + userId + payload — same input on each replica yields
  the same hash, so dedup still holds.
- BullMQ rejects duplicate jobIds across all states (waiting/active/
  completed/failed), so the second enqueue is a cheap no-op and the
  workflow runs exactly once even when N replicas race to add it.

This unlocks horizontal scaling of `wpp_painel-cliente-api` without
risking duplicate workflow execution for tenants with active LEAD_*
or workflow.* triggers.

Tests: 3 new specs in event-listener.service.spec.ts cover the
event.id-derived jobId, the hash fallback for synthetic events,
and idempotency across re-deliveries. All 11/11 spec cases pass.

Bumps painel-cliente-api 1.15.14 → 1.15.15.

title: feat(wpp): GET /messages/media/:messageId — lazy materialize via file-storage
body:
feat(wpp): GET /messages/media/:messageId — lazy materialize via file-storage

First call: looks up the WppMessage, fetches the live driver session
for the device that received it, calls driver.downloadMedia which
rehydrates the persisted protobuf and pulls bytes from the WhatsApp
CDN, then registers the file in the file-storage BB (via facade),
PUTs the bytes to the presigned upload URL, confirms the upload,
caches the resulting fileId in WppMessage.mediaFileId, and 302s
to the file-storage download URL.

Subsequent calls: cache hit on mediaFileId — straight 302 to a fresh
presigned URL, no driver round-trip, no re-download from the
WhatsApp CDN. Validated end-to-end: 770ms cold, 13ms warm.

If the cached download URL ever fails, falls through to re-
materialize rather than 500ing.

Error mapping:
- 404 if message not found / wrong org
- 400 if message has no media body (text/reaction/etc)
- 409 if legacy row predates deviceId / preserved protobuf
- 503 if device offline (operator reconnects + retries)
- 502 if WhatsApp CDN failed / media expired

file-storage's MimeType allowlist is narrow (PDF/PNG/JPEG/octet-stream)
because it inherits from a Smithy schema designed for KYC docs. WhatsApp
covers video/audio/sticker too, so we tell file-storage application/
octet-stream for those and keep the real mimetype on the persisted
WppMessage.payload for downstream consumers. Bytes are unchanged.

title: fix(wpp): per-device Redis lock in restoreActiveSessions for replica safety
body:
fix(wpp): per-device Redis lock in restoreActiveSessions for replica safety

The previous restoreActiveSessions fix (PR #124) made the worker actually
re-establish driver sessions on cold start, but had no cross-process
coordination: with replicas>1 — or during a rolling deploy where the new
worker boots before the old one shuts down — every replica would query
the same `status='open'` rows and race on each device. Multiple Baileys
sockets would attempt to bind to the same WhatsApp linked device,
producing 401/conflict disconnects (Meta enforces a single live socket
per linked device).

This change introduces atomic SETNX semantics on RedisService
(`setIfAbsent(key, value, ttlSeconds)`, backed by `SET key value NX EX`)
and uses it inside `restoreActiveSessions` to claim a per-device restore
lock at `wpp:reconnect-lock:{orgId}:{deviceId}` (30s TTL, same prefix as
the existing post-disconnect reconnect lock) before doing any work.
First replica to call SETNX wins and reconnects; the rest see the lock
held and skip.

Recovery characteristic: if a worker dies mid-restore (crash, OOM, etc.),
the lock survives until its 30s TTL elapses. The next boot will pick the
device up. Single-replica deploys are unchanged (lock always acquired).

Validated locally: a clean boot acquires the lock and reaches
`state_change → open` in ~2s; an immediate second boot (lock still
held from prior process) cleanly logs "Restore lock held by another
process, skipping" without spawning a duplicate driver.

Bumps to 1.0.7.

title: fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions queries devices across all orgs
body:
fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions queries devices across all orgs

The session-worker boot path called `deviceRepository.findAll('', { status: 'open' })`,
passing an empty string as `organizationId`. The repo's `findAll` filters by
`WHERE organizationId = $1`, so the query effectively became
`organizationId = '' AND status = 'open'`, returning zero rows in production.
Net effect: no device was ever resurrected on session-worker boot — every restart
left previously connected WhatsApp sessions dead until a manual reconnect request.

Changes:
- Add `DeviceRepository.findAllAcrossOrgs({ status?, driver? })`: cross-org lookup
  that returns `DeviceEntity[]` directly (no pagination wrapper). It is intentionally
  not exposed via the public router/service layer — it exists only for boot-time
  reconciliation.
- `SessionManager.restoreActiveSessions` now calls `findAllAcrossOrgs` and treats
  the result as a flat array.

Why cross-org (and not "loop per org"): the current deployment runs a single shared
session-worker process that owns sockets for every tenant. Boot-time recovery has
to enumerate devices regardless of organizationId. If we ever shard the worker per
tenant, the call site changes (caller already has the orgId), but the repository
method stays useful for ops/diagnostics.

Tests:
- New repo tests cover no-filter (multi-org rows), status filter, driver filter.
- Session-manager `restoreActiveSessions` suite migrated to the new method and a
  regression test was added: two devices in distinct orgs, both `status: 'open'`,
  both must produce `reconnect_attempt` log entries.

title: fix(wpp): coordinator waits 10s before XADD to let other replicas join group
body:
fix(wpp): coordinator waits 10s before XADD to let other replicas join group

The previous Option C implementation worked correctly (1 SETNX winner
enqueues, no duplication, devices restored end-to-end) but local 3-worker
test showed 3-0-0 distribution: worker A's first XREADGROUP COUNT=10
drained the entire stream before workers B/C registered their consumers
in the group. Redis Streams delivers a whole batch to whichever consumer
asks first; round-robin only happens between consumers actively blocked
on XREADGROUP.

Adding a 10s delay between SETNX win and XADD gives Docker Swarm rolling
update the typical 5-15s window it needs to spawn the next replica and
have its consumer register in the group. Worst case: a slow replica
(>10s boot) misses the burst and still gets nothing. Defensive option
(XINFO-poll for consumer count) documented in
docs/wpp/auto-restore-and-distribution.md for future reference.

title: feat(wpp): distribute restoreActiveSessions via Redis Streams across replicas
body:
feat(wpp): distribute restoreActiveSessions via Redis Streams across replicas

Coordinator-elect (`SET NX EX wpp:restore-coordinator`, 60s) ensures exactly
one worker queries the DB and XADDs one SESSION_RESTORE job per device into
the existing stream; the consumer group then round-robins each device to
exactly one replica. Per-device idempotency is preserved via the existing
`wpp:reconnect-lock:{org}:{device}` SET NX EX lock plus an in-memory
`this.sessions.has` short-circuit, so stream redelivery is safe.

Why not the previous "lock per device only" design: with N replicas each
running their own restore loop they would each enqueue duplicate
`reconnect_attempt` log rows and fight over the same Baileys socket — even
with the per-device lock, the losers still did the DB scan and the log
write. The coordinator-elect cuts that to one DB scan and one set of log
rows total, regardless of replica count.

title: fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions actually re-establishes driver sessions
body:
fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions actually re-establishes driver sessions

Pre-bug: restoreActiveSessions only wrote a `reconnect_attempt` row in
wpp_connection_logs and returned. No driver was instantiated, no socket
opened — workers came up "running" with the in-memory sessions Map empty
while DB still showed devices as `open`. Effective behaviour: every
worker restart silently dropped every previously-paired session until
someone hit POST /devices/:id/reconnect manually.

The earlier PR #122 fix (`findAllAcrossOrgs`) made the query work, but
the actual restore step was a no-op all along (visible in git history
since the first wpp commit f9fbd92).

Now: each restored row goes through `getOrCreateSession` after the log
is written. wireEventListeners fires, the Baileys socket opens, and the
driver's `connection.update` event flips `wpp_devices.status` back to
`open` (or `closed` if auth was revoked remotely). Per-device errors
are caught and logged at warn — one stale auth doesn't block the others.

Validated end-to-end locally: a paired device went from cold boot to
state_change=open in ~2.3s without any manual reconnect call.

Also bumps to 1.0.6.

fix(ai-tools): cap list_* tool results to prevent context inflation

URGENT FIX continuation. Bench 2026-05-02 after fixing leadtype context
showed 3 cases REGRESSING (+44k tokens) because they call list_*
tools (list_whatsapp_devices, list_workflows, list_leads, list_agents)
that returned ALL of the user's resources unbounded into the next
LLM call's input tokens.

Smoking gun from bench JSON:
- broadcast-message t1 tools: [list_leads, list_whatsapp_devices, suggest_navigation] → 35193 tokens
- workflow-update-status t1 tools: [list_whatsapp_devices] → 44615 tokens
- workflow-followup t1 tools: [list_whatsapp_devices, request_resource_selection] → 47639 tokens
- agent-create-basic (control, no list_*): 9880 tokens, latency 10s ⭐

The 3 worsened cases all call list_whatsapp_devices. Stg has dozens of
test devices accumulated; each device serialized with CUID + name + phone
≈ 50 tokens. 100 devices = 5000 tokens injected after EVERY list call.
Same pattern for list_workflows, list_leads, list_agents.

returns top-N items + total + truncatedHint instructing the AI to use
request_resource_selection or specific filters when total > shown.

- list_whatsapp_devices: 10  (sort connected first)
- list_workflows:        15  (sort active first, recent updatedAt)
- list_leads:            20  (also enforces server-side limit≤20 to ignore inflated input.limit)
- list_agents:           10  (sort active first)

The truncatedHint is critical: tells the AI explicitly NOT to keep
asking for larger lists, but instead use:
  - request_resource_selection → for UI-driven picking
  - get_<resource>(id) → for specific fetch
  - filters / search params → for narrowing

title: fix(ai-assistant): hydrate cached skills on implicit selection turns
body:
fix(ai-assistant): hydrate cached skills on implicit selection turns

Bug seen in prod 2026-05-04:
  Turn 1: "Quero workflow para minha adega..." → 2 tools called ✓
  Turn 2: "vamos usar o 3414"             → 0 tools called, AI fabricated
                                            "Instalado! ID: wfl_cmlz..."

Root cause (ai-assistant.service.ts:152-197):
- Intent router classifies short follow-ups without explicit confirmation
  tokens as chitchat (rawIsChitchat=true).
- Previous Fix #4 hydration block only re-hydrated cached skills when
  detectConfirmation matched ("sim", "ok", "pode", emoji, ...).
- "vamos usar o 3414" is a SELECTION, not a confirmation → fails the
  pattern → hydratedFromCache=false → toolsToUse=[] → LLM has no real
  tools but conversation context says it should install/create something
  → hallucinates success.

Fix:
- Extract a static helper `isImplicitContinuation(message)` that returns
  true for short messages (<80 chars) that aren't standalone greetings
  and don't contain negation/cancellation tokens.
- Try the helper first in the Fix #4 block; fall back to the existing
  detectConfirmation path. Behavior is strictly more permissive — every
  prior confirmation still hydrates, plus selection/continuation turns.
- Static so it's testable without the full DI graph.

Tests: 52 cases covering implicit continuations ("vamos usar o 3414",
"esse aí", "o 11999..."), explicit confirmations ("sim", "ok", emoji),
negations ("não, cancela", "esquece"), standalone greetings ("oi", "bom
dia"), boundary cases (length 79/80, case-insensitive), and the exact
prod transcript turn that broke.

Full ai-assistant suite: 1515 passed / 1515.

Context: docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md (continuation
of Phase 0 hardening, post PRs #262 #263 #264).

override would be cleaner long-term, but the env bump is non-invasive,

Cache presence IS the mid-task signal. Previous gates (isImplicitContinuation

workflow recreation flow):

classification layer, not provider response layer.

because: (a) cache TTL 30min auto-expires when task done, (b) loaded

body:
fix(ai-orchestrator): SEND_MESSAGE AFTER agent é OBRIGATÓRIA, não proibida

User pegou regressão: meu fix anti-pattern #6 ("agente como única action")
deixou o agent gerando resposta SEM ninguém enviar pro user. Atendimento
WhatsApp tem dois pares de SEND_MESSAGE, com semântica oposta:

- ❌ STATIC SEND_MESSAGE *ANTES* de RUN_AGENT  (canned greeting tone-deaf)
- ✅ DYNAMIC SEND_MESSAGE *DEPOIS* de RUN_AGENT consumindo
  {{actions.AGENT.output.text}}  (envia resposta do agent ao user — sem
  ela atendimento não existe)

Padrão correto:

  trigger: MESSAGE_RECEIVED
    └─ action 1: RUN_AGENT  ("vetVirtual")
         └─ action 2: SEND_MESSAGE
              text={{actions.vetVirtual.output.text}}, dependsOn=[vetVirtual]
         └─ action 3 opcional: CREATE_LEAD se output do agent indica intenção

**Prompt anti-pattern #6 atualizado**:
- Seção "PADRÃO CORRETO" agora mostra 2 actions (agent + send), não 1
- Aviso CRÍTICO ⚠️ explicando que RUN_AGENT só GERA, SEND_MESSAGE ENVIA
- Exemplos concretos (igreja, petshop, vinharia) com SEND_MESSAGE após
- Auto-checklist 6.4 reescrito: pergunta "depois ou antes?" e tem
  duas perguntas separadas pra SEND_MESSAGE e pra RUN_AGENT

**Validator novo**: WORKFLOW_AGENT_RESPONSE_NOT_SENT
- Severity: error
- Só fire em workflows com trigger MESSAGE_RECEIVED (heurística "atendimento
  WhatsApp" — em workflows agendados/internos o agent pode legitimamente
  não enviar mensagem)
- Detecta RUN_AGENT/AI_HUB_AGENT cuja output não é consumido por NENHUM
  SEND_MESSAGE downstream
- Mensagem: "ADICIONE SEND_MESSAGE com text={{actions.X.output.text}}"

Inline validation hook em finalize_workflow_diagram já injeta esse erro
no tool_result com instrução, então o modelo auto-corrige antes de

E2E smoke on stg revealed: when chat routed through clarify+plan phases (Builder

examples of tool_use blocks. The model then mimics that style in its TEXT
response when no tools are made available (clarify uses provider.complete,
not completeWithTools).

clarify+plan branch in OrchestrationService.run and routes straight to the
executor's single-shot path. The model gets all 155 tools (TOOLS_REGISTRY +
preview) and the orchestrator-enriched system prompt with anti-patterns +

fix(ai-orchestrator): inline workflow validation on finalize + ABSOLUTE anti-pattern #6

User retested with "Atendimento Igreja" and got the same broken pattern
(SEND_MESSAGE → RUN_AGENT) DESPITE anti-pattern #6 being deployed. Root cause:
Claude has a strong training-data bias toward "greet first then process",
and the previous prompt was too soft (listed exceptions that the model
rationalized into "this case qualifies").

Three-layer reinforcement:

1. **Prompt: anti-pattern #6 made ABSOLUTE**
   - Header: "REGRA ABSOLUTA — leia 3×"
   - "NUNCA, JAMAIS, EM HIPÓTESE NENHUMA" + emoji ⛔
   - Concrete examples for igreja/petshop/vinharia showing the right pattern
     (RUN_AGENT as first action, single-action workflow)
   - Section "6.2 Exceções — NARROW e raras" reduces to 2 cases (LGPD
     disclaimer, off-hours filter), explicitly tells the model "if you don't
     have absolute clarity, OMIT"
   - Section "6.4 Auto-checklist" — explicit yes/no questions the model
     should ask itself BEFORE calling add_workflow_action

2. **Validator severity bumped warning → ERROR**
   - WORKFLOW_STATIC_GREETING_BEFORE_AGENT now blocks isValid=false
   - Error message tells the model exactly what to do (REMOVA, mover conteúdo
     pro systemPrompt do agente)

3. **Inline validation hook on finalize_workflow_diagram**
   - executor.dispatchTool now runs workflowValidator IMMEDIATELY when
     finalize_workflow_diagram returns successfully
   - If errors, injects them into the tool result via _validation field
     with explicit instruction "você DEVE corrigir antes de responder"
   - Model sees the errors INSIDE its iteration loop and can call
     update_workflow_action / delete_workflow_action to fix
   - Without this, errors only surfaced post-execute as a report — too
     late for self-correction

userId now propagated through executePhase to dispatchTool so the inline
hook can scope validation correctly.

title: feat(ai-orchestrator): Phase 2.4 — token budget tracker
body:
feat(ai-orchestrator): Phase 2.4 — token budget tracker

Replaces the hardcoded maxIterations cap as the primary execution control.
BudgetTracker accumulates input + output tokens across all provider iterations
and throws BudgetExceededError when total exceeds config.tokenBudget.perTurn.

Wired into executor.executeSingleShot via the onIterationComplete callback:
- After each iteration the LLM provider reports tokens used
- BudgetTracker.add() throws if consumed > limit
- Catch translates to ExecuteResult { stopReason: 'budget_exceeded' }
- isCancelled also returns true after budget exceeded so the loop exits cleanly

Why budget instead of iter cap:
- One iteration can be 10k tokens (large tool result) or 200 tokens (short text)
- Long-horizon plans may need 30+ iterations legitimately
- User-perceived cost is tokens, not iterations
- Provider-level maxIterations stays as a backstop (set to 25)

Default budgets (set by wrappers):
- AI Assistant: 50k tokens per turn
- AI Agent: 30k tokens per turn (configurable via Agent.executionBudgetMs)
- Builder UX (executeMultiTask): unlimited per turn (legacy behavior; tasks
  are themselves bounded). Phase 5 may add per-session budget.

User reported a consistent regression: AI Assistant kept inserting

   SEND_MESSAGE has order N and the action at order N+1 is RUN_AGENT or
   AI_HUB_AGENT.

time; validator catches it post-creation if the model still slips.

title: fix(ai-assistant): teach the model the right WorkflowActionType + recover from JSON-string config
body:
fix(ai-assistant): teach the model the right WorkflowActionType + recover from JSON-string config

Two correlated bugs that broke `add_workflow_action` for RUN_AGENT
(reproduced live in stg today building "Atendimento Restaurante Demo"):

1. Knowledge Base referenced `AI_AGENT` as the workflow action type for
   internal agents. That value does not exist in the `WorkflowActionType`
   enum — only `RUN_AGENT` (internal) and `AI_HUB_AGENT` (legacy external).
   The model learned the wrong value and burned 4–7 iterations sending it
   before falling back to `get_action_schema`. Updated:
   - entries/workflow-building-blocks.md
   - entries/common-patterns.md
   - entries/anti-patterns.md  (also added an explicit "do not use AI_AGENT" callout)
   - core-knowledge.contributor.ts (two entries + the "common errors" list)
   - root CLAUDE.md (Action Types section)

2. The model occasionally serializes `config` as a JSON string instead of
   an object literal (Anthropic tool calling does not enforce JSON Schema
   on the model side). Inside `add_workflow_action` we ran
   `fieldName in input.config`, which throws TypeError on a string operand
   and surfaced as the opaque "Cannot use 'in' operator..." error. Added
   a defensive `coerceConfigObject` helper that auto-parses JSON-string
   configs at the tool entry point; non-strings and unparseable strings
   pass through so the SDK / validator still produces a real error if the
   shape is genuinely wrong.

Coverage: 9 unit tests in tools-executor.config-coercion.spec.ts pin the
parser behavior (object pass-through, JSON string parse, malformed input
unchanged, primitives pass-through) plus one regression assertion that
the KB does not contain positive guidance like `actionType="AI_AGENT"`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ai-assistant): forward toolCalls/toolResults from orchestrator path

The orchestrator wrapper for /ai/chat (system-assistant-orchestrated.service)
hardcoded `toolCalls: []` and `toolResults: []` in the response with a comment
about callbacks — but for synchronous /ai/chat there are no callbacks, so the
structured tool data was silently lost.

Symptom (verified in stg):
- POST /ai/chat 'Use create_workflow para criar...' → workflow created in DB
  with real id, but response had toolCalls=[] toolResults=[]
- 8 e2e tests in tests/painel-cliente/ai-workflow-consistency.spec.ts failed
  on `expect(response.toolCalls).toBeTruthy()`
- Frontend AI Assistant tool feedback rendering broken (consumes toolCalls)

Fix: forward orchestrator's toolCalls/toolResults using the same pattern that
agents/services/agent-executor.service.ts already uses correctly (synthesize
positional `toolCallId: tc_${idx}` since OrchestrationToolResult lacks one).

Regression introduced in PR #271 (Phase 4.1 — AI Assistant chat migration).
PRs #272-#274 inherited unchanged. PR #273 fixed agents path correctly but
the assistant wrapper was not updated to match.

Coverage: 3 new unit tests pin the contract (forward toolCalls, forward
toolResults with synthesized id, empty arrays when no tools).

title: feat(wpp-business): encrypt WppBizAccount.accessToken at rest (Passagem 6)
body:
feat(wpp-business): encrypt WppBizAccount.accessToken at rest (Passagem 6)

Bug #1 (CRÍTICA): Meta WABA access token gravado em PLAINTEXT no DB
(prisma/schema.prisma:3834). appSecret já era encriptado, mas o token de
maior valor — full messaging permissions — ficava exposto.

Estratégia: encryption transparente no repo layer + backward-compat para
legacy plaintext rows + migration script idempotente. Services consumidores
(message, template, flow, media, webhook, analytics, campaign,
business-profile, account — 30+ pontos) não mudam: continuam vendo
plaintext porque a (de)cifragem acontece no boundary do repo.

Mudanças:

* utils/crypto.ts
  - Novo isEncryptedFormat(value): detecta o shape iv:authTag:ciphertext
    via 3 segmentos hex com tamanhos exatos (24/32/N). Não colide com
    Meta access tokens que começam com 'EAA' e não têm ':'.
  - Novo decryptSecretIfEncrypted(value): decripta se for o shape;
    senão devolve o valor inalterado. Usado pelas leituras do repo
    durante o rollout — legacy plaintext rows passam transparentes
    até a migration script rodar.

* repositories/account.repository.ts — wrap encrypt-on-write +
  decrypt-on-read em todos os métodos:
    - encryptCreateInput / encryptUpdateInput: encripta accessToken
      antes de mandar pro Prisma. Suporta tanto a forma primitive
      quanto { set: ... } do Prisma update input.
    - decryptAccount / decryptAccounts: aplica decryptSecretIfEncrypted
      em todo accessToken retornado.
    - Cobre create, findById, findByWabaId, findDeletedByWabaId,
      findByWabaIdGlobal, findMany, update, findByWebhookVerifyToken,
      softDelete.

* scripts/encrypt-wpp-biz-access-tokens.ts (novo) — migration one-shot
  idempotente:
    - Itera rows em batches (cursor por id, batchSize 100 default).
    - Para cada row, skip se isEncryptedFormat(accessToken)===true
      (já migrada) ou empty (segurança).
    - Re-encripta plaintext rows com encryptSecret(token).
    - --dry-run flag: conta o que mudaria sem escrever.
    - Erros por row são logados mas não abortam o batch (failed counter).
    - Exit code 1 se houver failures.
    - Operacional: rodar APÓS deploy do código de Passagem 6, ANTES de
      qualquer rotação de master key. Master key rotation é dance
      separado fora de escopo aqui.

Master key: WPP_BUSINESS_CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY em prod ainda é o
placeholder 5555… (memória credential_master_keys_placeholder). Esta
passagem coloca a infra; rotação no SOPS é follow-up separado.

Testes:
- crypto.test.ts: +12 testes para isEncryptedFormat (rounds-trip,
  Meta token rejeitado, separadores errados, lengths errados, non-hex)
  + decryptSecretIfEncrypted (decrypt happy path, plaintext passthrough,
  empty string).
- account.repository.test.ts: reescrito com seção 'at-rest encryption'
  cobrindo (1) encrypt on create, (2) encrypt on update primitive,
  (3) encrypt on update {set:...}, (4) update sem accessToken não toca,
  (5) decrypt on findById, (6) decrypt on findMany, (7) plaintext
  legacy passthrough, (8) null row passthrough. Plus regression suite
  CRUD inteira atualizada para shape encriptada.
- scripts/encrypt-wpp-biz-access-tokens.test.ts (novo): 5 testes

  TokenInvalidSignatureError, TokenInvalidError, TokenClaimInvalidError,
  TokenTypeMismatchError, MissingAuthorizationError. Top-level code
  permanece UNAUTHORIZED (não inflar enum); sub-tipo vai em details.code

  preserva o AppError original em vez de descartá-lo.

title: feat(wpp-business): typed Meta API errors + token validation
body:
feat(wpp-business): typed Meta API errors + token validation

Sintomas 1 & 2 tinham raiz comum: 401/403 da Meta virava InternalError genérico
(cloud-api.client.ts:642-647) e debugToken().scopes era capturado mas nunca
validado (account.service.ts:217,261). Painel só recebia 500 'Cloud API
request failed: ...' onde o usuário precisava ver 'reautentique-se' ou
'permissões insuficientes'.

Mudanças:

* providers/cloud-api/cloud-api-errors.ts (novo)
  - CloudApiError class carrega envelope da Meta (httpStatus, metaCode,
    metaSubcode, metaType, metaMessage, fbtrace_id) parseado de doRequest.
  - parseCloudApiError(response) extrai o JSON de erro da Meta tolerante
    a payloads não-JSON (fallback para texto raw).
  - appErrorFromCloudApi(error) mapeia para AppError tipado por
    code/subcode da Meta:
      * code 190 + subcode 463 → META_TOKEN_EXPIRED (401, UNAUTHORIZED)
      * code 190 + subcode 460/467/458 → META_TOKEN_REVOKED (401)
      * code 190 (sem subcode) → META_TOKEN_INVALID (401)
      * HTTP 401 (sem code 190) → META_TOKEN_INVALID
      * HTTP 403 / code 200 / code 10 → META_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE (403, FORBIDDEN)
      * HTTP 429 / codes 4,17,32,80004 → META_RATE_LIMIT (429, INTERNAL)
      * resto → META_API_ERROR (status original, INTERNAL — mantém retry semantics)
  - InsufficientScopeError + InvalidTokenError factories standalone para uso
    em validações pré-Graph (ver account.service abaixo).

* providers/cloud-api/cloud-api.client.ts
  - doRequest agora joga CloudApiError (via parseCloudApiError) em vez de
    'throw new Error'.
  - requestWithRetry mapeia CloudApiError via appErrorFromCloudApi; non-HTTP
    errors caem no path legado InternalError para preservar shape.
  - isRetryable agora bloqueia retry de META_RATE_LIMIT (top-level INTERNAL
    cairia no retry mas hammerar mais não ajuda — Meta diz para back off).

* services/account.service.ts
  - Novo helper validateDebugTokenInfo() chamado em resolveWppBizAppId() e
    createStandaloneDevice() logo após client.debugToken().
  - Valida info.isValid → InvalidTokenError; info.scopes inclui
    'whatsapp_business_management' → InsufficientScopeError.
  - Sintoma 2 (import device falha tarde): agora token sem scope correto
    falha imediato com erro estruturado (FORBIDDEN + META_INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE
    + presentScopes) antes de getPhoneNumberInfo retornar BAD_REQUEST opaco.

Testes:
- cloud-api.client.test.ts: 7 novos testes cobrindo cada branch do mapper
  (token expirado/revogado/inválido, scope insuficiente, rate limit HTTP
  429, rate limit por código 80004, fallback genérico INTERNAL, body
  não-JSON). 1 teste antigo atualizado (asserção INTERNAL → UNAUTHORIZED).
- account.service.test.ts: 4 novos testes (META_TOKEN_INVALID + scope
  insuficiente para create() e createStandaloneDevice()). Mocks existentes
  com scopes:[] atualizados para incluir whatsapp_business_management.

Total: 164 testes passando (1 falha pré-existente em 'appSecret encryption'
não relacionada a este change — confirmado via stash).

aegis/audit/beacon/marketing/platform schemas (DDL + indexes + FKs +
enum types).

audit_events is hand-patched to add PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)
since drizzle-kit doesn't model partitioning. Postgres requires a
plain sequence (not bigserial) on the partitioned parent, so 'seq'
is rewritten as bigint DEFAULT nextval(…). Two seed partitions are
created (2026-05, 2026-06) plus a DEFAULT partition catch-all so
writes outside the seeded range can never silently fail before the
rotation job catches up.

Subsequent monthly partitions are created by a future cron/pg_cron
job — see follow-up issue.

title: feat(builder-vm): add destroy.sh with strict confirmation gates
body:
feat(builder-vm): add destroy.sh with strict confirmation gates

Last-resort emergency lever. STOPS and DESTROYS the configured VMID. The
script is gated by FIVE independent confirmations:

  1. --i-know-what-im-doing flag must be passed (no flag => die)
  2. .env BUILDER_VMID must exist on this node (qm status check)
  3. The VM's name (qm config | grep name:) must equal BUILDER_HOSTNAME
     (mismatch => refuse — protects against typos pointing at unrelated VMs)
  4. The VM must contain /etc/developy/builder-vm.marker with the string
     'managed-by: scripts/bootstrap/builder-vm/provision.sh'. This is
     written by the cloud-init template, so only VMs created by this repo
     can pass. Bypassable only via BUILDER_SKIP_MARKER_CHECK=1 (with a
     loud warning).
  5. Interactive prompt: must type 'DESTROY <vmid>' verbatim.

Even with all gates passed, dry-run is still the default; --apply must be
explicit. The first thing the script prints (after arg parsing) is a
multi-line ASCII banner reminding the operator this is irreversible
without a PBS / ZFS snapshot.

Before destruction:
  - Lists qm listsnapshot output for the VMID
  - Lists PBS backups (best-effort via proxmox-backup-client or pvesm)

After qm destroy (with --purge --destroy-unreferenced-disks 1), it also
removes the cloud-init snippet file in /var/lib/vz/snippets — but ONLY the
one tagged with this VMID (never a wildcard).

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly.

title: feat(builder-vm): add provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)
body:
feat(builder-vm): add provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)

The end-to-end orchestrator. Default mode is --dry-run: every qm/ssh/scp
invocation is prefixed with WOULD: and never executed. --apply requires
typing APPLY at an interactive prompt.

Steps:
  1. Run preflight.sh (read-only validation)
  2. Confirm: type APPLY (anything else aborts)
  3. Render cloud-init.yaml.tpl with awk substitution into a mktemp file
  4. cp the rendered snippet to /var/lib/vz/snippets/builder-cloudinit-<vmid>.yaml
  5. qm create — minimal VM stub with virtio-scsi, serial console, agent on
  6. qm importdisk — bring the cloud template into BUILDER_STORAGE
  7. qm set — wire scsi0 + boot order + cloudinit drive + cicustom + ipconfig
  8. qm resize scsi0 to BUILDER_DISK_GB
  9. qm start
 10. Wait up to BUILDER_SSH_TIMEOUT for qemu-guest-agent to expose an IP,
     then up to 60s for SSH (deploy-bot key-based)
 11. SCP + run zfs-datasets.sh inside the VM
 12. SCP + run install-tooling.sh inside the VM
 13. Run validate.sh from the operator host
 14. Print success summary + IP + concrete next steps

On failure: NEVER auto-destroys the VM. Prints the error, leaves the VM
running for inspection, and exits non-zero. Operator decides whether to
keep, fix, or destroy (via destroy.sh).

Logging: in --apply mode, all stdout/stderr is tee'd to
builder-vm-provision-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSZ.log in cwd via re-exec.

The script does NOT call the Proxmox HTTP API — it relies on local qm
(and so must run on the Proxmox node). This is the safest path for a
bootstrap that should never be executed by an automation it doesn't fully
trust.

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly. Dry-run output captured in PR description.

body:
feat(db/audit): add Herald schema (events, partitioned by month)

Adds the Herald audit log as an append-only, monthly-partitioned table.

Drizzle definition (audit_events):
  seq          bigserial
  tenant_id    text (NULL = platform-wide)
  source       varchar(32) — module producing the event
  type         varchar(96) — 'iam.role.granted', 'forge.vm.start', …
  severity     enum info/notice/warn/error/critical
  actor        jsonb  — { id, kind, ip, user_agent, … }
  resource     jsonb  — { kind, id, name, parent, … }
  action       varchar(32)
  outcome      enum allow/deny/success/failure/conditional
  before       jsonb (nullable)
  after        jsonb (nullable)
  context      jsonb — request_id, trace_id, …
  created_at   timestamptz — partition key

Composite PK (seq, created_at) so the table can be declared
PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at) — Postgres requires the partition
key to be part of the PK on partitioned tables. The PARTITION BY
clause + first monthly partition are stitched into the generated
migration in the next commit (drizzle-kit doesn't model partitioning
natively).

Indexes target audit-explorer query shapes: by tenant+time, by type+time,
by source+time, by outcome+time. All include created_at as the second
column so they live happily inside per-partition btrees post-migration.

channel. Today notifyReload defaults to a no-op; PowerDNS will pick up
writes at the next query subject to its in-process record cache (60s

title: fix(devices-bundle): hotfix CORS — Cache-Control no response, not request
body:
fix(devices-bundle): hotfix CORS — Cache-Control no response, not request

Production smoke caught it: clicking "Exportar bundle" surfaces
"Network Error" with no HTTP status. Root cause: the frontend was
sending `Cache-Control: no-store` on the *request*, which is not in
CORS-safelisted request-headers (Accept, Accept-Language,
Content-Language, Content-Type) and so triggers a preflight OPTIONS.
The API's `enableCors({ allowedHeaders: [Content-Type, Authorization,
X-Requested-With, Accept, X-API-Key] })` doesn't list `Cache-Control`,
so the preflight is rejected and the browser blocks the POST entirely.
Axios sees no response and surfaces a generic "Network Error".

The intent of `no-store` was always to keep the plaintext payload
(carrying Meta accessToken + App Secret in the milliseconds between
server fetch and client-side encrypt) off intermediaries and disk
caches. That belongs on the *response*, not the request.

- painel-cliente: drop the `Cache-Control` header from
  exportBundleSingle + exportBundleMany requests.
- painel-cliente-api: add `@Header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')` and
  `@Header('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff')` to all three bundle
  endpoints (single export, many export, import).

Build verified: vite + tsc -p tsconfig.build.json both green.

title: fix(painel-cliente): explicit Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> for WebCrypto
body:
fix(painel-cliente): explicit Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> for WebCrypto

TS 5.7+ tightened BufferSource to require Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> (not
the more general <ArrayBufferLike> which would allow SharedArrayBuffer).
The decrypt site choked on `iv` + `ciphertext` from fromBase64 because
their inferred generic was ArrayBufferLike.

Fix: declare fromBase64 return as Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> with a single
cast at the construction site (length-overload of Uint8Array creates an
ArrayBuffer-backed view); widen deriveKey's salt param to BufferSource
since that's what crypto.subtle.deriveKey actually wants.

Verified end-to-end via tsx roundtrip: encrypt → decrypt(correct) →
equal payload, decrypt(wrong) → BundleAuthTagError. Vite build green.

because the bundle was shipping `device.bbDeviceId` (BB-internal UUID

body:
feat(beacon): add beaconMetaAdapter (maps BeaconStoreData → drizzle ops)

Implements PostgresBackendAdapter<BeaconStoreData> for the StoreBackend
SPI. Only handles the collections beacon_meta owns:

  - clusters → beacon_meta_clusters  (full CRUD via drizzle)
  - nodes    → beacon_meta_nodes     (full CRUD via drizzle, FK CASCADE
                                       from cluster deletion)

Zones and records are intentionally no-ops here — they live in

don't have to special-case anything.

so future schema drift surfaces as a type error at compile time. The
adapter is constructed lazily — getDb() is only called once
STORE_BACKEND=postgres routes here.

body:
feat(atlas): adopt StoreBackend SPI + postgres adapter (Wave 2 Tier 3)

Migrates the Atlas meta store (.atlas-store.json) from encrypted JSON to
Postgres behind the StoreBackend SPI. Mirrors Beacon (PR #21), Aegis
(PR #24), Marketing (PR #23) shape — same lazy-singleton, env-flip
toggle, zero-regression JSON-mode default.

Schema (apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/atlas.ts):
- atlas_clusters            text PK, jsonb lxc_ids/tags, pgEnum
                            engine/size/status/ha_mode
- atlas_credentials         text PK, FK cluster_id ON DELETE CASCADE,
                            partial-index-friendly composite on
                            (cluster_id, revoked_at)
- atlas_idempotency_records request_id PK, 24h TTL (enforced at app),
                            indexes on expires_at + resource_id

Migration (0004_create_atlas_meta_tables.sql):
- All CREATE TABLE — no ALTER on incoming-FK columns, so the FK
  ordering bug from PR #27 doesn't apply.
- Hand-written via pnpm db:new (new workflow, not drizzle-kit generate).

Adapter (apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/postgres-adapter.ts):
- Lossless row↔domain mapping for all three collections.
- replaceAll uses a transaction; child-table deletes happen first to
  match the marketing/beacon pattern.
- upsertOne handles `idempotencyRecords` by routing the SPI id to
  request_id (the natural PK for that collection).

Store rewrite (apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/store.ts):
- Thin wrappers over backend.load/saveEntity/deleteEntity.
- Custom getItemId understands both `id` (clusters/credentials) and
  `requestId` (idempotency) for JSON-mode saveEntity.
- saveIdempotencyRecord preserves the expired-record sweep at the
  store layer so both backends behave identically.
- deleteCluster manually cascades credentials in JSON mode; Postgres
  mode also has FK CASCADE as defence-in-depth.
- revokeCredential reads → mutates → saveEntity (avoids partial
  upsert losing other columns).

Migrate-stores mapper (scripts/migrate-stores/modules/atlas.ts):
- Three collections mapped with conflictTargets for idempotent re-runs.
- `lxcIds`/`tags` jsonb columns serialized via JSON.stringify and
  parsed back through a tolerant helper that accepts both string and
  array shapes (drizzle returns objects, MemoryDriver compares strings).
- IdempotencyRecord aliases requestId as non-enumerable request_id so
  the runner's dedupe step sees a unique key without polluting the
  recovered JSON shape (same trick audit uses for external_id).

Tests added: 23 (8 mapper round-trip + 15 store regression).
- Mapper test covers row count parity, optional-field handling, jsonb
  array round-trip, idempotency, empty-store edge case.
- Store regression test covers JSON-mode CRUD + filter + cascade +
  revokeCredential + saveIdempotencyRecord sweep + env-flip routing.

Also updated tests/atlas/01-store.integration.test.ts to call
resetAtlasStoreBackendForTesting() around its ATLAS_STORE_PATH env
swaps — required because the lazy singleton caches the resolved path
on first call.

Append-only entry in scripts/migrate-stores/modules/index.ts; does
not touch any sibling _meta module (spark/tide/nexus/flux/mesh own
their own migrations).

Typecheck clean except the 3 pre-existing ignite test errors.

feat(migrate-stores): runner state machine + types + drivers

Adds the orchestrator that walks a ModuleMigrator's collections,
applies toRow/fromRow, and pushes rows through a PostgresDriver
interface. The runner is module-agnostic — all schema knowledge lives
in the mappers under modules/.

Drivers:

    (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2 salt matches @proxmox-manager/core byte-for-byte)
  - MemoryDriver: in-memory test fake with ON CONFLICT semantics
  - PostgresJsDriver: postgres-js-backed prod driver; lazy-imports
    the `postgres` package so the CLI loads cleanly in workspaces
    that don't depend on apps/web

Direction-aware behaviour:
  - json-to-postgres: read JSON, map, insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  - postgres-to-json: read tables, map back, merge into the existing
    JSON store (de-dup on conflict targets so it stays idempotent)

Dry-run path is fully exercised — reads source, runs every mapper,
logs counts + sample row — but skips destination mutation AND
checkpoint persistence so a dry-run never poisons a follow-up apply.

title: fix(wave2): post-cutover fixes — root postgres dep + 0003 FK ordering
body:
fix(wave2): post-cutover fixes — root postgres dep + 0003 FK ordering

Two issues discovered during 2026-05-11 prod cutover:

## 1. `postgres` package missing from root deps
`scripts/migrate-stores/drivers/postgres-driver.ts` lazy-imports `postgres`
but the package was only declared in `apps/web/package.json`. The CLI runs
from repo root via `bun scripts/migrate-stores/index.ts` and Bun's resolver
couldn't find the package there. Beacon cutover apparently worked because a
prior install left a stale copy. Fix: declare `postgres@^3.4.9` as a root
dependency so frozen-lockfile deploys keep it.

## 2. Migration 0003 ALTER COLUMN order incompatible with real Postgres
The aegis follow-up agent's drizzle-kit-generated 0003 alters columns in
declaration order. Postgres rejects `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE` on a
column that has an FK to a column whose type would mismatch — the alter
must drop the FK first. pg-mem in tests doesn't enforce this so the
agent's tests passed.

This caused 0003 to partially apply on prod (some text alters succeeded,
others failed mid-file, FK adds at end failed too). Prod was manually
repaired via explicit DDL (drop 7 FKs → alter all uuid→text → re-add FKs)
and 0003 was marked applied with hash `2b4a36ed1e043...`.

Fix: rewrite 0003_minor_saracen.sql to drop all referencing FKs first,
alter both sides of each relation, then re-ADD the FKs. Same end state,
order-of-operations correct for real Postgres.

* feat(ship): orchestrator state machine, phases, target compositions

Adds the deploy state machine and per-phase logic.

Phases (scripts/ship/phases/):
  - preflight    git clean/branch/pushed; Aegis policy stub
  - build        SSH builder VM: git checkout, pnpm install/build/test,
                 docker buildx + push, trivy scan; skipped if --image given
  - migrate      mgmt API dry-run + apply; renders schema diff to log;
                 self-skips for marketing/beacon
  - deploy       three flavors picked by strategy:
                   rolling   — single startDeploy via mgmt API
                   canary:N  — deploy cohort, verify, then promote to 100
                   blue-green— mgmt API does the swap atomically
                 every variant snapshots previousSha for rollback
  - verify       Pulse baseline check (error_rate < +2pp, p95 < 1.5x)
  - finalize     tag :env-current, Herald success event, Discord webhook
  - rollback     restores previousSha via mgmt API + Herald high event

Orchestrator (ship.ts):
  - composes phases per target + strategy
  - persists DeployJob to deploy log after each phase (atomic rename)
  - honors --skip and per-phase shouldRun()
  - auto-rollback when deploy/verify/finalize fail (unless --no-rollback)
                 — preflight/build failures don't trigger rollback (no
                 production impact yet)
  - explicit subcommand: 'bun ship rollback <env> <target> --to=<sha>|
    --previous' walks the deploy log for --previous

Target compositions (targets/):
  web, marketing, atlas, spark, tide, beacon — each defines its phase
  list. 'all' is a topo-ordered list fanned out by index.ts (one
  DeployJob per target, abort on first failure).

State (state/deploy-log.ts):
  Persists ~/.developy/deploys/<id>.json (or tmpdir in tests via
  createDeployLogStore(dir)). Atomic write via tmp + rename.

Entrypoint (index.ts):
  Bun shebang, import.meta.main guard, mock drivers by default.
  DEVELOPY_REAL_INFRA_ENABLED=1 currently throws — real impls are next PR.

deps stage:

  - mounts a BuildKit cache at /root/.local/share/pnpm/store so the pnpm

    "localhost" via IPv6 first, but Next binds to 0.0.0.0 IPv4 only;
    using the literal IP avoids a dual-stack mismatch)

  - runcmd: enable docker, add deploy-bot to docker group, install pnpm
    via corepack, install bun for deploy-bot user, install trivy via the
    official apt repo (non-fatal — install-tooling.sh retries)

Final-message points the operator at the next steps (zfs-datasets.sh,
install-tooling.sh, validate.sh).

Passes yamllint with sane rules.

* feat(builder-vm): add ZFS datasets setup script

Creates the per-cache hierarchy under rpool/build:

  rpool/build              -> /data/build (parent, compression=zstd, atime=off)
  rpool/build/turbo        -> /data/build/turbo
  rpool/build/buildx       -> /data/build/buildx
  rpool/build/pnpm         -> /data/build/pnpm

Each dataset is owned by deploy-bot:deploy-bot, mode 0755. The script is
fully idempotent: every dataset creation is gated on `zfs list`, every
dir-prep step is mkdir -p / chown / chmod (all of which are idempotent).

Refuses to touch a non-existent zpool unless in dry-run (so syntax checks
pass on operator laptops without ZFS). Dry-run is default — pass --apply.

via --user. Both default to rpool / deploy-bot.

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly.

* feat(builder-vm): add tooling install script (docker/buildx/pnpm/bun)

Runs INSIDE the VM (post-cloud-init) as deploy-bot. Complements cloud-init
with the steps that need to happen after ZFS datasets exist:

  1. corepack enable + activate latest pnpm (idempotent)
  2. docker buildx create --name developy-builder --driver docker-container
     (skipped if it already exists)
  3. docker login $REGISTRY_URL (skipped if REGISTRY_PASSWORD is unset or
     left at the placeholder value)
  4. git clone --bare $BUILDER_GIT_REMOTE → /data/build/git/...git
     (or git fetch --all --prune if the bare repo already exists)
  5. Print version table for: docker, buildx, pnpm, bun, trivy, git, age,
     sops — useful as a sanity check from the operator's terminal

Defaults to --dry-run; --apply executes. Re-runnable: each step checks
state before mutating.

Note: rotating REGISTRY credentials does NOT remove old auths from
~/.docker/config.json — that's intentional (the script never deletes
state it didn't create in this run).

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(builder-vm): add validate.sh post-provision sanity check

Runs from the OPERATOR host. SSHes into the builder as deploy-bot and runs
a series of checks; emits one JSON object per check on stdout, then a
summary object. Non-zero exit if any check fails.

Checks:
  ssh         — `ssh deploy-bot@host echo ok` succeeds
  cloud-init  — /var/lib/developy/cloudinit-done marker exists (= cloud-init
                runcmd phase finished)
  docker      — docker run --rm hello-world succeeds
  buildx      — docker buildx ls includes 'developy-builder'
  zfs         — /data/build/{turbo,buildx,pnpm,git} are mountpoints
  registry    — ~/.docker/config.json has an auths entry for REGISTRY_URL
  bun         — bun --version returns a semver

Each check emits {"check":"name","ok":true|false,"detail":"..."}
with shell-escaped detail. Final summary: passed/failed/total.

Default mode is --dry-run (prints WOULD-SSH lines, marks every check as
trivially ok). --apply actually SSHes.

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(builder-vm): add provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)

The end-to-end orchestrator. Default mode is --dry-run: every qm/ssh/scp
invocation is prefixed with WOULD: and never executed. --apply requires
typing APPLY at an interactive prompt.

Steps:
  1. Run preflight.sh (read-only validation)
  2. Confirm: type APPLY (anything else aborts)
  3. Render cloud-init.yaml.tpl with awk substitution into a mktemp file
  4. cp the rendered snippet to /var/lib/vz/snippets/builder-cloudinit-<vmid>.yaml
  5. qm create — minimal VM stub with virtio-scsi, serial console, agent on
  6. qm importdisk — bring the cloud template into BUILDER_STORAGE
  7. qm set — wire scsi0 + boot order + cloudinit drive + cicustom + ipconfig
  8. qm resize scsi0 to BUILDER_DISK_GB
  9. qm start
 10. Wait up to BUILDER_SSH_TIMEOUT for qemu-guest-agent to expose an IP,
     then up to 60s for SSH (deploy-bot key-based)
 11. SCP + run zfs-datasets.sh inside the VM
 12. SCP + run install-tooling.sh inside the VM
 13. Run validate.sh from the operator host
 14. Print success summary + IP + concrete next steps

On failure: NEVER auto-destroys the VM. Prints the error, leaves the VM
running for inspection, and exits non-zero. Operator decides whether to
keep, fix, or destroy (via destroy.sh).

Logging: in --apply mode, all stdout/stderr is tee'd to
builder-vm-provision-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSZ.log in cwd via re-exec.

The script does NOT call the Proxmox HTTP API — it relies on local qm
(and so must run on the Proxmox node). This is the safest path for a
bootstrap that should never be executed by an automation it doesn't fully
trust.

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly. Dry-run output captured in PR description.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(builder-vm): add destroy.sh with strict confirmation gates

Last-resort emergency lever. STOPS and DESTROYS the configured VMID. The
script is gated by FIVE independent confirmations:

  1. --i-know-what-im-doing flag must be passed (no flag => die)
  2. .env BUILDER_VMID must exist on this node (qm status check)
  3. The VM's name (qm config | grep name:) must equal BUILDER_HOSTNAME
     (mismatch => refuse — protects against typos pointing at unrelated VMs)
  4. The VM must contain /etc/developy/builder-vm.marker with the string
     'managed-by: scripts/bootstrap/builder-vm/provision.sh'. This is
     written by the cloud-init template, so only VMs created by this repo
     can pass. Bypassable only via BUILDER_SKIP_MARKER_CHECK=1 (with a
     loud warning).
  5. Interactive prompt: must type 'DESTROY <vmid>' verbatim.

Even with all gates passed, dry-run is still the default; --apply must be
explicit. The first thing the script prints (after arg parsing) is a
multi-line ASCII banner reminding the operator this is irreversible
without a PBS / ZFS snapshot.

Before destruction:
  - Lists qm listsnapshot output for the VMID
  - Lists PBS backups (best-effort via proxmox-backup-client or pvesm)

After qm destroy (with --purge --destroy-unreferenced-disks 1), it also
removes the cloud-init snippet file in /var/lib/vz/snippets — but ONLY the
one tagged with this VMID (never a wildcard).

Passes shellcheck -x cleanly.

feat(migrate-stores): JSON↔Postgres migration CLI + Beacon mapper (Wave 2 Fase 3) (#20)

* feat(migrate-stores): CLI parser and entry point

Sets up scripts/migrate-stores/ with the Bun entrypoint, arg parser,
and tiny structured logger. Mirrors scripts/ship/ in shape — own
parseArgs (no yargs/commander), TTY-aware coloured output, silent
logger for tests.

CLI surface:
  bun migrate:stores --module=<m> --from=<json|postgres>
                     --to=<json|postgres> [flags]

Flags: --dry-run (default), --apply, --limit=N, --state-file,
--work-dir, --help. Validates that --from differs from --to and that
--apply isn't accidentally combined with --dry-run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(migrate-stores): runner state machine + types + drivers

Adds the orchestrator that walks a ModuleMigrator's collections,
applies toRow/fromRow, and pushes rows through a PostgresDriver
interface. The runner is module-agnostic — all schema knowledge lives
in the mappers under modules/.

Drivers:
  - JsonSource: reads/writes the encrypted .{m}-store.json file
    (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2 salt matches @proxmox-manager/core byte-for-byte)
  - MemoryDriver: in-memory test fake with ON CONFLICT semantics
  - PostgresJsDriver: postgres-js-backed prod driver; lazy-imports
    the `postgres` package so the CLI loads cleanly in workspaces
    that don't depend on apps/web

Direction-aware behaviour:
  - json-to-postgres: read JSON, map, insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  - postgres-to-json: read tables, map back, merge into the existing
    JSON store (de-dup on conflict targets so it stays idempotent)

Dry-run path is fully exercised — reads source, runs every mapper,
logs counts + sample row — but skips destination mutation AND
checkpoint persistence so a dry-run never poisons a follow-up apply.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(migrate-stores): checkpoint persistence

Per-module run state lives under ~/.developy/migrations/<m>.json so a
failed migration can resume from where it left off (the runner skips
collections marked `completed` on the second pass).

Schema is versioned (`version: 1`) so future changes don't trip
existing checkpoints. Writes are atomic — write to <path>.tmp, then
rename — surviving a crash mid-write. The runner gates checkpoint
saves through a `persistCheckpoint()` wrapper that's a no-op in
dry-run mode (a dry-run then an apply on the same --state-file works
as expected: apply still does the real work).

title: fix(hooks): inject Bearer auth header in 20 client hooks (#14)
body:
fix(hooks): inject Bearer auth header in 20 client hooks (#14)

* fix(beacon): inject Bearer auth header in apiFetch

The Beacon GET routes call requireSession() (unlike Nexus/Atlas which
don't), so the client must send the Authorization: Bearer <token> header.

The apiFetch helper was only sending Content-Type, causing all Beacon
client queries to fail silently with 401 — manifesting as empty cluster
and zone lists in the dashboard even though the underlying store had
data.

Other modules (use-ignite, use-iam, use-aegis, etc) likely have the
same bug — separate audit PR forthcoming.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(hooks): inject Bearer auth header across all API helpers

Same root cause as previous Beacon fix: client hooks were not sending
the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Endpoints that call
requireSession() on the server (beacon, ignite, iam, mesh, etc) were
returning 401 silently, manifesting as empty dashboards.

Patched 19 hooks: aegis-settings, atlas, audit, blaze, connections,
flux, herald, ignite, memberships, mesh, nexus, organizations,
projects, pulse, radar, reconciliation, spark, teams, tide.

(use-beacon already patched in previous commit.)

This is the cause of the 'Beacon shows 0 clusters', 'Mesh shows nothing',
'Ignite not working' user reports.

A more permanent fix is to introduce a shared lib/api-fetch.ts helper
that all hooks consume. Deferred to a refactor PR — this patch is
mechanical and minimal.

feat(beacon): PowerDNS backend + zones/records read through backend (#15)

* feat(beacon): define DnsBackend interface and shared types

Add the abstraction Beacon will use to talk to DNS providers (DigitalOcean,
PowerDNS, or in-memory mocks). Establishes Zod schemas for record/domain
shapes, a typed DnsBackendError, and the capability matrix surfaced by
backends. Documents the idempotency contract that callers can rely on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): add mock backend for tests

In-memory DnsBackend implementation that honours the full contract: SOA
serial bumping, idempotent createRecord, TSIG storage, capability flags.
Used as the default backend when nothing else is configured in dev/test
(see factory.ts) and as the contract baseline that the SQL- and CLI-
backed implementations are validated against.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(beacon): migrate DigitalOcean logic to backend implementation

Move the doctl-based DNS code out of doctl-client.ts and into a proper
DnsBackend implementation. Adds idempotent createDomain/createRecord,
healthCheck via 'doctl account get', and an injectable executor so tests
can replay canned doctl JSON without spawning the binary.

Capability flags reflect what doctl actually exposes — DigitalOcean does
not surface DNSSEC or TSIG via the CLI, so those are false here.

doctl-client.ts is intentionally left in place for now; subsequent commits
will turn it into a deprecation shim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): add PowerDNS backend implementation (Postgres-backed)

Implements DnsBackend by writing directly to PowerDNS' gpgsql tables —
the same schema PowerDNS reads on every query (see schema.pgsql.sql).
Creates an SOA record automatically on createDomain so PowerDNS treats
the zone as authoritative; bumps notified_serial + the SOA record
serial on every mutation so secondaries notice the change.

Surfaces DNSSEC and TSIG capabilities (cryptokeys / tsigkeys tables
read+write) and supports a notifyReload hook for plugging in an
out-of-band 'pdns_control reload <zone>' once we have an SSH/HTTP
channel. Today notifyReload defaults to a no-op; PowerDNS will pick up
writes at the next query subject to its in-process record cache (60s
default).

The pg driver is injected via an SqlPool interface so tests can use a
hand-rolled mock without pulling pg-mem in as a dependency.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): backend factory with env-based selection

Add getDnsBackend() / selectBackendId() / resetDnsBackend(). Selection
priority documented at the top of factory.ts: explicit BEACON_BACKEND
beats inferred-from-env, which prefers PowerDNS when DATABASE_URL is set
and falls back to DigitalOcean when only the doctl token is present.
Production must configure something explicitly — no silent mock fallback.

The factory caches per-process; tests can call resetDnsBackend() or
setDnsBackend(stub) to swap implementations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(beacon): contract tests for all backends + smoke

Three test layers:
- interface.test.ts: contract suite that runs the same scenarios against
  Mock, PowerDNS (with fake pg pool), and DigitalOcean (with fake doctl).
  Covers idempotent create, update keeps id, delete is no-op on missing,
  list filters, capability-flag presence, TSIG roundtrip where supported.
- powerdns-backend.test.ts: SQL-shape regression tests — auto SOA insertion,
  NS seeding, serial bumping, disabled flag, notifyReload hook firing.
- digitalocean-backend.test.ts: doctl arg shape, idempotency on
  (name, type, content), token-leak guard.
- factory.test.ts: env-based selection rules + cache behavior.

Adjusts two backend behaviours so contract tests pass uniformly across
all three implementations:
- DigitalOceanDnsBackend.listRecords swallows not_found and returns [],
  matching Mock and PowerDNS contracts.
- PowerDNS buildPgPool wraps pg.Pool.query with a properly typed adapter.

Helpers (helpers/sql-fake.ts, helpers/doctl-fake.ts) are intentionally
narrow — they recognise only the SQL/CLI shapes the backends emit. Adding
a new query in the backend requires extending the fake.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(beacon): orchestrator uses DnsBackend interface

Move the NS-record management away from a hard-wired PowerDNS REST client
onto the new DnsBackend abstraction. The orchestrator and provisioner now
import from ./backends/ns-helpers, which routes through getDnsBackend()
— so PowerDNS, DigitalOcean, and the mock backend are all interchangeable
without code changes elsewhere.

The legacy pdns-client.ts is reduced to a deprecation shim that
re-exports from ns-helpers; the obsolete resolvePdnsIp() now returns ""
since the configured backend handles transport.

Cluster lifecycle stays in the in-memory store (BeaconCluster) — the
backend is only consulted for the DNS write side. Herald events are
preserved verbatim.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(beacon): deprecate doctl-client.ts (re-export shim)

Reduce doctl-client.ts to a thin shim that delegates to the new
DigitalOceanDnsBackend. The exported surface (listDomainRecords,
createDomainRecord, updateDomainRecord, deleteDomainRecord, setNsRecord,
removeNsRecord) is preserved 1:1 so any out-of-tree consumer keeps
compiling. Each export carries a @deprecated tag pointing at the
DnsBackend abstraction or ./backends/ns-helpers.

The file will be removed after the next release cycle once external
imports are migrated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(beacon): README with backend selection and migration guide

Document the DnsBackend abstraction:
- Capability matrix per backend (DNSSEC / TSIG support).
- Env-var selection rules with priority order.
- Trade-offs between PowerDNS, DigitalOcean, and the mock backend.
- Step-by-step zero-downtime migration from DigitalOcean to PowerDNS.
- Let's Encrypt DNS-01 + TSIG flow for wildcard certs.
- How to add a new backend (implement contract, register, add test cases).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(beacon): listZones/listRecords delegate to DnsBackend

When BEACON_BACKEND=powerdns (or BEACON_DATABASE_URL is set), the
store-level reads (listZones, getZone, getZoneByFqdn, listRecords)
delegate to the configured DnsBackend instead of the local JSON.

Eliminates drift between PowerDNS reality and the painel for zones
and records (e.g. catalisa.app served by PowerDNS but missing from
the JSON snapshot; records created via pdnsutil that never round-tripped

Cluster/node metadata still lives in JSON — backends don't model that.

feat(db): StoreBackend SPI + Beacon as reference implementation (#21)

* feat(db/schema): add beacon_meta tables (clusters, nodes, settings)

Append three tables to schema/beacon.ts for Beacon's platform metadata:

- beacon_meta_clusters — BeaconCluster (cluster topology, HA mode, size,

beacon_node_status) mirror the corresponding unions in
@sidefuel/platform/beacon and data-products/types — kept in sync by
