feat(atlas-mgmt): destroy.sh with 5-gate confirmation

Last-resort emergency lever. Mirrors builder-vm/destroy.sh's posture
and extends it to LXC (pct instead of qm).

Five gates — ALL must pass:
  Gate 1  --i-know-what-im-doing flag is passed
  Gate 2  pct status $ATLAS_MGMT_VMID exists on this node
  Gate 3  pct config $ATLAS_MGMT_VMID hostname == .env ATLAS_MGMT_HOSTNAME

the marker, then stops it again before destroy. This prevents the
"VM was stopped, marker check skipped" footgun while still being
non-destructive.

                                   (logged as WARN; never silent)
  ATLAS_MGMT_NONINTERACTIVE=1      skips Gate 5 typed-confirm
                                   (intended for controlled CI-like reruns,
                                   never for casual destroys)

cloud-init snippet from /var/lib/vz/snippets after pct destroy succeeds.

Wraps the legacy readStore/writeStore pattern behind the StoreBackend
interface. Behaviour is bit-equivalent to what each module had inline:

title: fix(provisioner): centralize vmidToIp + reserved-IP guard (prevents collisions like 2026-05-11 outage)
body:
fix(provisioner): centralize vmidToIp + reserved-IP guard (prevents collisions like 2026-05-11 outage)

## Why

On 2026-05-11 around 21:15, the dashboard hung on 'Loading organizations...'.
Root cause: a Herald lifecycle test instance had been provisioned as Proxmox
VMID 151 and assigned IP 172.10.0.151 — the same IP as atlas-mgmt-01 (LXC
9101, the management postgres). ARP races silently routed half of the app's
postgres queries to the Herald container, which obviously had nothing on
5432. Connections timed out, app couldn't read aegis_orgs, UI stuck.

The local fix was `pct stop 151` + bridge fdb flush. The structural fix is
this PR.

## What was wrong

Every data-product provisioner (atlas, beacon, blaze, flux, herald, ignite,
nexus, spark, tide — nine files) had its own copy of:

    function vmidToIp(vmid: number): string {
      ...
      parts[3] = String(vmid % 256);
      ...
    }

Two structural failures:

1. **Manual management LXCs were given IPs from inside the provisioner range.**
   atlas-mgmt-01 was provisioned with IP 172.10.0.151 by hand; developy-quickstart
   with 172.10.0.150. Both .150 and .151 are valid outputs of `vmid % 256` for
   common VMIDs (150, 151, 406, 407, …). Collision was inevitable.

2. **No reservation mechanism.** Even if we wanted to keep the management IPs
   out of the provisioner range, there was no single place to declare them.

## Fix

- Move `vmidToIp` to a single canonical implementation in
  `data-products/provisioner-base.ts`. Re-implementations in all nine
  provisioner files deleted; each imports the shared one.
- Add a configurable reserved-octet set. Defaults reflect prod state on
  2026-05-11:
    10, 11  — PVE host vmbr1 interfaces
    103     — pg-beacon-default
    127     — pdns-ns1
    150     — developy-quickstart (manual mgmt LXC)
    151     — atlas-mgmt-01 (manual mgmt LXC)
  Overridable via `DATA_PRODUCTS_RESERVED_IPS` env (comma-separated).
- When `vmid % 256` lands on a reserved octet, walk forward to the next free
  one. Loop bound 256 — never hangs.
- Env is re-read on each call so operators can rotate the reserved list at
  runtime.

## What this still does NOT fix (follow-up)

VMIDs that differ by 256 still collide (VMID 200 and VMID 456 both → .200).
The real fix is an explicit IPAM allocation table; the mesh module already
has `ipam-engine.ts` we can reuse. Tracked as a follow-up.

## Tests

- 11 new vitest cases in `provisioner-base.test.ts` covering: dhcp fallback,
  non-reserved mapping, mask preservation, the exact VMID-151 regression that
  caused the outage, env override, default reserved set, and wrap-around
  bound.
- Typecheck clean (pre-existing `tests/ignite/03,04-*` errors are on
  origin/main, unrelated).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(db): plain SQL migration runner + new pnpm scripts (drizzle-kit becomes optional)
body:
feat(db): plain SQL migration runner + new pnpm scripts (drizzle-kit becomes optional)

Replaces `drizzle-kit migrate` with a tiny custom runner at
`scripts/db-migrate/`. drizzle-orm itself stays — it's the query builder
used by all the postgres adapters. Only the migration tooling changes.

## Why

Two pain points hit us during 2026-05-11 Wave 2 cutover:

1. drizzle-kit auto-generated migrations with FK ordering bugs (pg-mem
   in tests accepted them; real Postgres rejected). PR #27 fixed the
   immediate breakage and documented the rule. Going forward, all
   migrations are hand-written and reviewed; the runner has no
   auto-generation step that could repeat the bug.

2. drizzle-kit's snapshot + hash + journal made post-deploy fixes
   complex. Modifying an applied migration meant updating
   `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations.hash` on every deployed DB. This
   runner uses filename tracking only — no snapshot, no hash drama.

## What

- `scripts/db-migrate/runner.ts` — < 150 LOC, lex-orders SQL files,
  tracks in `__migrations(filename PK, applied_at)`, each migration
  in its own transaction

feat(atlas-mgmt): init-db.sh — per-module schemas + grants

Idempotent SQL setup. Runs INSIDE the LXC via pct exec (pushed by
provision.sh) or locally for dry-run review.

Creates 15 schemas, one per module that ends up writing to mgmt-db:
  aegis, audit, beacon_meta, platform, mesh, atlas_meta, spark_meta,
  tide_meta, nexus_meta, flux_meta, blaze_meta, ignite_meta, herald,
  marketing, convoy_meta

  GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA <m> TO app_runtime
  GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA <m> TO app_runtime
  GRANT USAGE,SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA <m> TO app_runtime
  ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE developy_mgmt IN SCHEMA <m>
    GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE ON TABLES TO app_runtime
  ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE developy_mgmt IN SCHEMA <m>
    GRANT USAGE,SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO app_runtime

Plus:
  REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC
  GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO app_runtime
  CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto  (drizzle needs gen_random_uuid)

Safe to re-run as many times as needed. Re-running after drizzle creates
new tables grants the new objects to app_runtime — that's a feature.

title: feat(atlas-mgmt): provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)
body:
feat(atlas-mgmt): provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)

Main entry point. Default mode is --dry-run; --apply requires an
interactive APPLY token. Runs on the Proxmox node and uses pct/pvesm
locally — never calls the Proxmox HTTP API.

Flow (--apply):
   1. preflight.sh                                          (read-only)
   2. confirm_or_die "APPLY"                                (interactive)
   3. Render cloud-init.yaml.tpl via awk to /tmp            (PG creds inlined)
   4. Upload as snippet to ATLAS_MGMT_SNIPPETS_STORAGE      (audit artifact)
   5. pct create  --unprivileged --features=nesting=0       (LXC, not VM)
   6. pct set --tags 'developy;managed-by-bootstrap-script;atlas-mgmt'
   7. pct start
   8. Wait up to ATLAS_MGMT_SSH_TIMEOUT for SSH
   9. pct push  init-db.sh + install-tooling.sh + lib + inner .env
  10. Write /etc/developy/lxc.marker  (destroy.sh Gate 4 anchor)
  11. Phase A — apt install postgresql-16, pgbouncer, ufw, fail2ban
  12. Phase B — postgresql.conf + pg_hba.conf, restart postgres
  13. Phase C — create owner + app roles, createdb, pgbouncer userlist,
                ufw rules, enable fail2ban
  14. init-db.sh --apply           (schemas + grants)
  15. install-tooling.sh --apply   (verify + tune)
  16. validate.sh --apply --host <ip>  (nine JSON checks)
  17. Print success summary  (passwords MASKED in display)

Safety notes:
  - Root password is passed via stdin (--password -) so it never appears
    in /proc/<pid>/cmdline or shell history
  - The /tmp rendered cloud-init contains the Postgres creds; it is
    removed at exit
  - On failure the LXC is NEVER auto-destroyed — operator decides whether
    to keep for debug or run destroy.sh manually
  - Logs are tee'd to atlas-mgmt-provision-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSZ.log in cwd
    (only when --apply; dry-run keeps stdout pristine for review)

* feat(atlas-mgmt): init-db.sh — per-module schemas + grants

Idempotent SQL setup. Runs INSIDE the LXC via pct exec (pushed by
provision.sh) or locally for dry-run review.

Creates 15 schemas, one per module that ends up writing to mgmt-db:
  aegis, audit, beacon_meta, platform, mesh, atlas_meta, spark_meta,
  tide_meta, nexus_meta, flux_meta, blaze_meta, ignite_meta, herald,
  marketing, convoy_meta

For each schema:
  CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS <m> AUTHORIZATION developy_mgmt
  GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA <m> TO app_runtime
  GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA <m> TO app_runtime
  GRANT USAGE,SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA <m> TO app_runtime
  ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE developy_mgmt IN SCHEMA <m>
    GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE ON TABLES TO app_runtime
  ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE developy_mgmt IN SCHEMA <m>
    GRANT USAGE,SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO app_runtime

Plus:
  REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC
  GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO app_runtime
  CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto  (drizzle needs gen_random_uuid)

Safe to re-run as many times as needed. Re-running after drizzle creates
new tables grants the new objects to app_runtime — that's a feature.

Identifiers go through a `qi()` quoting helper so schema names with mixed
case or reserved-word collisions stay well-formed.

* feat(atlas-mgmt): provision.sh orchestrator (dry-run by default)

Main entry point. Default mode is --dry-run; --apply requires an
interactive APPLY token. Runs on the Proxmox node and uses pct/pvesm
locally — never calls the Proxmox HTTP API.

Flow (--apply):
   1. preflight.sh                                          (read-only)
   2. confirm_or_die "APPLY"                                (interactive)
   3. Render cloud-init.yaml.tpl via awk to /tmp            (PG creds inlined)
   4. Upload as snippet to ATLAS_MGMT_SNIPPETS_STORAGE      (audit artifact)
   5. pct create  --unprivileged --features=nesting=0       (LXC, not VM)
   6. pct set --tags 'developy;managed-by-bootstrap-script;atlas-mgmt'
   7. pct start
   8. Wait up to ATLAS_MGMT_SSH_TIMEOUT for SSH
   9. pct push  init-db.sh + install-tooling.sh + lib + inner .env
  10. Write /etc/developy/lxc.marker  (destroy.sh Gate 4 anchor)
  11. Phase A — apt install postgresql-16, pgbouncer, ufw, fail2ban
  12. Phase B — postgresql.conf + pg_hba.conf, restart postgres
  13. Phase C — create owner + app roles, createdb, pgbouncer userlist,
                ufw rules, enable fail2ban
  14. init-db.sh --apply           (schemas + grants)
  15. install-tooling.sh --apply   (verify + tune)
  16. validate.sh --apply --host <ip>  (nine JSON checks)
  17. Print success summary  (passwords MASKED in display)

Safety notes:
  - Root password is passed via stdin (--password -) so it never appears
    in /proc/<pid>/cmdline or shell history
  - The /tmp rendered cloud-init contains the Postgres creds; it is
    removed at exit
  - On failure the LXC is NEVER auto-destroyed — operator decides whether
    to keep for debug or run destroy.sh manually
  - Logs are tee'd to atlas-mgmt-provision-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSSZ.log in cwd
    (only when --apply; dry-run keeps stdout pristine for review)

* feat(atlas-mgmt): destroy.sh with 5-gate confirmation

Last-resort emergency lever. Mirrors builder-vm/destroy.sh's posture
and extends it to LXC (pct instead of qm).

Five gates — ALL must pass:
  Gate 1  --i-know-what-im-doing flag is passed
  Gate 2  pct status $ATLAS_MGMT_VMID exists on this node
  Gate 3  pct config $ATLAS_MGMT_VMID hostname == .env ATLAS_MGMT_HOSTNAME
  Gate 4  /etc/developy/lxc.marker inside the LXC references
          scripts/bootstrap/atlas-mgmt/provision.sh
  Gate 5  Operator types  "DESTROY <vmid>"  verbatim at prompt

If the LXC is stopped at Gate 4, the script briefly starts it to read
the marker, then stops it again before destroy. This prevents the
"VM was stopped, marker check skipped" footgun while still being
non-destructive.

Escape hatches:
  ATLAS_MGMT_SKIP_MARKER_CHECK=1   bypasses Gate 4 only
                                   (logged as WARN; never silent)
  ATLAS_MGMT_NONINTERACTIVE=1      skips Gate 5 typed-confirm
                                   (intended for controlled CI-like reruns,
                                   never for casual destroys)

Lists current snapshots + PBS backups before destroying. Removes the
cloud-init snippet from /var/lib/vz/snippets after pct destroy succeeds.
Does NOT delete pg_dumps in mgmt-tide or weekly B2 archives — restore
remains possible.

Running with no flags: prints banner, fails Gate 1, exits 1.

title: feat(audit): adopt StoreBackend SPI + postgres adapter
body:
feat(audit): adopt StoreBackend SPI + postgres adapter

Mirrors Beacon template (PR #21). Adapter maps AuditStoreData ↔ drizzle rows
with append-only semantics. Store uses getStoreBackend() — default JSON,
postgres when AUDIT_STORE_BACKEND=postgres. Migrate-stores CLI gains audit
mapper with pg-mem round-trip tests covering append behavior.

Schema gains one column: `external_id text NOT NULL` plus a composite
unique index `(external_id, created_at)`. The producer-supplied legacy id
("aud-<ts>-<n>") survives as the natural identity so the StoreBackend SPI
can upsert and the migrate-stores CLI can dedupe re-runs idempotently. The
composite-unique with the partition key satisfies Postgres's partitioning
rule (every UNIQUE must include the partition key).

Counter is recomputed from the highest legacy-id suffix on load — not a
separate kv blob — so audit.events stays a single-collection store.

JSON-mode behaviour is unchanged: same in-memory MAX_EVENTS=1000 ring,
fire-and-forget persist, auditEnabled gating, listAuditEvents newest-first
ordering.

body:
feat(atlas): adopt StoreBackend SPI + postgres adapter (Wave 2 Tier 3) (#35)

Migrates the Atlas meta store (.atlas-store.json) from encrypted JSON to
Postgres behind the StoreBackend SPI. Mirrors Beacon (PR #21), Aegis
(PR #24), Marketing (PR #23) shape — same lazy-singleton, env-flip
toggle, zero-regression JSON-mode default.

Schema (apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/atlas.ts):
- atlas_clusters            text PK, jsonb lxc_ids/tags, pgEnum
                            engine/size/status/ha_mode
- atlas_credentials         text PK, FK cluster_id ON DELETE CASCADE,
                            partial-index-friendly composite on
                            (cluster_id, revoked_at)
- atlas_idempotency_records request_id PK, 24h TTL (enforced at app),
                            indexes on expires_at + resource_id

Migration (0004_create_atlas_meta_tables.sql):
- All CREATE TABLE — no ALTER on incoming-FK columns, so the FK
  ordering bug from PR #27 doesn't apply.
- Hand-written via pnpm db:new (new workflow, not drizzle-kit generate).

Adapter (apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/postgres-adapter.ts):
- Lossless row↔domain mapping for all three collections.
- replaceAll uses a transaction; child-table deletes happen first to
  match the marketing/beacon pattern.
- upsertOne handles `idempotencyRecords` by routing the SPI id to
  request_id (the natural PK for that collection).

Store rewrite (apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/store.ts):
- Thin wrappers over backend.load/saveEntity/deleteEntity.
- Custom getItemId understands both `id` (clusters/credentials) and
  `requestId` (idempotency) for JSON-mode saveEntity.
- saveIdempotencyRecord preserves the expired-record sweep at the
  store layer so both backends behave identically.
- deleteCluster manually cascades credentials in JSON mode; Postgres
  mode also has FK CASCADE as defence-in-depth.
- revokeCredential reads → mutates → saveEntity (avoids partial
  upsert losing other columns).

Migrate-stores mapper (scripts/migrate-stores/modules/atlas.ts):
- Three collections mapped with conflictTargets for idempotent re-runs.
- `lxcIds`/`tags` jsonb columns serialized via JSON.stringify and
  parsed back through a tolerant helper that accepts both string and
  array shapes (drizzle returns objects, MemoryDriver compares strings).
- IdempotencyRecord aliases requestId as non-enumerable request_id so
  the runner's dedupe step sees a unique key without polluting the
  recovered JSON shape (same trick audit uses for external_id).

Tests added: 23 (8 mapper round-trip + 15 store regression).
- Mapper test covers row count parity, optional-field handling, jsonb
  array round-trip, idempotency, empty-store edge case.
- Store regression test covers JSON-mode CRUD + filter + cascade +
  revokeCredential + saveIdempotencyRecord sweep + env-flip routing.

Also updated tests/atlas/01-store.integration.test.ts to call
resetAtlasStoreBackendForTesting() around its ATLAS_STORE_PATH env
swaps — required because the lazy singleton caches the resolved path
on first call.

Append-only entry in scripts/migrate-stores/modules/index.ts; does
not touch any sibling _meta module (spark/tide/nexus/flux/mesh own
their own migrations).

title: fix(calendar-integrations): 30s idempotency short-circuit in completeOAuth
body:
fix(calendar-integrations): 30s idempotency short-circuit in completeOAuth

Real production flow: user clicks 'Conectar Google' once → BB creates 1
connection → frontend hits /oauth/callback-return; if the call is retried
(double-click, browser retry on prior 302→CORS failure, etc), the second
call sees the connection already claimed → either picks a DIFFERENT
unclaimed connection (bad UX — gives user the wrong calendar) or throws
NotFoundException.

Short-circuit: if the user has any calendar-bb Credential created <30s
ago, return it instead of picking another unclaimed connection. Matches
the intuition 'duplicate retries should be idempotent'.

Trade-off: a user genuinely connecting two calendars within 30s would
get the first one returned. Refresh + retry works around it. Better than
silently grabbing a stale unclaimed connection.

Confirmed in stg parallel-call test 2026-05-13: pre-fix, two parallel
callback-return hits grabbed two different unclaimed connections (Outlook
3885d006 + Google 04b365bd). With this fix, the second call returns the
first call's Credential.

fix(calendar-integrations): decrypt config before extracting connectionId

Follow-up to e388e19d. The earlier idempotency/dedupe checks read
`cred.config.connectionId` directly, but `Credential.config` is the
**encrypted string** stored in DB — not a decrypted object. Result:
claimedIds was always empty, every completeOAuth call picked the same
'newest unclaimed' BB connection (even when it had been claimed seconds
before by an earlier call from the same user), and duplicates kept
appearing despite the new idempotency code.

Confirmed in stg post-deploy re-test 2026-05-13: hitting /oauth/callback-return
re-claimed BB connection 55b28752 even though admin already had a Credential
pointing to it.

Fix: invoke credentials.findOneDecrypted per Credential to read the real
decrypted connectionId. O(n) per user — fine for typical < 10 calendar
credentials. Same fix applied to both the initial claimedIds calculation
and the pre-create dedupe re-check.

title: fix(calendar-integrations): idempotent completeOAuth + JSON callback response
body:
fix(calendar-integrations): idempotent completeOAuth + JSON callback response

Two bugs surfaced during stg manual smoke 2026-05-13 (admin@catalisa.app
clicked 'Conectar Google' → saw 'Network Error' on the OAuth return page,
but list now shows 2 Credentials pointing to the same BB connectionId).

Bug 1 — Network Error: oauthCallbackReturn returned 302 → frontendUrl.
Axios followed the cross-origin redirect from panel-api.* → panel.*
SPA static host, which has no CORS for the API caller → preflight fails →
'Network Error'. The Credential was created server-side but the frontend
never saw the success. Fix: return JSON { success, credentialId } instead
of the 302; CalendarOAuthReturn.tsx already navigates client-side.

Bug 2 — Duplicate Credentials: two parallel callback-return hits both
saw the new BB connection as 'newest unclaimed' (584ms apart) and both
wrote Credentials. Race window between findAll() and credentials.create().
Fix: two-layer idempotency in completeOAuth:
  a) If every ACTIVE BB connection is already claimed by this user AND
     the most recent claim is < 30s old, return it (handles 'retry after
     visible Network Error' scenario).
  b) After picking an unclaimed connection but before create, re-fetch
     this user's credentials and check if the picked connection is now
     claimed (parallel call beat us to the write). Return it.

Both fixes are surgical and backwards-compatible (frontend already
ignored the 302 response body; existing single-call flow goes through
unchanged paths). 2 new unit tests pin the idempotency + dedupe paths.

fix(calendar-integrations): SLOTS contract — match BB findSlotsSchema 1:1

Stg smoke 2026-05-13 (AI agent test): get_calendar_slots looped 5 times
trying different ranges before falling back. Root cause: param names
diverged from BB Calendar Hono service contract.

BB expects (per findSlotsSchema in building-blocks-v2/src/calendar/types/
index.ts:378):
  - startDate (NOT startDateTime)
  - endDate (NOT endDateTime)
  - duration: number 5..480 (NOT durationMinutes)

  - quantity: 1..100, default 10 (NOT maxSlots)

    timeZone fallback ('America/Sao_Paulo' if not provided by config)
  - removed workingHours/bufferMinutes (not in BB schema); periodStart/
    periodEnd pass through as HH:MM strings; weekdaysOnly pass through

processNotification used to look up the EmailProviderSubscription by
body.value[0].subscriptionId (Graph format only). Pub/Sub push has a
different shape — body.subscription is the Pub/Sub resource path, not
our external_id. We now detect the provider format and, for Gmail,
decode the base64 message.data envelope to read emailAddress (which
is what we stored as externalId at watch time).

column has a unique constraint with no soft-delete predicate, so

title: feat(wpp): Baileys outbound webhooks via webhooks-engine parity
body:
feat(wpp): Baileys outbound webhooks via webhooks-engine parity

Brings wpp (Baileys) to feature parity with wpp-business for outbound webhook
delivery. Subscribers register a WppDispatcher; the webhooks-engine BB handles
signing, retry, and delivery. Same architecture wpp-business uses, but without
the four inherited debts (httpMethod field, per-dispatcher signingSecret,
text-serialized customHeaders, duplicated retryConfig).

Key points:
- WppDispatcher model with deviceId pre-filter (Baileys equivalent of
  phoneNumberId) and JSONPath conditions for ADVANCED mode
- Dispatch-specific re-publish trick: when deviceId/conditions are set, the
  subscription filter is wpp.dispatch.{id} and the matched event is re-published
  in evaluateDispatchers — engine sees only events that passed pre-filtering
- New wpp.v1.* event namespace published in parallel to legacy wpp.* (back-compat
  for internal consumers, public surface for external subscribers)
- emitWppPublic helper in lib/public-events.ts wires every user-facing publish
  point (message/device/chat/group/contact) without touching service constructors
- DispatcherService registered in registerPostFacadeServices to resolve
  WebhooksEngineFacadeToken (same pattern as WppBizDispatcherService)
- Anti-SSRF validation on endpointUrl (blocks localhost, private IPs, .internal)
- Permissions WPP_DISPATCHERS_READ/WRITE added to IAM types

Smoke-tested end-to-end: dispatcher CRUD → subscription auto-created in
webhooks-engine → real device create triggers wpp.v1.device.status.changed
via emitWppPublic → consumer delivers HTTP 200 to httpbin. Per-device
pre-filter verified: raw v1 events don't leak to dispatchers with a deviceId
set. 15 unit tests covering deriveEventFilters, matchesDispatcher, CRUD
orchestration.

title: feat(deploy): implement migration + verify/current/tag-current/rollback endpoints (#38)
body:
feat(deploy): implement migration + verify/current/tag-current/rollback endpoints (#38)

Server-side counterparts to the CLI's MgmtApiDriver. Previously the CLI's
mgmt-api.ts was calling `/api/deploy/migrations/{dry-run,apply}` and four
other endpoints that didn't exist — every ship hit a 404 (or middleware
hang) on those phases. This PR adds them.

Endpoints
=========

POST /api/deploy/migrations/dry-run
  Returns { applied[], pending[], diff } for the requested env. Uses the
  same scripts/db-migrate/runner.ts the `pnpm db:apply` CLI uses, so
  filename ordering and the __migrations tracking table stay consistent.
  Resolves DATABASE_URL_<ENV> only — REFUSES to fall back to bare
  DATABASE_URL (preventing prod migrations from accidentally running
  against a dev DB).

POST /api/deploy/migrations/apply
  Same env resolution. Captures the diff BEFORE apply so the response
  carries the SQL that ran (audit trail + Herald event payload). Each
  migration runs in its own transaction; partial failures don't roll
  back previously-applied migrations from the same call (forward-only).

GET  /api/deploy/verify?env&target
  Returns { errorRate, errorRateBaseline, p95Ms, p95BaselineMs, healthy }.
  Today: synthetic but realistic numbers. The MgmtVerifyResponse contract
  is locked — when Radar/Pulse Prometheus rules land, swap collectVerify's
  body to pull real series without touching the API surface.

GET  /api/deploy/current?env&target
  Returns the sha currently deployed (from the on-disk current-store).
  Used by orchestrator previousSha bookkeeping.

POST /api/deploy/tag-current
  Finalize-phase callback. Records env+target -> sha+image+actor in
  ~/.developy/deploys/current.json (atomic write via tmp + rename).

POST /api/deploy/rollback
  Reverts to a prior sha. Today: records the rollback as the new current
  eagerly + returns a jobId; actual container restart is the orchestrator's
  job via the deploy phase using --image=<sha>. Idempotent if orchestrator
  crashes mid-rollback.

State store
===========

lib/server/deploy/current-store.ts — small on-disk JSON map keyed by
"env:target". Persists across mgmt-panel restarts (in-memory map would
forget what's live on every deploy). Write failures are logged but
non-fatal — worst case is one stale 'current' entry that the next
successful deploy corrects.

Safety
======

All endpoints require requireWriteSession except verify/current (read).
The DATABASE_URL_<ENV> env scheme means the mgmt panel must be configured
per env — there's no way to point one mgmt deployment at the wrong DB
without explicit setup.

Tested locally with `bun ship` against http://localhost:3000:
  - verify: HTTP 200 with proper shape
  - migrations/dry-run: HTTP 400 when DATABASE_URL_PROD unset (correct
    refusal), HTTP 200 with applied/pending/diff when configured

title: feat(ship): real drivers + OAuth-link CLI auth flow (#37)
body:
feat(ship): real drivers + OAuth-link CLI auth flow (#37)

Wires up real infra drivers behind DEVELOPY_REAL_INFRA_ENABLED=true and
adds a device-flow auth subcommand so the CLI no longer needs a manual
bot token to talk to mgmt-api.

Previously `bun ship:prod` always ran with mock drivers — buildDrivers
throw'd when realInfraEnabled=true (scripts/ship/index.ts:80, pre-change).
Result: every `ship` invocation looked theatrical, no real prod work
happened, and migrations like 0010_cleanup_atlas_repl_test_zombies.sql
never reached prod.

Real drivers
============

scripts/ship/drivers/registry.ts (new)
  Docker Registry V2 HEAD-manifest check. Follows a Bearer challenge
  once when the registry returns 401 (Harbor, GHCR, Docker Hub all
  speak the same dance). parseImage handles digests and nested repos.

scripts/ship/drivers/herald.ts (new)
  Posts deploy events to Loki using the same wire format as the web
  app emitter (apps/web/src/lib/server/herald/emitter.ts). Nanosecond
  timestamps via BigInt to avoid precision loss past 2^53. Failures
  are swallow-by-default (best-effort observability — a Loki outage
  must not kill the deploy).

scripts/ship/index.ts
  buildDrivers(ResolvedConfig) — when realInfraEnabled, returns real
  ssh-builder + mgmt-api + registry + git + herald (Loki if configured,
  otherwise herald-mock). Fails fast with a friendly error if no
  bearer token is resolvable.

scripts/ship/config.ts + types.ts
  New env knobs: DEVELOPY_REGISTRY_USER/PASSWORD,
  DEVELOPY_HERALD_LOKI_URL/LABELS/USER/PASSWORD,
  DEVELOPY_BUILDER_IDENTITY_FILE. All optional.

OAuth-link CLI auth
===================

`bun ship auth login` runs a GitHub-device-code-style flow:

  1. POST /api/deploy/cli/init → { code, verifyUrl, interval, expiresInSec }
  2. CLI prints the verifyUrl and the 8-char code
  3. User opens verifyUrl → existing Aegis login bounces them back to
     /auth/cli?code=ABCD-1234 with a session cookie
  4. The /auth/cli page POSTs /api/deploy/cli/authorize (write session
     required) which mints an HMAC-signed bearer via the existing
     issueSession() and binds it to the pending code
  5. CLI poll loop hits /api/deploy/cli/poll until status=approved,
     then writes ~/.developy/auth.json (mode 0600)

Token resolution order in the CLI:
  1. DEVELOPY_DEPLOY_BOT_TOKEN env (CI / service accounts)
  2. ~/.developy/auth.json (interactive)
  3. None → friendly error

Subcommands: `bun ship auth login | logout | status`.

Backend (apps/web)
==================

apps/web/src/lib/server/deploy/cli-auth-store.ts
  In-memory map of pending sessions. 10-minute TTL, 32-bit codes,
  one-shot consume on poll. Test reset hook for vitest isolation.
  When the web app eventually goes multi-instance behind an LB this
  needs to move to Postgres/Redis — single swap-out point documented.

apps/web/src/app/api/deploy/cli/{init,poll,authorize}/route.ts
  init + poll are public (knowing the code is the auth). authorize
  requires requireWriteSession and mints a 24h token via issueSession.

apps/web/src/app/auth/cli/page.tsx
  Minimal page (~140 LOC): reads ?code=, shows the code for visual
  confirmation, Authorize / Deny buttons. If not signed in, bounces
  to /login with next= preserving the code. No new design tokens or
  shadcn-ui additions — uses existing Card/Button.

Tests
=====

  scripts/ship: 113 tests, 81 existing + 32 new
    - drivers/registry.test.ts (10)  — parseImage cases, HEAD 200/404/401-bearer-retry/500
    - drivers/herald.test.ts (5)     — Loki payload shape, swallow/propagate, basic auth
    - auth.test.ts (17)              — save/load + mode 0600, resolver priority, full poll loop
  apps/web:
    - lib/server/deploy/cli-auth-store.test.ts (10) — init/approve/poll one-shot/TTL expiry

typecheck: zero new errors in apps/web or scripts/ship.

Brings wpp (Baileys) to feature parity with wpp-business for outbound webhook
delivery. Subscribers register a WppDispatcher; the webhooks-engine BB handles
signing, retry, and delivery. Same architecture wpp-business uses, but without
the four inherited debts (httpMethod field, per-dispatcher signingSecret,
text-serialized customHeaders, duplicated retryConfig).

Key points:
- WppDispatcher model with deviceId pre-filter (Baileys equivalent of
  phoneNumberId) and JSONPath conditions for ADVANCED mode
- Dispatch-specific re-publish trick: when deviceId/conditions are set, the
  subscription filter is wpp.dispatch.{id} and the matched event is re-published
  in evaluateDispatchers — engine sees only events that passed pre-filtering
- New wpp.v1.* event namespace published in parallel to legacy wpp.* (back-compat
  for internal consumers, public surface for external subscribers)
- emitWppPublic helper in lib/public-events.ts wires every user-facing publish
  point (message/device/chat/group/contact) without touching service constructors
- DispatcherService registered in registerPostFacadeServices to resolve
  WebhooksEngineFacadeToken (same pattern as WppBizDispatcherService)
- Anti-SSRF validation on endpointUrl (blocks localhost, private IPs, .internal)
- Permissions WPP_DISPATCHERS_READ/WRITE added to IAM types

Smoke-tested end-to-end: dispatcher CRUD → subscription auto-created in
webhooks-engine → real device create triggers wpp.v1.device.status.changed
via emitWppPublic → consumer delivers HTTP 200 to httpbin. Per-device
pre-filter verified: raw v1 events don't leak to dispatchers with a deviceId
set. 15 unit tests covering deriveEventFilters, matchesDispatcher, CRUD
orchestration.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-05-14-wpp-baileys-webhooks-engine-parity.md

fix(wpp): emit wpp.v1.message.received.* from session-manager Baileys path

Closes parity gap with wpp-business's HTTP-ingested path: before this, the
Baileys `messages.upsert` handler at session-manager.ts:651-680 went directly
from `messageRepository.upsertByKeyId` to the internal Pub/Sub channel
`wpp-events:{orgId}` only — `wpp.v1.message.received.*` was NEVER emitted to
webhooks-engine subscribers, so dispatcher pre-filter routing produced zero
delivery_logs even for matching events.

Now mirrors message.service.ts:171-198 (Cloud API path): after the upsert
resolves, emits a public v1 event with the canonical publicPayload shape
(organizationId, messageId, keyId, remoteJid, fromMe, type, deviceId) so
the webhooks-engine fan-out + DispatcherService.evaluateDispatchers can
do their job.

Imports `messageReceivedV1` from @wpp/types/events (already exported there).

Smoke-proven end-to-end against `operacao-digital-real-test` device with operacao-digital as a
subscriber: 4 hello_world templates from wpp-business stg → BB Baileys
sync → emit → dispatcher match → delivery → HTTP 200 ACK + operacao-digital Message
row created (see operacao-digital CHANGELOG.md 2026-05-15 parte 11).

title: feat(mesh+atlas): networks as first-class IPAM + IPv6 default + UI (#39)
body:
feat(mesh+atlas): networks as first-class IPAM + IPv6 default + UI (#39)

* feat(mesh+atlas): networks as first-class IPAM with IPv6 default + UI

The platform's IP topology is now visible and managed through Mesh.
Atlas — and any future data product — allocates IPs from named
'networks' instead of hash-modulo'd vmid math. Default network is the
operator's public IPv6 /56, so new databases get publicly-routed
addresses with no NAT mangling.

Schema (3 migrations)
=====================

0011 — extend mesh_ip_pools with bridge / nameservers / dns_search.
  A pool was an abstract address range; now it can also describe a
  real Proxmox network. Provisioners read every field they need from
  one record.

0012 — add network_pool_id + ip_allocation_id to atlas_clusters.
  Each cluster row remembers which Mesh pool it came from and the
  exact allocation id so deprovision can release it back.

0013 — pool source enum + parent_pool_id FK.
  'platform-rented' (carved subnet from an upstream pool we own) vs
  'byo' (org-owned range we just track). Sets up the SaaS model where
  customers either rent /64 from us or bring their own.

Provisioner refactor
====================

apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/networks.ts (new)
  getOrCreateDefaultNetwork() bootstraps a pool named 'default' on
  first call. Reads DATA_PRODUCTS_* env when no pool exists yet.

apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/provisioner.ts
  Replaces vmidToIp(vmid%256) with mesh.reserveAddress(poolId).
  Family-aware: ip6/gw6 instead of ip/gw when the pool is IPv6.
  releaseClusterAllocations() drops every allocation tagged with
  serviceId=<clusterId> on deprovision or provision failure.
  Persists networkPoolId + ipAllocationId so a crash-restart can find
  the allocations for cleanup.

apps/web/src/lib/server/data-products/provisioner-base.ts
  When only IPv6 is supplied, sets net0 ip=manual (not dhcp). The
  Debian 13 LXC template was sitting on 'iface eth0 inet dhcp' waiting
  for a v4 lease that never came, blocking ifupdown from reaching the
  inet6 stanza below it. The manual fix unblocks IPv6-only LXCs.

apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/store.ts + postgres-adapter.ts +
db/schema/atlas.ts + validation.ts
  AtlasCluster gains networkPoolId + ipAllocationId. POST /clusters
  accepts an optional networkPoolId; null falls back to the default
  pool.

Atlas endpoint encoding (provisioner.ts)
  IPv4 (private pool, NAT): DNAT 5000+vmid on the Proxmox public IPv4
    → LXC :5432. Endpoint = '<public-host>:<port>'.
  IPv6 (public routed pool): no NAT, no port mangling. Endpoint =
    '[<ipv6>]:5432' bracketed per RFC 3986.

Mesh IPAM type changes
======================

packages/platform/src/mesh/entities.ts
  IPPool gains bridge, nameservers, dnsSearch, source, parentPoolId.

apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/ipam-engine.ts
  createPool() and CreatePoolInput accept the new fields.

apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/postgres-adapter.ts
  Maps the new columns; nameservers serialised as CSV in the text
  column.

apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/validation.ts
  CreateIPPoolSchema accepts bridge / nameservers / dnsSearch / source
  / parentPoolId.

UI
==

apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/mesh/networks/page.tsx (new)
  '/mesh/networks' — single page that lists every pool with a clear
  status (family badge, source badge, used / total counter). Create
  dialog accepts family, CIDR, bridge, gateway, nameservers, source.
  Delete is gated on zero active allocations.

apps/web/src/lib/modules/mesh.module.ts
  Nav: 'Networks' top-level under the 'Network' group; old 'IP Pools'
  kept and re-labeled 'IP Pools (legacy)' for backwards compat.

End-to-end validation (against prod 2026-05-15)
================================================

  curl -X POST /api/atlas/clusters {engine:postgresql, size:xs}
   → status=requested
   → status=provisioning, IP=2804:1740:f:2000::4/56 from pool default
   → status=configuring (apt over IPv6, AAAA-resolved)
   → status=active, endpoint=[2804:1740:f:2000::4]:5432   (1m 12s)
   → herald cluster.provisioned success
  TCP from a real-IPv6 host: connection accepted, postgres 17.10
  responding.

Deletion path validated too: release tags the cluster's allocations
'released', deprovisioner removes the LXC and the atlas_clusters row.

Known gaps tracked for the next PR
==================================

- Tenant scoping on the pool API: today /api/mesh/ipam/pools trusts
  whatever tenantId the body carries. Once we have an org-membership
  resolver (Aegis already has tenant data), POST should force
  tenantId=session.org and GET should filter by it. The schema is
  already tenant-aware (unique on tenant_id, name).
- Subnet carving: POST /pools/:id/sub-pools that simultaneously
  reserves the child range in the parent and creates a child pool with
  parentPoolId=parent. Today operators do it manually in two steps.
- Default-network UI selector in Atlas create dialog: currently the
  Mesh default is implicit. A future drop-down on cluster create
  should let users pick any of their networks.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(mesh): subnet carving + rentable flag + 2-step network UI

Builds on PR #39 (networks as first-class IPAM) with the UX the user
called out as missing: when you rent from a platform network you need
to pick *which* one, and the system should suggest sensible sizes so
addresses don't sprawl unbilled.

Schema (1 migration)
====================

0014 — ALTER TABLE mesh_ip_pools ADD COLUMN is_public_rentable boolean
  DEFAULT false. Operator flag, decoupled from source/tenantId. When
  true the pool appears in tenants' 'Rent from' dropdowns. Default
  false — explicit opt-in, no surprises about cross-tenant visibility.

  Initial state in prod: only the IPv6 default (/56) is rentable; the
  two IPv4 platform pools stay operator-only.

Carving engine (server)
=======================

apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/ipam-engine.ts
  carveSubPool({parentId, name, tenantId, childPrefixLen}):
    1. Validates parent exists + is public-rentable (or owned by the
       requesting tenant).
    2. Finds the next aligned subnet of childPrefixLen not already
       carved (checks existing children CIDRs + marker allocations).
    3. Creates child pool: source='platform-rented', parentPoolId set,
       bridge/gateway/nameservers/dnsSearch inherited from parent.
    4. Records a marker allocation on the parent with
       serviceId='sub-pool:<childId>' blocking the range from being
       re-carved AND letting deletePool find + release it.

  deletePool now reverses the marker on the parent when a carved
  child is removed (and decrements the parent's allocatedAddresses).

  IPv6 arithmetic: ipv6ToBigInt + bigIntToIpv6 helpers do shorthand-
  aware expansion and longest-zero-run compression. Good enough for
  the ::-style addresses our pools use.

API
===

POST /api/mesh/ipam/pools/:parentId/carve
  Body: { requestId, name, childPrefixLen, tenantId? }
  Response: the freshly-created child IPPool.

Validation: CarveSubPoolSchema in mesh/validation.ts.

Type / adapter updates
======================

packages/platform/src/mesh/entities.ts
  IPPool gains isPublicRentable: boolean.

apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/mesh.ts + postgres-adapter.ts
  Maps the new boolean column.

apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/validation.ts
  CreateIPPoolSchema accepts isPublicRentable.

UI
==

apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/mesh/networks/page.tsx
  Create dialog is now a 3-screen wizard:

  Step 1 (source) — two big radio cards:
    'Rent from a platform network' (recommended for most teams) vs
    'Bring my own range (BYO)'.

  Step 2A (rent) — pick a platform network, pick a size from a
  predefined list with friendly labels:
    IPv6: 1 / 256 / 65k addresses or full /64 (typical).
    IPv4: 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 addresses.
  Preview shows the CIDR + inherited bridge/gateway/DNS before
  committing.

  Step 2B (BYO) — CIDR, optional bridge, gateway, DNS, plus a
  'Allow other tenants to rent from this network' toggle (off by
  default).

  The networks table now shows a 'Rentable' badge so operators can see
  at a glance which pools tenants can carve from.

apps/web/src/hooks/use-mesh.ts
  useCarveSubPool() hook, useCreateMeshIPPool() extended with the new
  optional fields (bridge / nameservers / dnsSearch / source /
  parentPoolId / isPublicRentable).

End-to-end validation (prod 2026-05-15)
========================================

  curl POST /api/mesh/ipam/pools/<default-pool>/carve
    { name: 'my-test-net', childPrefixLen: 64 }
  →
    pool-1778854151287-dofv38
    cidr: '2804:1740:f:2000::/64'
    source: 'platform-rented'
    parentPoolId: <default-pool>
    bridge/gateway/nameservers: inherited

  DELETE /api/mesh/ipam/pools/<child>
    → marker allocation released on parent
    → parent allocatedAddresses decremented
    → child row removed

Known gaps for next PR
======================

- **Carving doesn't propagate parent-level reservations into children.**
  The IPv6 default pool has ::1 (gateway) and ::2/::3 (host) marked as
  infrastructure-reserved on the parent. Carving the first /64
  (2804:1740:f:2000::/64) produces a child whose allocator doesn't
  know about those reservations and would happily hand out ::2.
  Workaround: don't carve the first /64 of the parent (or pre-mark it
  reserved before opening the parent to rent). Real fix: either copy
  relevant parent reservations into the child at carve time, OR have
  reserveAddress walk up the parent chain when checking conflicts.
- **Pricing/billing surfaces.** The size dropdowns mention pricing
  ('/mo per IP') as the eventual model but no billing wiring yet.
- **Tenant scoping** still trusts body tenantId (called out in PR #39).
- **Quantity != prefix sometimes.** For IPv6 'rent 1 IP' currently
  carves a /128. That works but is conceptually wasteful for a
  parent-level allocation. Could be a single-IP allocation in parent
  with no child pool. Decided later when the billing model lands.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(mesh): carving uses O(n) gap-finding instead of slot enumeration

Picking the next free sub-CIDR was iterating every aligned slot
(2^(child-parent)). For a /128 carve out of a /56 parent that's 2^72
slots — Math.pow returns ~1.8e21 and we threw 'Prefix delta too
large' before even looking. User hit this when picking '1 address'
(/128) from the dropdown.

New approach: collect the bigint ranges already taken (existing
children + carve markers), sort, walk from parent base looking for the
first aligned step-sized gap. Cost is O(existing-carves), not
O(slots). For an empty parent we find the first slot in one comparison.

Bigint math runs the same code path for both families now — helpers
toBigInt(addr,family) and fromBigInt(n,family) collapse the v4/v6 fork
that nthAlignedSubnetAddress used to have.

Validated against the IPv6 /56 default pool:
  /128 → 2804:1740:f:2000::/128            (slot 0)
  /120 → 2804:1740:f:2000::100/120         (jumped past /128)
  /64  → 2804:1740:f:2001::/64             (jumped past /128 and /120)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(atlas): pg_hba.conf needs ::/0 too on IPv6-only LXCs

Provisioner was writing only 'host all all 0.0.0.0/0 md5' to pg_hba.
With the IPv6 default network LXCs have no IPv4 — every external
client connecting via [ipv6]:5432 got the TCP accept but the
postgres protocol then closed the connection because pg_hba had no
matching v6 rule. TCP probe (bash /dev/tcp) succeeded but
pg_isready/psql said 'no response' / 'no pg_hba entry'.

Add the v6 counterparts to both the user-auth and replication
lines. Hot-patched the running e2e-ipv6-v2 cluster to confirm the
fix unblocks the protocol — sending an SSLRequest now gets back 'S'
(yes, SSL supported) instead of a close.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(mesh): conflict detection + auto-fix proposals + Atlas defense

User-facing problem: a carve that lands in the same /N as the parent's
gateway/host IPs (::1/::2/::3 on our /56) silently works until a service
joins the network and collides at allocation time. Non-technical users
won't know the carve is in a 'danger zone'.

Now the system reasons about it on three layers.

Layer 1 (already in previous commit)
====================================

carveSubPool's gap-finder includes parent allocations as blockers. New
carves automatically land in safe slots. No user thought required.

Layer 2 — conflict detection + auto-fix proposal
================================================

apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/ipam-engine.ts
  detectPoolConflict(poolId) — for a child pool, returns:
    - conflictingAddresses: parent allocations whose address falls
      inside the child's CIDR (gateway, infra reservations, etc.).
    - proposedSafeCidr: same prefix length, next aligned non-conflict
      slot. Null when the parent has no free slot of that size.

  findNextFreeSubnetCidr(parent, prefixLen, excludePoolId?) — pulled
  out of carveSubPool so detection can share the gap-finder logic
  without mutating state. excludePoolId lets the conflict propose a
  replacement for THIS same pool.

  autoFixPoolConflict(poolId) — delete-and-recarve flow:
    1. Validate pool has parent + zero active allocations (auto-fix
       would otherwise need service migration, which we don't do).
    2. deletePool() — cascades the carve marker release on parent.
    3. carveSubPool() with the same name+tenant+prefix; new gap-finder
       puts it in a safe slot.
  Refuses with POOL_IN_USE when the caller still has services
  attached — the UI then tells the user to release them first.

Layer 3 — Atlas defense
=======================

apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/provisioner.ts
  Before reserveAddress(), call detectPoolConflict(). If the target
  pool overlaps with platform reservations, refuse to provision with
  a message pointing at the proposed safe CIDR. Catches the case
  where layer 2 hasn't been auto-fixed yet.

API
===

GET  /api/mesh/ipam/pools/:id/conflicts
  Returns { conflictingAddresses[], proposedSafeCidr|null }.

POST /api/mesh/ipam/pools/:id/auto-fix
  Body: { requestId? }. Returns the freshly-carved replacement pool.

UI
==

apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/mesh/networks/page.tsx
  - PoolConflictBadge — fetches /:id/conflicts for any pool with a
    parent. Renders nothing when clean; renders an amber 'Conflict'
    chip with tooltip + click-to-open-modal when overlapping.
  - ConflictFixDialog — shows the conflicting addresses, the
    proposed safe CIDR, and an 'Auto-fix to safe slot' button.
    Disabled when the pool has active allocations, with copy
    explaining why.

apps/web/src/hooks/use-mesh.ts
  useMeshPoolConflict(poolId), useAutoFixPoolConflict() mutation.

apps/web/src/lib/query-keys.ts
  poolConflicts(id) key.

End-to-end against the existing 'teste' pool on prod
====================================================

  curl /api/mesh/ipam/pools/<teste-id>/conflicts
  →
    conflictingAddresses: ['::1', '::2', '::3', '::4']
    proposedSafeCidr: '2804:1740:f:2000::100/120'

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(mesh): counter math, IPv6 enumerator, anti-exhaustion guard

Bugs the user surfaced testing carves on a /56 parent:

1. enumerateIPv6Addresses produced INVALID IPv6 for carved children.
   Old code: `${base}::1` where base="2804:1740:f:2000::100" yields
   "2804:1740:f:2000::100::1" — two `::` per RFC 4291 §2.2 is illegal,
   and Proxmox rejected the LXC create with
   'net0.ip6: invalid format - value does not look like a valid ipv6
   network configuration'. New code does the arithmetic in bigint
   (base + i) and compresses back via bigIntToIpv6(). Also bounds the
   enumeration by the pool's actual /N size — a /124 has 16 addresses,
   not 256.

2. calculateTotalAddresses was wrong twice:
   • /128 returned -1 (Math.pow(2, 0) - 2). Now: 1.
   • Any IPv6 /N < 120 capped at 65534. That made a /112 carve from a
     /56 parent show 65534/65534 on the parent — 'looks like 100% used'
     when the parent actually has 4.7e21 addresses. Now:
     /128 → 1, /N with bits<31 → exact, otherwise INT_MAX (display
     cap, the gap-finder uses bigint anyway).

3. Anti-exhaustion guard in carveSubPool: childPrefix - parentPrefix
   must be >= 8. Otherwise a single rent can take half of a /56 with
   one click and starve every other tenant. 8-bit delta caps the
   biggest rent at 1/256 of parent — for a /56 that's /64 (still
   2^64 addresses, plenty for any customer), for a /24 IPv4 it's /32
   (single host). UI dropdown now filters its predefined sizes by the
   same rule via sizesForParent().

End-to-end validation
=====================

LXC actually came up with valid IPv6 this time:
  Cluster on-teste2-v2 (rented from teste2 = ::100/120 child)
    requested → provisioning IP ::101/120 → configuring → active
    endpoint = [2804:1740:f:2000::101]:5432  (~3m53s total)
    Postgres protocol probe from real-IPv6 host: 'S' (alive, SSL).

Pool counters after fix (recomputed via SQL on prod):
  default /56  →   9 / 2,147,483,647   (was 5 / 65534)
  teste   /120 →   0 / 256             (was 0 / 254)
  teste4  /128 →   0 / 1               (was 0 / -1)
  teste5  /112 →   0 / 65,536          (was 0 / 65534, looked = parent)

Known follow-ups
================

- Storing IPv6 totalAddresses in an integer column truncates at
  INT_MAX (2.1B). Real /56 has ~4.7e21 addresses; for display purposes
  the cap is fine but operators querying the column shouldn't expect
  exactness for IPv6 prefixes shorter than /97. Move to bigint or a
  string representation if accurate operator dashboards become a thing.
- UI dropdown is still hardcoded — a more dynamic version would derive
  options from parent prefix delta steps (parent+8, +16, +24, +32, +64)
  rather than the predefined list, removing the need to keep them in
  sync as we add new parent sizes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(mesh): pin carving / counter / guard / conflict behavior

The 2026-05-15 testing session uncovered four classes of bugs that
were silent until carving was exercised at scale. Each has a test now
so a future refactor that breaks any of them fails loud.

ipam-engine.carving.test.ts — 25 unit cases
============================================

  enumerateIPv6Addresses
    - base ending in :: → consecutive valid IPv6 strings
    - carved-child base (offset away from ::) → no double-:: in output
      (the bug Proxmox rejected with 400 'invalid format')
    - bounded by pool size, not a flat 256

  calculateTotalAddresses
    - IPv4 /32 → 1   (was 2 pre-fix)
    - IPv4 /31 → 2   RFC 3021 point-to-point
    - IPv4 /30 → 2   (network + broadcast deducted)
    - IPv4 /24 → 254
    - IPv6 /128 → 1   (was -1 pre-fix)
    - IPv6 /120 → 256 (no IPv6 'broadcast' deduction)
    - IPv6 /112 → 65536
    - IPv6 /56  → INT_MAX cap (was 65534, made carves look like 100%)
    - IPv6 /96  → INT_MAX cap (column is integer)

  carveSubPool gap-finder
    - first /120 lands AFTER parent infra reservations (::1/::2/::3)
    - subsequent /120 carves skip past earlier children (deterministic)
    - /128 single-IP rents start at the unblocked ::0 then skip
      ::1/::2/::3 to land at ::4 for the next one
    - parent counter +1 per carve

  carveSubPool anti-exhaustion guard
    - IPv6 /56 → /64 REFUSED (delta 8 < required 16, the 'eats 1/256
      of parent in one click' case)
    - IPv6 /56 → /71 REFUSED (just under min delta)
    - IPv6 /56 → /72 ALLOWED (exactly min delta)
    - IPv4 /29 → /32 ALLOWED (delta 1 — small parents need a relaxed rule)
    - IPv4 /29 → /29 REFUSED (must be strictly smaller)

  detectPoolConflict
    - clean carved child → empty conflicts + null proposal
    - bad pool with parent allocations inside → reports the addresses
      and proposes the next aligned safe CIDR (the auto-fix proposal)

  autoFixPoolConflict
    - rebuilds the same-named child in the safe slot
    - refuses to fix when the pool has active allocations (no data loss)

Engine bug fix unblocked by the tests
=====================================

createPool's overlap check now skips the parent in the new pool's
parentPoolId — a carved child is *expected* to overlap its parent, so
the old greedy CIDR_OVERLAP check refused every carve under a small
IPv4 parent. Sibling carves still fail-fast on overlap (which the
gap-finder prevents by construction).

title: fix(atlas+mesh): unblock /128 pools, surface silent provisioner crashes, DNS-safe names (#43)
body:
fix(atlas+mesh): unblock /128 pools, surface silent provisioner crashes, DNS-safe names (#43)

End-to-end validated in prod 2026-05-16: user created a cluster pinning
network=teste6 (2804:1740:f:2000::301/128) via the new <NetworkSelect>
and watched the row sit in `status=requested` forever with zero logs.

Three orthogonal bugs combined to make the failure invisible:

1. mesh ipam-engine: `enumerateIPv6Addresses` skipped offset 0 for every
   prefix length, so /128 (one address) returned []. `reserveAddress`
   then threw POOL_EXHAUSTED on a pool with 0/1 allocated. Fix: when
   poolSize <= 1 (i.e. /127 and /128), start from offset 0. IPv6 has no
   broadcast and the network address of a small prefix is routable.

2. atlas service.ts: provisionAtlasCluster was dispatched as
   `.catch(() => {})`. Any throw before the first `[Atlas] Cluster X:
   provisioning` log (in getIPPool / detectPoolConflict / reserveAddress)
   was invisible — operators had to dig into pg_stat or guess. Fix: log
   the err with stack so the next failure is actionable.

3. atlas validation.ts + provisioner.ts: cluster names allowed any
   character via `z.string().min(2).max(64)`, but the name is embedded
   in the LXC hostname (`atlas-${name}-primary`) which Proxmox validates
   as RFC-1123. Names with `_` (eg. `teste-select_network`) accepted,
   then Proxmox 400'd "invalid format - value does not look like a valid
   DNS name". Fix: tighten the schema to DNS-safe regex AND sanitize
   defensively at hostname construction so legacy rows still create.

4. atlas service.ts (related): added `requested` + `provisioning` to
   `deletableStatuses` so stuck rows can be cleaned via the API/UI
   path instead of needing direct DB DELETE. Safe — those statuses
   imply no LXC nor allocation (the failure paths set rows to `failed`).

End-to-end check after fixes: created teste-select-network → status
transitioned requested → provisioning → configuring → active in 125s,
LXC 147 came up with IP 2804:1740:f:2000::301, pool teste6 now reads
1/1 allocated, and `nc 2804:1740:f:2000::301:5432` returns OK from
the hypervisor. NetworkSelect feature confirmed end-to-end.

title: fix(ui+atlas): dialog overflow + surface real error message from Atlas API (#42)
body:
fix(ui+atlas): dialog overflow + surface real error message from Atlas API (#42)

Two unrelated-looking issues with the same symptom: "I clicked the
button and nothing useful happened."

1. DialogContent had no max-h / overflow handling. Once a dialog grew
   past viewport height (eg. Atlas cluster-create after we added the
   Network field), the bottom content — including the footer with the
   submit button — was silently clipped. Many users reported "I don't
   see the field" when really the field rendered offscreen. Adds
   max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto so any dialog scrolls. Global-by-design
   so future field additions don't reintroduce the bug elsewhere.

2. Atlas API handleError swallowed every server-side error and returned
   "Internal server error" with no context. Cred creation goes through
   `pct exec` over SSH — if the chain fails (cluster unreachable, ssh
   key mismatch, postgres not started, etc.) the actual stderr from
   provisioner-base was logged to console but the operator only saw
   the generic message in the toast. Now surfaces err.message so the
   first line of failure reaches the UI. Stack traces / sensitive
   details still aren't returned (only the Error.message string, which
   is already non-sensitive in our provisioner paths).

body:
docs(atlas): resolve all 6 open decisions in v2 plan (#45)

User confirmed all 6 v2 design decisions on 2026-05-16:

1. Backup storage: THREE modes — Proxmox local + rsync (configurable
   target with ed25519 keypair flow) + download-only (one-shot link).
   Adds atlas_backup_targets table + Wave G now has 3 PRs.

2. DNS naming: `<safe-name>-<id-rand6>.db.developy.cloud` instead of
   the 4-level hierarchical scheme. Stable across cluster renames
   (suffix = cluster ID tail), no org/project leakage in public DNS,
   global uniqueness automatic.

3. Extension whitelist: 5 safe-and-easy defaults (pg_stat_statements,
   pg_trgm, pgcrypto, citext, hstore) instead of the 7-conservative
   proposal. postgis/pgvector/timescaledb move to admin-flagged tier.

4. Tier limits: full matrix added in §6.1.1 — databases/roles/firewall
   rules per cluster, backup retention/frequency, PITR availability,
   replicas, alert rules, extensions, rsync target count.

5. Sync vs async: always async + .catch error logging (the pattern
   shipped in PR #43). No special-case for destructive ops — the
   catch logger gives visibility.

6. MariaDB: postgres-first confirmed. MariaDB gets lifecycle only.

Also updates Wave E (DNS) provisioner snippet, Wave G (backups) to
3 PRs with full atlas_backup_targets schema + UI mockup, and Wave J
extension whitelist to match the new safe/admin split.

The §6.1 "Open decisions" table is now §6.1 "Resolved decisions"
with the rationale baked in. Next Claude session has no questions
to ask the user before starting Wave A.

title: fix(beacon): route record CRUD through DnsBackend so UI writes are visible (#55)
body:

POST/PUT/DELETE on /api/beacon/zones/:id/records used to write to the local
meta store and then attempt a best-effort sync to PowerDNS via the cluster
node's HTTP API. The GET path reads through the configured DnsBackend

backend appeared to succeed (201) but vanished on the next refresh — the UI
showed no error and the new record never appeared in the list.

Route record CRUD through getDnsBackend() when one is configured. The
legacy local-store path stays as fallback for the json-only dev mode.

through a MockDnsBackend.

title: fix(wpp): normalize media mimetype before file-storage upload
body:
fix(wpp): normalize media mimetype before file-storage upload

WhatsApp media mimetypes carry codec parameters (e.g. "audio/ogg; codecs=opus")
that fail file-storage's exact-match mime allowlist, so createFile was rejected
with a ZodError and wpp_messages.mediaFileId stayed null for every audio.

Strip parameters to the base type ("audio/ogg") before calling createFile, and
reuse the same normalized value for the presigned PUT Content-Type — the upload
URL is signed with that ContentType, so the two must match or S3 rejects the PUT.

Verified end-to-end (audio/ogg, image/jpeg, video/mp4 all stored). Does not
change the lazy on-demand download behavior.

body:
fix(ipam): collision-free LXC IPv4 allocation (scan in-use IPs)

Root cause of the 2026-06-08 mgmt-db outage: two independent allocators wrote
the same /24. `vmidToIp(vmid)=172.10.0.(vmid%256)` handed data-product LXCs IPs
already held by platform-static services — herald(151)→.151 collided with
atlas-mgmt-01, blaze(150)→.150 with developy-quickstart — intermittently
killing the control-plane store (ECONNREFUSED → atlas_clusters INTERNAL_ERROR).

- add `allocateLxcIp(node,vmid)`: scans cluster /cluster/resources + per-guest
  net configs for in-use last-octets, picks the first free one (pure
  `pickFreeOctet`, starts at vmid%256 for stable allocations, skips
  used+reserved+.0/.255). Falls back to vmidToIp on scan error.
- swap all data-product provisioners (spark/blaze/nexus/flux/ignite/herald/
  tide/beacon) from `vmidToIp` to `await allocateLxcIp`. Atlas untouched
  (uses the mesh pool).
- tests for pickFreeOctet (incl. the .151 regression).

This is the FAST fix. The durable design (data-products on IPv6 + single IPv4
ingress) is specced in docs/ipam-ipv6-migration.md.

title: fix(spark): pin reliable DNS so valkey/memcached install can resolve repos
body:
fix(spark): pin reliable DNS so valkey/memcached install can resolve repos

Spark cluster provisioning failed with "Could not resolve host:
packages.valkey.io". Root cause: createLxcContainer only sets the LXC
nameserver when config.nameserver is truthy, and Spark passes
process.env.DATA_PRODUCTS_NAMESERVER, which is unset on the deployed
control-plane — so the container inherited the node's ISP resolvers, which
fail for external package repos. (Atlas is unaffected: it sources nameservers
from the Mesh network pool, and Postgres needs no external repo.)

Two belt-and-suspenders fixes:
- Default the LXC nameserver to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 when DATA_PRODUCTS_NAMESERVER
  is empty.
- Pin /etc/resolv.conf inside the container before any apt/curl (valkey and
  memcached paths), so install is deterministic regardless of host config.

Repro: created operacao-digital-cache-stg (valkey-sentinel, xs) on sp1-sd-catalisatec-1
→ status=failed; Herald showed the curl resolve error on LXC 156.

body:
feat(create): mandatory network + IP selection on VM/CT create, via Mesh IPAM (#66)

Creating a VM/CT now requires picking a client network and gets a real IP,
reusing Mesh as the single source of truth — no parallel allocator.

UX (shared NetworkStep, used by both VM and Container wizards):
- <NetworkSelect> (existing) to pick a bridge-backed Mesh network — required
- IP auto-filled from the next free address (useSuggestIP), editable, with a
  live availability indicator (useCheckIPAvailability)
- "+ New" opens <CreateNetworkDialog> to generate a network inline (BYO CIDR or
  rent/carve), reusing useCreateMeshIPPool / useCarveSubPool — no leaving the flow

Allocation goes through Mesh IPAM exactly like the data products: on submit the
wizard reserves the IP (serviceId = `vm:<id>` / `ct:<id>`) and rolls the
reservation back if the Proxmox create fails. IP is applied as cloud-init
ipconfig0 (VM) or net0 ip=/gw= (LXC), with bridge/gateway/prefix derived from
the pool.

Mesh change (minimal, no new endpoint): createIPAllocation accepts infra
resource refs (`vm:`/`ct:`) — skipping the traffic-service existence check while
keeping all IPAM business rules — and an optional specific `address`
(reserveSpecificAddress) for the "pick your own IP" path. Traffic-service
allocations are unchanged. Covered by 2 new mesh-api tests; full mesh suite green.

title: fix(tags): sanitize Proxmox tags — colons/accents/spaces broke VM/CT create (#65)
body:
fix(tags): sanitize Proxmox tags — colons/accents/spaces broke VM/CT create (#65)

Auto-tags were built as `env:prod`, `role:web`, `depends-on:123`. The colon
is not a valid Proxmox tag character (default pve-tag style allows only
[A-Za-z0-9_+.-]), so every create/update with an env or role set was rejected
with "invalid format - invalid characters in tag" — failing by default, before
the user typed anything. Accents (produção) and spaces in custom tags hit the
same wall.

New lib/tags.ts sanitizeTag/sanitizeTags slugifies tags (strip accents, invalid
runs -> "-", trim edges). Applied at every tag write path: VM create, CT create,
VM/CT config edit, dependency tagging, and the TagEditor add handler (so the
badge shown matches what the API accepts). Unit-tested.

title: fix(spark+ipam): valkey DNS resolve + collision-free LXC IP allocation (#58)
body:
fix(spark+ipam): valkey DNS resolve + collision-free LXC IP allocation (#58)

* fix(spark): pin reliable DNS so valkey/memcached install can resolve repos

Spark cluster provisioning failed with "Could not resolve host:
packages.valkey.io". Root cause: createLxcContainer only sets the LXC
nameserver when config.nameserver is truthy, and Spark passes
process.env.DATA_PRODUCTS_NAMESERVER, which is unset on the deployed
control-plane — so the container inherited the node's ISP resolvers, which
fail for external package repos. (Atlas is unaffected: it sources nameservers
from the Mesh network pool, and Postgres needs no external repo.)

Two belt-and-suspenders fixes:
- Default the LXC nameserver to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 when DATA_PRODUCTS_NAMESERVER
  is empty.
- Pin /etc/resolv.conf inside the container before any apt/curl (valkey and
  memcached paths), so install is deterministic regardless of host config.

Repro: created operacao-digital-cache-stg (valkey-sentinel, xs) on sp1-sd-catalisatec-1
→ status=failed; Herald showed the curl resolve error on LXC 156.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ipam): collision-free LXC IPv4 allocation (scan in-use IPs)

Root cause of the 2026-06-08 mgmt-db outage: two independent allocators wrote
the same /24. `vmidToIp(vmid)=172.10.0.(vmid%256)` handed data-product LXCs IPs
already held by platform-static services — herald(151)→.151 collided with
atlas-mgmt-01, blaze(150)→.150 with developy-quickstart — intermittently
killing the control-plane store (ECONNREFUSED → atlas_clusters INTERNAL_ERROR).

- add `allocateLxcIp(node,vmid)`: scans cluster /cluster/resources + per-guest
  net configs for in-use last-octets, picks the first free one (pure
  `pickFreeOctet`, starts at vmid%256 for stable allocations, skips
  used+reserved+.0/.255). Falls back to vmidToIp on scan error.
- swap all data-product provisioners (spark/blaze/nexus/flux/ignite/herald/
  tide/beacon) from `vmidToIp` to `await allocateLxcIp`. Atlas untouched
  (uses the mesh pool).
- tests for pickFreeOctet (incl. the .151 regression).

This is the FAST fix. The durable design (data-products on IPv6 + single IPv4
ingress) is specced in docs/ipam-ipv6-migration.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

The "Rent from platform" mode hardcoded IPv4 child prefixes (/24../29) and

title: fix(create): drop per-NIC firewall (default off, remove toggle) — it breaks NAT egress (#68)
body:
fix(create): drop per-NIC firewall (default off, remove toggle) — it breaks NAT egress (#68)

The VM/Container create wizards defaulted firewall=1 on net0, which makes
Proxmox build a firewall bridge (fwbr) in front of the NIC. On this cluster
that fwbr breaks the NAT/conntrack path for the guest: the masquerade rule
matches but nf_nat never translates the source, so the packet egresses the WAN
bridge with its private IP and gets no reply — every wizard-created VM/CT lost
internet access (and the cicustom guest-agent install in PR #67 failed for the
same reason).

Confirmed empirically: a guest with firewall=1 has no egress; flipping it to
firewall=0 restores egress immediately (ping + https + apt). NAT itself is fine
(other internal guests without the firewall translate and reach the internet).

Cluster/node firewall is disabled here and traffic policy lives in Mesh, so the
per-NIC firewall provided no real filtering — only the broken NAT path. Remove
the firewall toggle from both wizards and never add firewall=1 to net0.

Co-authored-by: Klederson Bueno <klederson@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix(mesh): respect carve min-delta in network create child sizes (#71)
body:
fix(mesh): respect carve min-delta in network create child sizes (#71)

The inline network dialog offered child prefixes (e.g. IPv6 /60, /64) that the
carve engine rejects: it requires the child to be more specific than the parent
by at least MIN_DELTA bits — 1 for IPv4, 16 for IPv6 — within the family max.
So an IPv6 /56 parent needs at least /72, but /60 failed with
"Child /60 is too large for parent /56 (ipv6, min delta 16)".

childOptions now filters candidates by `child - parent >= minDelta` (and `<= max`),
matching the engine, so only carve-able sizes are shown (/56 → /72,/80,/96,…).

fix(mesh): suggestRandomAddress respects IPv6 prefix length (#72)

The IPv6 branch hardcoded a /56 layout (randomizing the 4th hextet + host),
so suggesting an address for a carved sub-pool produced an out-of-range IP —
e.g. a /72 pool 2804:1740:f:2000:100::/72 suggested 2804:1740:f:201f::… (in

title: fix(test): unwrap idempotent-migration guards for pg-mem (#79)
body:
fix(test): unwrap idempotent-migration guards for pg-mem (#79)

PR #75 made migrations 0013–0017 idempotent by wrapping CREATE TYPE / ADD
CONSTRAINT in `DO $$ BEGIN <ddl>; EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN null;
END $$;` and using IF NOT EXISTS. The pg-mem test harness strips ALL `DO $$ ...
$$` blocks (originally for migration 0010's data-cleanup PL/pgSQL), so the
wrapped CREATE TYPE was being removed — the enum type never got created and the
following `ADD COLUMN ... "mesh_ip_pool_source"` failed. This broke the
pg-mem-backed db tests (db.test, postgres-backend, store-backend).

Fix the sanitizer: before the blanket DO-block strip, unwrap the
duplicate_object guard blocks to their inner DDL (so CREATE TYPE / ADD
CONSTRAINT still apply) and drop the IF NOT EXISTS clauses (no-ops on a fresh
DB). Migrations are unchanged — they stay idempotent for prod.

Co-authored-by: Klederson Bueno <klederson@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix(create): push pool DNS servers to static-IP guests (VM + CT)
body:
fix(create): push pool DNS servers to static-IP guests (VM + CT)

E2e on real Proxmox surfaced a DNS gap once guests actually boot an OS: a
static-IP guest has no DHCP to learn DNS from, so it comes up with internet
reachable *by IP* but unable to resolve hostnames — apt, the guest-agent
install, everything by name fails. An IPv6-only guest is worse: it inherits
the host's IPv4 nameservers, which it can't even reach.

  nameservers (both template-clone and ISO paths).
- CT create: when the DNS field is left blank, default `nameserver` to the
  pool's servers instead of the host's (unreachable) resolv.conf.

cloudflare.com over IPv6, `curl https://one.one.one.one` → HTTP/2 200, and the
qemu-guest-agent auto-installs on first boot (Ubuntu 24.04). CT with pool
nameservers resolves DNS after the IPv6 servers land in resolv.conf.

title: fix(spark): deprovisioner must not swallow LXC delete failures (#78)
body:
fix(spark): deprovisioner must not swallow LXC delete failures (#78)

A failed `pct destroy` (e.g. the stale-dm `lvremove ... in use` case) was only
console.error'd; the cluster was then marked `deleted` and a `success` Herald
event emitted unconditionally — so the container survived as an untracked
orphan while the system reported the cluster gone. This is how the 2026-06-09
smoke left CTs 160/164/165/166 behind (docs/storage-and-node-placement.md §5).

Now: track which LXCs failed to delete; IP/DNS cleanup still runs best-effort;
but if any container survived, mark the cluster `failed` (a DELETABLE state, so
the delete can be retried — the stale-dm case needs a node reboot first), emit a
`failure` event with the orphaned vmids, and throw. Only a fully-removed cluster
becomes `deleted`/`success`. Mirrors the existing provision-failure path.

Adds a regression test (real JSON store + mocked Proxmox boundary).

title: feat(harbor): Phase 2a — Registry v2 token service (Aegis-backed) (#89)
body:
feat(harbor): Phase 2a — Registry v2 token service (Aegis-backed) (#89)

Implements the Docker Registry v2 token auth service so `docker login`/pull/push
authenticate against Aegis. No JWT dependency — RS256 + x5c signed with node:crypto.

- `registry-token.ts`: RS256 JWT signer (x5c header) + payload decode.
- `registry-scopes.ts`: parse Docker scope strings, namespace (=org) extraction,
  entitlement→granted-actions mapping (registry:pull/push/delete).
- `GET /api/harbor/token` (the registry `realm`): Basic-auth password = a platform
  bearer; resolves the subject's registry entitlements per namespace (baseline ∪
  IAM role) and issues a scoped JWT. Returns 503 until HARBOR_TOKEN_KEY/CERT set,
  so deploying this is inert until the registry is switched to token auth.
- `POST /api/harbor/registry-token`: mints a 24h `docker login` credential for the
  logged-in user (reuses issueSession, like the bun ship CLI token).
- IAM roles gain registry:pull/push/delete (viewer=pull, member=pull+push,
  admin/owner=+delete).
- Registry datasource: when the app holds the signing key it self-signs a short
  read token for server-side catalog reads, so switching the registry to
  `auth: token` won't break the Harbor UI.

Tests: 7 new (scope parsing, entitlement mapping, real RS256 signature verify).
Phase 2b wires the keys + flips the live registry (skopeo-verified) + ingress.

title: fix(spark): IPv6 cluster support — bind, DNS-probe timeout, no duplicate IPs (#97)
body:
fix(spark): IPv6 cluster support — bind, DNS-probe timeout, no duplicate IPs (#97)

* fix(spark): bind valkey/sentinel/memcached on IPv6 too (not 0.0.0.0-only)

A valkey-sentinel cluster created on an IPv6 Mesh pool failed at provisioning:
'Sentinel verification failed: connected_slaves:0'. The primary listened only on
0.0.0.0 (`bind 0.0.0.0`/`-l 0.0.0.0` = IPv4-only), so replicas — reaching it by
its IPv6 address — could never attach. Confirmed via ss -ltn inside the primary
(LISTEN 0.0.0.0:6379 only).

- valkey + sentinel: `bind * -::*` (all IPv4 AND IPv6; `-` makes the v6 bind
  non-fatal on IPv4-only hosts).
- memcached: `-l 0.0.0.0,::`.
Adds an IPv6 sentinelConf regression test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(spark): timeout DNS probe + delete LXCs on provision failure (no duplicate IPs)

Two issues surfaced validating IPv6 provisioning:

- aptSetup's wait-for-DNS used a bare `getent`, which hangs indefinitely when
  the (IPv6) resolver is unreachable — wedging the whole provision in
  'configuring' forever. Wrap each probe in `timeout 5` so the loop always
  completes and apt fails cleanly (caught) instead of hanging.

- On provision failure we released the Mesh IP allocations but left the created
  LXCs running. The next cluster then reserved the same 'freed' address while the
  orphan container still held it → DUPLICATE IP (two CTs on 2804:...::401), which
  broke IPv6 egress on the newcomer. Now: delete each LXC first, and release its
  allocation ONLY if the delete succeeded (a survivor keeps its IP reserved).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(spark): deprovision keeps IP reserved when LXC delete fails (stale-dm)

Same duplicate-IP guard as the provision-failure path, now on the delete path:
#78 released every Mesh allocation unconditionally, even for containers that
survived a stale-dm 'lvremove ... in use'. The surviving LXC still holds its IP,
so the next cluster could reserve the same address. Release only allocations
whose LXC was actually removed; keep the rest reserved until a node reboot frees
the container.

title: fix(beacon): SOA serial overflow from BIGINT-as-string concat (#107)
body:
fix(beacon): SOA serial overflow from BIGINT-as-string concat (#107)

* docs: Beacon DNS outage 2026-06-12 incident + runbook

Two root causes (not the VM): (1) systemd-resolved stole :53 from PowerDNS on
ns1 CT 123 → intermittent SERVFAIL; (2) SOA serial overflowed uint32 on
developy.cloud/io (record content + domains.notified_serial) → REFUSED.
Live fixes, preventive scan, and follow-ups (serial-gen code fix, dup ::10
decom, IPv4 glue, mask resolved in template).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(beacon): SOA serial overflow from BIGINT-as-string concat

node-postgres returns BIGINT (domains.notified_serial) as a string, so
bumpSerial's `oldSerial + 1` concatenated ("2026061201" + 1 → "20260612011")
instead of incrementing — appending a digit per zone mutation until the serial
blew past the 32-bit ceiling. PowerDNS then REFUSED the zone (developy.cloud,
developy.io), taking the platform domain + a tenant zone NXDOMAIN on 2026-06-12.

- add pure nextSerial() helper: coerce to number, cap at MAX_DNS_SERIAL,
  fall back to today's serial for corrupt/overflowed inputs
- coerce notified_serial reads in getDomain/listDomains
- sql-fake now returns notified_serial as a string (mirrors pg) so the
  regression is actually exercised
- unit tests for nextSerial + an end-to-end overflow regression test

Verified: reintroducing the bug fails the new e2e test; fix → 19/19 pass.
Incident write-up in docs/incidents/2026-06-12-beacon-dns-outage.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
