fix(banking-app): selfie pedida NO ENVIO do Pix — mesma intenção, mesma chave (#1724)

* fix(banking-app): selfie pedida NO ENVIO do Pix — mesma intenção, mesma chave

O bloco banking (building-blocks-v2 #518) passou a reconferir no envio o
acumulado do dia e a noite. Quando a intenção nasceu sem selfie e o envio
passa a exigir, `sendPix` responde BIOMETRIC_REQUIRED com
`details.stepUp: "selfie"` e `details.selfieTriggers`, antes do desafio e
da reserva: nada saiu, nada foi gasto. O app só dizia "a selfie não chegou,
refaça" e a pessoa perdia o fluxo.

Agora `confirmPix` abre a selfie sobre o MESMO hash (createBiometricSession
com o operationHash da intenção, a página do biometrics no WebView) e reenvia
a MESMA intenção com a MESMA chave de idempotência e a MESMA assinatura, mais
o biometricSessionId. A assinatura não é refeita: a selfie não entra nos bytes
assinados e o desafio segue vivo. Uma vez só por intenção. Se o desafio venceu
antes ou durante a selfie, gasta o crédito único de renovação (o caminho do
CHALLENGE_EXPIRED); a intenção nova já nasce pedindo selfie e não conta como
"mudou".

- banking-core: `OrchestrationError.stepUpEscalation`, `parseStepUpEscalation`,
  `stepUpEscalationOf`, `stepUpEscalationError`, tipo `SelfieTrigger`
- cliente HTTP lê `error.details`; servidor de referência o escreve
- ExampleOrchestrationClient simula a noite e o acumulado no envio
- tela de selfie diz o motivo: "valor acima do limite", "limite do dia",
  "noite"; a revisão passava RÓTULOS onde a tela espera CÓDIGOS, e o motivo
  nunca aparecia (corrigido também no cadastro de chave)
- selfie cancelada / reprovada: "Nenhum valor saiu da sua conta" e volta à
  revisão

body:
fix(banking-app): selfie pedida NO ENVIO do Pix — mesma intenção, mesma chave

O bloco banking (building-blocks-v2 #518) passou a reconferir no envio o
acumulado do dia e a noite. Quando a intenção nasceu sem selfie e o envio
passa a exigir, `sendPix` responde BIOMETRIC_REQUIRED com
`details.stepUp: "selfie"` e `details.selfieTriggers`, antes do desafio e
da reserva: nada saiu, nada foi gasto. O app só dizia "a selfie não chegou,
refaça" e a pessoa perdia o fluxo.

Agora `confirmPix` abre a selfie sobre o MESMO hash (createBiometricSession
com o operationHash da intenção, a página do biometrics no WebView) e reenvia
a MESMA intenção com a MESMA chave de idempotência e a MESMA assinatura, mais
o biometricSessionId. A assinatura não é refeita: a selfie não entra nos bytes
assinados e o desafio segue vivo. Uma vez só por intenção. Se o desafio venceu
antes ou durante a selfie, gasta o crédito único de renovação (o caminho do
CHALLENGE_EXPIRED); a intenção nova já nasce pedindo selfie e não conta como
"mudou".

- banking-core: `OrchestrationError.stepUpEscalation`, `parseStepUpEscalation`,
  `stepUpEscalationOf`, `stepUpEscalationError`, tipo `SelfieTrigger`
- cliente HTTP lê `error.details`; servidor de referência o escreve
- ExampleOrchestrationClient simula a noite e o acumulado no envio
- tela de selfie diz o motivo: "valor acima do limite", "limite do dia",
  "noite"; a revisão passava RÓTULOS onde a tela espera CÓDIGOS, e o motivo
  nunca aparecia (corrigido também no cadastro de chave)
- selfie cancelada / reprovada: "Nenhum valor saiu da sua conta" e volta à
  revisão

fix(iam): quem concede papel, recusa com rastro e quatro olhos para acesso sensível

Três furos de controle de acesso no iam, achados no console do backoffice do CBP
(painel #1750) e na auditoria do BaaS (G3).

1. Escalada de privilégio. Quem tinha gestão de acesso (IAM_MANAGER) dava ADMIN a si
   ou a outra pessoa. Agora (src/iam/authorization/access-guard.ts):
   - só concede ou tira um papel quem tem TODAS as permissões dele, comparado com o
     mesmo mapa que monta o token (teste roda a guarda ao lado de resolvePermissions
     para todo par de papéis);
   - ninguém altera os próprios papéis, nem root;
   - máquina (chave, M2M) não concede papel de pessoa, salvo a organização `dono`
     (como o painel provisiona o dono de um tenant novo);
   - não há rota de papel customizado/editar permissão; catraca falha se nascer.

2. Recusa sem rastro. Middleware auditAccessRefusals entre authMiddleware e
   requirePermission publica `*.refused` (association, mfa, access-request,
   access-policy, api-keys.key) com a organização do autor e o autor — nunca
   actorType sem userId, nunca o alvo em payload.userId.

3. Quatro olhos. Política por organização (organizations.access_approval_required,
   NULL = padrão da casa desligado, declarado como padrão; recomendação: ligado no
   CBP). Papel administrativo/financeiro, reset de segundo fator, chave com escrita e
   afrouxar a própria política viram pedido (iam.access_requests) que outra pessoa da
   organização aprova, com prazo de 24 h, reivindicação condicionada e trilha. Chave
   aprovada é resgatada só pelo autor; PATCH não amplia chave para escrita.

feat(baas): quórum de assinatura e alçada por representante (D-PJ2) (#550)

* feat(baas): quórum de assinatura e alçada por representante (D-PJ2)

Modo QUORUM na política de autorização: representantes com teto por operação,
teto diário, vigência e minSigners ("conjunta, n"), e quórum por faixa de valor
(n de m, ou "ALL" = todos em vigor). signingRules entra no policyHash só quando
existe — as políticas já ancoradas não mudam de hash.

Numa conta QUORUM nenhuma assinatura sozinha move dinheiro: Pix, TED e chaves
Pix (e a própria mudança de política) viram um pedido de assinatura que coleta
assinaturas de representantes DIFERENTES sobre o mesmo payload (tipo, conta,
id e nonce do pedido, params). Aprovação decidida no banco sob trava do
representante e do pedido; execução pelos mesmos serviços das rotas diretas,
com o portão reconstruindo o payload, reconferindo as assinaturas e
reivindicando a execução (APPROVED → EXECUTING condicionado): uma execução só.
Expira (varredura + na assinatura), recusa assinada, cancelamento, retomada
idempotente (a chave da transferência é o id do pedido). Trilha
baas.signing.request.* com catraca de recusa.

Fachada: requireSigningQuorum e enforcesQuorum (quorumGate) para o #547 trocar
a pausa de pix.send/pix.keys pelo quórum.

Testes de corrida contra Postgres real (8 casos; sem as travas e a
reivindicação condicionada, 4 falham).

title: feat(analytics): agregado diário e funil do Pix por coorte, com passos cegos e a invariante (M4)
body:
feat(analytics): agregado diário e funil do Pix por coorte, com passos cegos e a invariante (M4)

PRs 6 e 7 da spec analytics-funis-metricas-e-alertas. As telas passam a ter de onde ler, e nunca
do evento cru.

- `analytics_event_daily`: por organização, dono, dia (UTC do occurred_at) e evento, o total e uma
  linha por atributo declarado (enumeração, booleano, faixa): eventos, sujeitos e jornadas
  distintos no dia.
- `analytics_funnel_daily`: o funil POR COORTE — jornadas que começaram no dia e o desfecho delas
  dentro da janela. É o que faz a janela de conversão valer (quem conclui depois não converte) e a
  leitura sobreviver à retenção do cru.
- Funil declarado em código (`src/analytics/funnels/`). Pix por intenção, janela de 24 h:
  - passos cegos declarados (`key_lookup`, `amount`, `step_up_passed`): `null` e "sem
    instrumento", nunca 0 nem 100%; a conversão ponta a ponta vem `null` enquanto o denominador
    (do app) for cego;
  - exigência de selfie é passo próprio (opcional);
  - saídas separadas: recusa por política (por motivo), falha técnica, desconhecido e abandono;
  - invariante: passo com volume menor que o seguinte e desfecho sem início (órfão) marcam
    instrumentação quebrada, e a queda não é desenhada;
  - sessões abertas como contexto (outra unidade), nunca divididas.
- Agregação agendada (15 min, molde LockedPass): refaz do cru os dias que receberam evento desde o
  cursor (`received_at`), apagando e reinserindo numa transação com a trava da organização. Dia
  cujo cru já começou a vencer NUNCA é refeito: apagaria o agregado.
- `GET /analytics/api/v1/funnels[/:key]`: JWT ou chave, permissão nova `ANALYTICS_READ` (ADMIN e
  VIEWER), dono exato pelo crachá (analytics em SUBACCOUNT_AWARE), período em UTC até 92 dias.
- `banking.pix.transfer.failed` entra no catálogo (o banking já publica).
- Os eventos do `baas` ficam fora do funil: a transação dele não carrega a intenção. A menor
  mudança (o `baas` publicar o `businessId` = `banking:intent:<id>` que já grava) está proposta no
  README §12, não feita aqui.

Testes: unidade (precedência dos desfechos, passos cegos, saídas separadas, invariante, órfão,
coorte parcial, período, funil x catálogo, container); integração com Postgres e Redis reais, do
barramento à rota HTTP (sete intenções com desfechos diferentes, janela, órfão, subconta, outra
organização com parâmetro forjado, idempotência e duas passadas simultâneas, agregado intacto
depois do expurgo do cru e evento atrasado para dia vencido, 401/403/404/400).

fix(baas): o status só avança — webhook, consulta e KYC não rebaixam nem republicam

O handler de webhook gravava o status que o provedor dizia com `update`
incondicional e publicava a cada aviso. O README §14 dizia que a
reivindicação condicionada segurava o aviso repetido sem id de evento; no
webhook ela não existia. Consequências medidas em teste:

- dois avisos do mesmo Pix sem id de evento (Celcoin, QI Tech e FitBank não
  mandam) publicavam `baas.pix.transfer.completed` duas vezes;
- `created`/`failed` atrasado rebaixava um Pix já concluído (FAILED com o
  dinheiro fora);
- `kyc.approved` atrasado reativava conta BLOCKED e ressuscitava conta CLOSED;
  reenviar KYC pela rota fazia o mesmo;
- `GET /pix/transfers/:id` (BAAS_READ) devolvia a COMPLETED um Pix recebido já
  estornado, porque no banco a ENTRADA continua concluída.

Agora as escritas de status usam `advanceStatus` (updateMany condicionado à
tabela de `utils/status-transitions.ts`) e só quem vira publica. A busca da

title: fix(iam): MFA lock holds under parallel guesses; reset confined to single-org users; challenge consumed once
body:
fix(iam): MFA lock holds under parallel guesses; reset confined to single-org users; challenge consumed once

Adversarial review of #525:

- Lock bypass by parallelism: the lock was read before evaluating and the failure counted
  after, so a burst of N concurrent guesses (one challenge each; the IP rate limit trusts
  X-Forwarded-For) had all N evaluated. Each answer now reserves an attempt with a
  conditional UPDATE before matching; the (max+1)-th request of a burst is refused unread.
- Reset across organizations: the factor belongs to the person and protects every org, but
  any admin whose org the user is linked to could reset it — and an admin can link any user
  into their own org. Non-root admins now reset only users who belong to no other org, never
  a root account, and never by API key.
- Challenge single use: consume() now reports whether it deleted the challenge; the loser of
  two concurrent second steps gets no session.

The desktop session still never moves money: it only creates a request
(createDesktopOperation, write, no signature). The phone lists it with amount,
recipient and key, opens the Pix intent FROM THE ROW through the same
createPixIntent, signs the canonical BaaS payload and sends with the same

  DesktopOperationRequestRepository: conditional transitions, intent swap
  bound to the previous intent_id, unique intent_id, unique idempotency key
  per desktop session
- PixIntentRepository.abandon (PENDING -> FAILED, conditional): refuse,
  cancel and intent swap race sendPix and exactly one wins
- 6 routes (create/get/cancel from the desktop, intent/refuse from the
  phone, desktop sessions list); getPixContacts, lookupPixKey, getDevices
  and signOutDesktop now reachable by the desktop session (read or
  privilege-reducing only); getPendingApprovals merges access and operations
- signOutDesktop cancels pending operation requests
- banking.desktop.operation.* events; every refusal is published
- unit tests (memory DB) and real-Postgres race tests; README section 7.4

feat(template-builder): remote build host tooling and a single fleet-wide template GC

Templates were built on the developer's machine, where the build died at

  both nodes after publishing, cleanup of image and tarball on exit. Exports
  LXC_TEMPLATE_KEEP=1000 to neutralise retention embedded in older commits.

  skipped while a build runs.
- template-gc.sh: the one place that removes templates from the nodes, for
  every family. In use = templateRef or runningTemplateRef across all Launch
  projects; fail closed globally and per family; keeps the 5 newest unused and
  anything younger than 72h; removing is moving to a 7-day trash; an in-use
  template absent from a node fails the run.
- workflows: build-template (dispatch + reusable) and template-gc (daily,
  report-only until TEMPLATE_GC_APPLY=true), both on the template-builder runner.

  inFlightAmount).

  valor volta); timeout/5xx → fica PENDING e segue contando (#516).

Três furos de controle de acesso no iam, achados no console do backoffice do CBP
(painel #1750) e na auditoria do BaaS (G3).

1. Escalada de privilégio. Quem tinha gestão de acesso (IAM_MANAGER) dava ADMIN a si
   ou a outra pessoa. Agora (src/iam/authorization/access-guard.ts):
   - só concede ou tira um papel quem tem TODAS as permissões dele, comparado com o
     mesmo mapa que monta o token (teste roda a guarda ao lado de resolvePermissions
     para todo par de papéis);
   - ninguém altera os próprios papéis, nem root;
   - máquina (chave, M2M) não concede papel de pessoa, salvo a organização `dono`
     (como o painel provisiona o dono de um tenant novo);
   - não há rota de papel customizado/editar permissão; catraca falha se nascer.

2. Recusa sem rastro. Middleware auditAccessRefusals entre authMiddleware e
   requirePermission publica `*.refused` (association, mfa, access-request,
   access-policy, api-keys.key) com a organização do autor e o autor — nunca
   actorType sem userId, nunca o alvo em payload.userId.

3. Quatro olhos. Política por organização (organizations.access_approval_required,
   NULL = padrão da casa desligado, declarado como padrão; recomendação: ligado no
   CBP). Papel administrativo/financeiro, reset de segundo fator, chave com escrita e
   afrouxar a própria política viram pedido (iam.access_requests) que outra pessoa da
   organização aprova, com prazo de 24 h, reivindicação condicionada e trilha. Chave
   aprovada é resgatada só pelo autor; PATCH não amplia chave para escrita.

* feat(iam): TOTP second factor with recovery codes, two-step login and amr claim

- Two-step login: right password + factor owed returns an opaque short-lived

  tested against Postgres); 5 wrong codes lock the factor for 15 min.
- Admin reset of another user's factor with mandatory reason, refresh tokens
  revoked; self reset refused; mfaEnabled removed from PATCH /users/:id.
- iam.mfa.* events mapped in the audit trail (resource user_mfa); no secret,
  code or recovery code in events or logs.

* fix(iam): MFA lock holds under parallel guesses; reset confined to single-org users; challenge consumed once

Adversarial review of #525:

- Lock bypass by parallelism: the lock was read before evaluating and the failure counted
  after, so a burst of N concurrent guesses (one challenge each; the IP rate limit trusts
  X-Forwarded-For) had all N evaluated. Each answer now reserves an attempt with a
  conditional UPDATE before matching; the (max+1)-th request of a burst is refused unread.
- Reset across organizations: the factor belongs to the person and protects every org, but
  any admin whose org the user is linked to could reset it — and an admin can link any user
  into their own org. Non-root admins now reset only users who belong to no other org, never
  a root account, and never by API key.
- Challenge single use: consume() now reports whether it deleted the challenge; the loser of
  two concurrent second steps gets no session.

feat(analytics): agregado diário e funil do Pix por coorte, com passos cegos e a invariante (M4) (#536)

* feat(analytics): agregado diário e funil do Pix por coorte, com passos cegos e a invariante (M4)

PRs 6 e 7 da spec analytics-funis-metricas-e-alertas. As telas passam a ter de onde ler, e nunca
do evento cru.

- `analytics_event_daily`: por organização, dono, dia (UTC do occurred_at) e evento, o total e uma
  linha por atributo declarado (enumeração, booleano, faixa): eventos, sujeitos e jornadas
  distintos no dia.
- `analytics_funnel_daily`: o funil POR COORTE — jornadas que começaram no dia e o desfecho delas
  dentro da janela. É o que faz a janela de conversão valer (quem conclui depois não converte) e a
  leitura sobreviver à retenção do cru.
- Funil declarado em código (`src/analytics/funnels/`). Pix por intenção, janela de 24 h:
  - passos cegos declarados (`key_lookup`, `amount`, `step_up_passed`): `null` e "sem
    instrumento", nunca 0 nem 100%; a conversão ponta a ponta vem `null` enquanto o denominador
    (do app) for cego;
  - exigência de selfie é passo próprio (opcional);
  - saídas separadas: recusa por política (por motivo), falha técnica, desconhecido e abandono;
  - invariante: passo com volume menor que o seguinte e desfecho sem início (órfão) marcam
    instrumentação quebrada, e a queda não é desenhada;
  - sessões abertas como contexto (outra unidade), nunca divididas.
- Agregação agendada (15 min, molde LockedPass): refaz do cru os dias que receberam evento desde o
  cursor (`received_at`), apagando e reinserindo numa transação com a trava da organização. Dia
  cujo cru já começou a vencer NUNCA é refeito: apagaria o agregado.
- `GET /analytics/api/v1/funnels[/:key]`: JWT ou chave, permissão nova `ANALYTICS_READ` (ADMIN e
  VIEWER), dono exato pelo crachá (analytics em SUBACCOUNT_AWARE), período em UTC até 92 dias.
- `banking.pix.transfer.failed` entra no catálogo (o banking já publica).
- Os eventos do `baas` ficam fora do funil: a transação dele não carrega a intenção. A menor
  mudança (o `baas` publicar o `businessId` = `banking:intent:<id>` que já grava) está proposta no
  README §12, não feita aqui.

Testes: unidade (precedência dos desfechos, passos cegos, saídas separadas, invariante, órfão,
coorte parcial, período, funil x catálogo, container); integração com Postgres e Redis reais, do
barramento à rota HTTP (sete intenções com desfechos diferentes, janela, órfão, subconta, outra
organização com parâmetro forjado, idempotência e duas passadas simultâneas, agregado intacto
depois do expurgo do cru e evento atrasado para dia vencido, 401/403/404/400).

body:
feat(banking-console): access control area — people, roles × permissions, machine credentials, four-eyes, organization and trail (#1750)

The owner's 24/09 decision: the backoffice exposes access control as its
own area. Every rule stays in the blocks (iam, api-keys, audit-trail); the
console reads, asks and shows the refusal.

Bridge
- The closed table reaches four blocks (baas, iam, api-keys, audit-trail),
  each at its own URL and prefix. api-keys and audit-trail URLs are
  optional: without them those tabs answer 503 AREA_UNAVAILABLE.
- Operations that need the organization declare sessionOrg ('path' or
  'body'); the bridge puts the BADGE's organization in after reading the
  session (withSessionScope). The browser still cannot send one: scope keys
  are refused anywhere in the request, path params only take UUIDs.
- 13 new ops: accessOrganization, listMembers, listRoles, createPerson,
  grantRole, activatePerson (status 'ativo' only), revokeRole (DELETE with
  body), resetSecondFactor (reason >= 5), listApiKeys, apiKey, createApiKey
  (allowedResources REQUIRED — without it api-keys mints an unrestricted
  key), revokeApiKey, listAccessTrail (resourceType required).
- Per-op refusal phrases for the iam's code-less 409/403; 204 becomes 200 {}.

Screens (/access/*)
- People: role, second factor, last login, status; invite = create ->
  grant -> activate, resumable from the failed step with the same person;
  temporary password generated in the browser and shown once.
- Person: change role (grant new before removing old), reset another

body:
feat(banking,biometrics): review dossier — applicant data and 5-min media for the human review desk

The human reviewer of an INCONCLUSIVE opening selfie needs to see who applied and what the
machine saw. Two person-only, audited reads, both POST with a mandatory reason:

- banking: POST /admin/opening-reviews/:biometricSessionId/applicant — the data declared in the
  opening draft (pii_cipher): full name, birth date, e-mail, masked phone, masked CPF, step, state
  and deadline. Never the CPF in clear.
- biometrics: POST /sessions/:id/review-media — 5-minute read-only presigned URLs for the document
  photo, the portrait extracted from it, the best selfie frame and the challenge video. DISCARD
  retention, purged media and missing evidence answer 200 with the reason and no URL.

Rules in both: BIOMETRICS_ADMIN and a PERSON (API key, client_credentials and the internal
block token are refused with 403); organization/subaccount only from the token (other org = 404);
every access publishes banking.onboarding.pii.viewed / biometrics.review.media.viewed (who, why,
which fields/pieces, never values or URLs) BEFORE responding — trail down = 503 and nothing leaves;
every refusal publishes *.refused. Cache-Control: no-store.

Supporting changes:
- file-storage download-url accepts expiresIn (30..3600 s) that only shortens PRESIGNED_URL_EXPIRY;
  the facade passes expiresInSeconds.
- credentialKindOf moved to @shared/utils/credential-kind (biometrics review reuses it).
- audit mapper: biometrics.review.* points at the biometrics_session.
- DI: BiometricsReviewService (#554) was resolved via @Service() with constructor deps and no
  Container.set — the DI ratchet flagged it BROKEN (the build emits no decorator metadata). It and

The host builds many times a day for several sessions at once. This makes the

build-template.sh (client): fila, cancelar; joins an existing run for the same
commit and family; shows what is ahead with an estimate; refuses to queue on

title: feat(decision-engine): executar a decisão-FOLHA do DRG, não decisions.first()
body:
feat(decision-engine): executar a decisão-FOLHA do DRG, não decisions.first()

A execução direta de política (decision.service) chamava o runner sem
decisionKey. O runner então usa `decisions.first()` — e o Camunda reordena as
decisões no parse, então "first" não é a primeira do XML e, num DRG, costuma ser
uma dependência, não a decisão que o chamador quer. Resultado: um DMN
multi-decisão rodava/simulava a decisão errada (uma não-folha) e nunca mostrava
o desfecho final.

findLeafDecisionId(dmnXml) acha a folha (decisão que nenhum requiredDecision
aponta) e a passamos como decisionKey; o runner então encadeia as dependências
(DmnExecutionService.kt:89-94). Modelo de 1 decisão: a única é a folha. Folha
ambígua (nenhuma ou várias) → undefined, mantém o comportamento do runner.

Parse por regex de propósito (conteúdo DMN confiável, sem puxar parser XML pro
hot path). 6 testes unitários.

fix(deploy-guard): find the running commit through refs/pull/*/head

Templates are built from any pushed commit and PRs are squash-merged. Once

title: fix: the bot survives a real-disk volume, login refuses an empty body, and the AI path gets a real smoke
body:
fix: the bot survives a real-disk volume, login refuses an empty body, and the AI path gets a real smoke

Three leftovers of the 'copilot stopped' front.

The meeting bot's entrypoint copied the profile seed with one `cp -a`. A
volume that is a real filesystem (Launch's is) comes with `lost+found`, which
not even the root of an unprivileged LXC can read: the copy failed, `set -e`
killed the container, and it restarted forever. The seed is now copied item by
item, without `lost+found`, and an unreadable cache file no longer costs the
session. It says so when the seed brings no session.
`entrypoint.selftest.sh` proves it without Chrome or audio, and fails on the
old entrypoint.

`POST /auth/login` took an inline type the ValidationPipe cannot see, so a body
without `email` reached Prisma as `undefined` and came back as a 500. It now
has a DTO: a missing field is a 400.

`scripts/smoke-painel-prod.sh` is the real smoke of the AI path in production —
assistant, agents, video copilot, knowledge index, link bot — 31 checks against
the live API on a demo account, credentials read from outside the repo.

title: feat(ai-insights): motor de análise por IA genérico + Insights/Agentes do Decision
body:
feat(ai-insights): motor de análise por IA genérico + Insights/Agentes do Decision

Um subsistema de análise por IA desacoplado, reutilizável por qualquer
vertical, e o primeiro consumidor dele: as telas Insights e Agentes de
análise do console do Decision.

## Motor genérico (`ai-insights`)
Módulo novo, cego ao domínio. `AnalysisRunnerService` roda um agente sobre
dados que o chamador montou, mede contra um saldo de créditos por ciclo e
guarda o histórico — tudo por uma chave opaca `(context, ownerKey, cycleKey)`
que o motor nunca interpreta. Usa o `ai-core` (LLMProviderFactory) para a
chamada ao LLM (CatalisaAI/Claude por padrão), pede uma saída JSON estruturada
e tolera resposta fora do formato (guarda o texto cru). Uma corrida que falha
entra no histórico como FAILED e NÃO é cobrada. Tabela/ledger `AiAnalysis`
(migração aditiva e idempotente).

## Decision: Insights + Agentes de análise (adaptador fino)
- Catálogo `DECISION_AGENTS` (4 agentes: desfechos, carteira, política, resumo
  executivo) com custo e gate por plano — catálogo interno, agentes sob medida
  são roadmap.
- Franquia mensal de créditos por plano (`aiCredits`: 20/100/500/2000/10000),
  no mesmo ciclo civil da cota e da fatura.
- `DecisionInsightsService`: resolve conta→franquia→ciclo, monta só o dado que
  o agente escolhido lê (via métodos públicos do portal) e chama o motor. As
  análises do Decision rodam na chave do fornecedor, pagas por créditos.
- 5 rotas no controller + 5 ops fechadas no BFF + telas `Insights.tsx` e
  `Agentes.tsx` no console (grupo "Inteligência" na sidebar).

## Mesmo motor como action de workflow (`AI_ANALYZE`)
Prova do desacoplamento: o handler `AI_ANALYZE` reusa o MESMO runner, mas paga
com a credencial do próprio tenant (como os demais handlers de IA), sem gate de
crédito. Registrado como os outros (barrel, registry, módulo, schema de
validação).

49 testes: motor (8), adaptador (8), catálogo (6), handler (4), planos (18), +
console (21) e BFF (6) inalterados e verdes.

title: perf(lxc): templates build in a fraction of the time — COPY --chown and rootfs straight from the build
body:
perf(lxc): templates build in a fraction of the time — COPY --chown and rootfs straight from the build

Where the minutes went in a panel-runtime build (measured 02/10/2026): 2m19s
in 'exporting to image' and 2m05s in 'chown -R /app' out of 5m15s.

- api and worker Dockerfiles: the user is created before /app and each COPY
  carries --chown. The worker assembles its /app in a stage of its own
  (lxc-deps) so it can be copied with ownership instead of chowned afterwards.
- scripts/build-lxc-template.sh: the rootfs comes straight out of the build
  (--output type=tar) instead of image → docker create → docker export.

Checked file by file against the old rootfs (name, owner, mode):
- api: 65949 entries, zero differences.
- worker: /app identical (23909 entries); the only difference is that
  /root/.cache/prisma — the CLI's download cache, 51 MB left behind by running
  'prisma generate' inside the rootfs stage — is no longer shipped.
The tar exporter differs from docker export only in what docker create
injects (/.dockerenv, dev/console, dev/pts, dev/shm, empty etc/hostname,
etc/hosts, etc/resolv.conf).

A causa raiz de "os ícones do modeler somem" NÃO era cache nem o bundler: o CSP
do hotsite-kit tinha `font-src https://fonts.gstatic.com` — só fonte do Google.
A fonte de ícones do dmn-js (self-hosted + base64) era barrada em silêncio, então
NENHUM ícone (paleta, lápis, arrastar, glifo do nó) renderizava.

body:
fix(ai-insights): resolver a credencial de IA pelos settings do usuário (nada hardcoded)

A LLMProviderFactory RECUSA a chave crua do ambiente de propósito: um call roda
numa credencial do sistema de credenciais. O runner chamava getProvider() sem
credencial quando o chamador não passava uma (o caminho medido/pago pelo
fornecedor, ex.: Decision) — e a factory recusava com "este usuário ainda não
tem credencial de IA", derrubando toda análise.

Agora o runner, quando não recebe `userCredential`, resolve pelo
`UserLlmCredentialResolver` a partir de um `resolveForUserId` que o chamador
passa: a credencial que o usuário escolheu nos settings → a do dono → a de
plataforma `catalisa-ai-<provider>`, com o PROVIDER vindo dos settings do
próprio usuário. NADA hardcoded (sem "anthropic" fixo, sem chave de env).

O adaptador do Decision passa como `resolveForUserId` o DONO da vertical
DECISION, que é CONFIGURÁVEL em `SystemSettings.codePortalOwnerUserIdByVertical`
— não um id fixo. A análise roda nos settings de IA desse dono; o cliente nunca
paga o modelo (o saldo de créditos paga).

Dependência de INSTALADOR: o dono da vertical precisa ter uma credencial de IA
utilizável (própria, ou a de plataforma `catalisa-ai-<provider>`). Sem ela a
análise falha graciosa (FAILED, sem cobrar). Injeções @Optional; testes que dão
`new` seguem passando (+ testes de resolveForUserId).

fix(deploy-guard): find the running commit through refs/pull/*/head (#567)

Templates are built from any pushed commit and PRs are squash-merged. Once
the PR branch is deleted, the commit a block runs is reachable only through
refs/pull/<n>/head, which `git fetch origin` does not bring even with
fetch-depth: 0. Guard 0b then refused every following deploy with "commit
desconhecido", and the only way out (--ignorar-migrations) turned off the
migration check for the whole fleet.

refs/deploy-guard/ so it does not flood `git branch -r`. Test: a commit
reachable only by refs/pull/7/head on a bare origin (red before, green after).

body:
fix(iam): close two four-eyes bypasses found in review

- With the rule on, changing the password or e-mail of ANOTHER person holding a
  sensitive role is refused (403 CREDENTIAL_CHANGE_FOUR_EYES), except root and the
  `dono` operator key. An ADMIN could set the other approver's password, log in as
  them and approve their own POLICY_RELAX; the weaker MFA reset already became a
  request (MFA_RESET), the password did not.
- PUT access-policy goes back to assertOrgAccess (person of the org, or root). Through
  the `dono` key the POLICY_RELAX request was authored by the platform key's user, so
  SELF_APPROVAL never matched the person who asked from the panel and the trail showed
  the platform. GET still accepts the operator key (count only).

title: feat(iam): four-eyes rule configurable by the account admin without trapping a single-admin org
body:
feat(iam): four-eyes rule configurable by the account admin without trapping a single-admin org

- Turning the access-approval policy ON requires at least 2 eligible approvers (distinct people
  who could decide POLICY_RELAX: active, already signed in, not root, same canonical e-mail counts
  once). Fewer -> 409 APPROVERS_INSUFFICIENT, refused on the trail.
- Turning it OFF with 2+ approvers still becomes a POLICY_RELAX request. With fewer it applies
  immediately, with reason 'single_approver' on iam.access-policy.changed — only by a person who
  holds the permission NOW in the database, root or the platform (dono) key.
- Turning it off (immediately or by approved request) CANCELS the org's PENDING requests, with
  iam.access-request.cancelled (cancelReason 'policy_disabled'). Approved key requests stay.
- Closes the "remove the other approver, then disable alone" shortcut: with the rule on, revoking
  or swapping a role, deactivating, deleting or re-e-mailing a user cannot take the org from 2+ to
  fewer than 2 approvers (409 APPROVER_QUORUM_PROTECTED); only root bypasses.
- Deciding a request re-checks the approver in the database (token permissions intersected with
  current roles): an admin removed while the request waited cannot approve with the old token.
- GET access-policy returns eligibleApprovers (count only), minApprovers, canEnable and
  canDisableImmediately; GET/PUT also accept the platform (dono) key for any org, so the panel can
  offer the toggle to the tenant's account admin.

title: fix(iam): serialize approver-quorum check and write per organization
body:
fix(iam): serialize approver-quorum check and write per organization

Two concurrent removals each saw 3 approvers and both passed, leaving 1 who
could then turn the rule off alone (10/10 in review). Removing/swapping a role,
deactivating, changing e-mail, deleting a user and turning the rule on/off now
check and write under pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(org)), held by a transaction
that stays open until the write lands. The lock is tried (not awaited) so a waiter
never holds a pool connection while the holder needs another to write; busy for
10 s -> 409 APPROVER_QUORUM_BUSY.

The new integration race test fails without the lock (all four removals pass)
and passes with it.

title: feat(iam): regra de quatro olhos configurável sem prender a org de um admin só (#579)
body:
feat(iam): regra de quatro olhos configurável sem prender a org de um admin só (#579)

* feat(iam): four-eyes rule configurable by the account admin without trapping a single-admin org

- Turning the access-approval policy ON requires at least 2 eligible approvers (distinct people
  who could decide POLICY_RELAX: active, already signed in, not root, same canonical e-mail counts
  once). Fewer -> 409 APPROVERS_INSUFFICIENT, refused on the trail.
- Turning it OFF with 2+ approvers still becomes a POLICY_RELAX request. With fewer it applies
  immediately, with reason 'single_approver' on iam.access-policy.changed — only by a person who
  holds the permission NOW in the database, root or the platform (dono) key.
- Turning it off (immediately or by approved request) CANCELS the org's PENDING requests, with
  iam.access-request.cancelled (cancelReason 'policy_disabled'). Approved key requests stay.
- Closes the "remove the other approver, then disable alone" shortcut: with the rule on, revoking
  or swapping a role, deactivating, deleting or re-e-mailing a user cannot take the org from 2+ to
  fewer than 2 approvers (409 APPROVER_QUORUM_PROTECTED); only root bypasses.
- Deciding a request re-checks the approver in the database (token permissions intersected with
  current roles): an admin removed while the request waited cannot approve with the old token.
- GET access-policy returns eligibleApprovers (count only), minApprovers, canEnable and
  canDisableImmediately; GET/PUT also accept the platform (dono) key for any org, so the panel can
  offer the toggle to the tenant's account admin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(iam): close two four-eyes bypasses found in review

- With the rule on, changing the password or e-mail of ANOTHER person holding a
  sensitive role is refused (403 CREDENTIAL_CHANGE_FOUR_EYES), except root and the
  `dono` operator key. An ADMIN could set the other approver's password, log in as
  them and approve their own POLICY_RELAX; the weaker MFA reset already became a
  request (MFA_RESET), the password did not.
- PUT access-policy goes back to assertOrgAccess (person of the org, or root). Through
  the `dono` key the POLICY_RELAX request was authored by the platform key's user, so
  SELF_APPROVAL never matched the person who asked from the panel and the trail showed
  the platform. GET still accepts the operator key (count only).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(iam): serialize approver-quorum check and write per organization

Two concurrent removals each saw 3 approvers and both passed, leaving 1 who
could then turn the rule off alone (10/10 in review). Removing/swapping a role,
deactivating, changing e-mail, deleting a user and turning the rule on/off now
check and write under pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(org)), held by a transaction
that stays open until the write lands. The lock is tried (not awaited) so a waiter
never holds a pool connection while the holder needs another to write; busy for
10 s -> 409 APPROVER_QUORUM_BUSY.

The new integration race test fails without the lock (all four removals pass)
and passes with it.

title: fix(credentials): BB key under four-eyes returns PENDING_APPROVAL and can be redeemed
body:
fix(credentials): BB key under four-eyes returns PENDING_APPROVAL and can be redeemed

With the iam four-eyes policy on (building-blocks-v2 #549), POST /api-keys with a
write scope answers 202 with an access request and no key. generateBbApiKey read
`data.key` from it and returned `key: undefined`, and the credential modal toasted
"API Key gerada" over an empty field (staging, 06/10, org b0000000-...-0001).

API
- generateBbApiKey returns {status:'ISSUED', key, keyId, prefix} or
  {status:'PENDING_APPROVAL', requestId, expiresAt}; a 2xx without key (or a 202
  without request) is now a 502, never a success.
- POST /credentials/redeem-bb-key/:requestId calls from-request with the caller's
  own token (BB enforces author-only, once, 24h); BB refusal codes become pt-BR.
- Every outcome goes to the log and to AccessLog (BB_API_KEY_ISSUED / _PENDING_APPROVAL
  / _GENERATE_FAILED / _REDEEMED / _REDEEM_REFUSED), with id and prefix only — the
  key never reaches log or trail.
- merchant-bb and credit-blocks-bb no longer store a credential with an undefined
  key when the request is pending; they refuse with an explanation.

Front
- CredentialModal shows the approval notice and a "Resgatar a chave" button that
  fills the field; the success toast only fires with a real key. The pending request

body:
fix(credentials): chave do BB com quatro olhos — PENDING_APPROVAL + resgate (#1774)

* fix(credentials): BB key under four-eyes returns PENDING_APPROVAL and can be redeemed

With the iam four-eyes policy on (building-blocks-v2 #549), POST /api-keys with a
write scope answers 202 with an access request and no key. generateBbApiKey read
`data.key` from it and returned `key: undefined`, and the credential modal toasted
"API Key gerada" over an empty field (staging, 06/10, org b0000000-...-0001).

API
- generateBbApiKey returns {status:'ISSUED', key, keyId, prefix} or
  {status:'PENDING_APPROVAL', requestId, expiresAt}; a 2xx without key (or a 202
  without request) is now a 502, never a success.
- POST /credentials/redeem-bb-key/:requestId calls from-request with the caller's
  own token (BB enforces author-only, once, 24h); BB refusal codes become pt-BR.
- Every outcome goes to the log and to AccessLog (BB_API_KEY_ISSUED / _PENDING_APPROVAL
  / _GENERATE_FAILED / _REDEEMED / _REDEEM_REFUSED), with id and prefix only — the
  key never reaches log or trail.
- merchant-bb and credit-blocks-bb no longer store a credential with an undefined
  key when the request is pending; they refuse with an explanation.

Front
- CredentialModal shows the approval notice and a "Resgatar a chave" button that
  fills the field; the success toast only fires with a real key. The pending request
  id (never the key) survives closing the modal.

SEND_TYPING liga o indicador na conversa da mensagem recebida e o mantém vivo
(re-envio a cada 20 s; a Meta apaga em 25 s). Desliga no primeiro destes:
CANCEL_TYPING, uma mensagem SAIR para a conversa (conferido no banco a cada volta —
vale para agente, SEND_MESSAGE, template e envio pela tela, em qualquer réplica) ou
o teto de 300 s. O fluxo não lida com segundos: `timeoutSeconds` só reduz o teto.

Conversa, mensagem e device saem do gatilho de mensagem recebida: no atendimento o
nó não tem configuração. Nunca derruba o workflow. Só Cloud API por enquanto
(Baileys registrado como não suportado, sem erro). Depende do BB
POST /wpp-business/api/v1/messages/typing (building-blocks-v2, feat/wpp-biz-typing-indicator).

title: fix(network): scope port forwards to the host's own addresses
body:
fix(network): scope port forwards to the host's own addresses

DNAT rules were written without a destination match, so a forward for
public port N also rewrote container-to-container traffic to port N on the
bridge. On 09/10/2026 the Scylla forward --dport 8112 -> 172.10.0.112:9042
was hijacking Traefik's connections to a hotsite listening on
172.10.0.231:8112, which answered 500 for weeks; about twenty other forwards
on the node had the same reach.

- dnatSpec adds -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL (every address the host owns,
  nothing else; no per-node config).
- parseDnatRules flags rules without a destination match as unscoped.
- The reconciler rescopes a wanted legacy rule (scoped rule added first,
  legacy copy removed after, so the port never goes dark); on by default,
  rescopeLegacy:false turns it off.
- Deletes remove both shapes, so a deprovision cannot leave the legacy
  rule behind.

title: feat(launch): path-prefix routing per custom domain
body:
feat(launch): path-prefix routing per custom domain

A Launch service's customDomains entry can now be a bare host (as before)
or {host, paths}: only those path prefixes of the host reach the service,
so two services can share one hostname (e.g. api.operacao-digital.ai /waitlist /kb on
the hotsite API, everything else on the app API).

- ingress/traefik: optional explicit router priority; prunePublicRoutes
  removes a service's stale route files by prefix.
- provisioner: bare hosts stay on launch-<id>; each path-scoped domain gets
  launch-<id>-p<n> with PathPrefix and priority 10000, written before the
  main router; stale path routers are pruned on every finalize and removed
  on stop / delete / no healthy replicas / no HTTP. All routers share the
  same cert subjects, so no extra ACME order per host.
- launch-domains: pure helper (split / normalize / parse / text form).
- validation: both shapes accepted on create and POST /services/:id/domains;
  paths match traefik's safePath guard, 1-10 per host.
- postgres adapter + migrate-stores read both shapes back from the jsonb.
- UI: domains card and create dialog take `host /path /path`; detail page
  renders path entries instead of [object Object].

title: fix(launch): native redeploy keeps the volume's data
body:
fix(launch): native redeploy keeps the volume's data

A native rolling redeploy deleted each replica's LXC before creating the
new one, and the Launch volume (mp0) is a disk owned by that LXC, so every
redeploy brought the service back with an empty volume (operacao-digital-site,
/srv/operacao-digital, on 2026-10-09).

With a volume, the rebuild now stops the old guest, creates the new one
without a disk of its own, reassigns the old mp0 to it before the first
boot (POST /nodes/{node}/lxc/{vmid}/move_volume with target-vmid and
target-volume=mp0), and only then deletes the old guest. If the move or
anything after it fails, the disk is moved back and the old replica is
restarted with its row; if moving it back fails, the new guest is kept
stopped. Nothing that holds the volume is deleted on a failure path, and
the rollout stops with a statusMessage saying where the data is.

The escorted single-replica flow uses the same rebuild for replica 0; the
temporary replica's fresh volume is destroyed with it. Services without a
volume rebuild exactly as before. A pinned vmid (baseVmid) plus a volume
is refused before anything is touched, since the new guest cannot take
back the id while the old one still holds the disk.

Also fixes the comment that claimed the mount point survives a redeploy.

feat(hotsites): one Launch template for every public hotsite (hotsite-runtime)

The hotsites run on hand-made LXC guests (CT 140/141/142/143/154/306). This
adds the template family that lets them run as Launch native services instead:

- deploy/lxc/hotsite/Dockerfile: builds all six sites (`node build.mjs`) from
  the commit, scans dist/ for secrets, boots every site from the built tree
  (rehearse.mjs: healthz, pt home, en home, real 404 per language) and only
  then lays the tree on Debian + systemd as `lxc-rootfs`.
- hotsite@.service + hotsite-start: the instance picks the site
  (`hotsite@agora` -> /srv/apps/agora, env in /etc/bb/agora.env); the
  launcher drops the guests' *_DIST paths and points COUNTER_FILE at the
  unit's StateDirectory. Same sandbox the guests run with.
- apps/med/server/index.mjs: med has no BFF; this reproduces the Caddyfile
  contract (try_files, real 404 per language, the three 301s with the query
  kept, nosniff/referrer headers, gzip, etag) so med runs from the same
  template. Covered by server.test.mjs; the Caddy guest is unchanged.
- build-lxc-template.sh: `--only hotsite-runtime` (opt-in; a panel build
  does not build hotsites). Built only on the build host, like every family.

O adaptador de cartão salvo (`BbSavedCardPaymentMethod`) nomeava a vertical
e a tabela: lia e gravava o cliente do provedor em `biometricsAccount`, abria
o cadastro com o dono da vertical BIOMETRICS e marcava as cobranças com

vertical BIOMETRICS"; em produção, onde o Biometrics tem dono, salvaria e
cobraria pelo vendedor errado. Achado no smoke da tela de cartões.

- a origem da cobrança vem da vertical; sem `bindTo`, o adaptador recusa

title: fix(tide): credential path takes mc from the mirror, verified
body:
fix(tide): credential path takes mc from the mirror, verified

Creating a Tide credential ran
`which mc || curl -sSL https://dl.min.io/... -o /usr/local/bin/mc`.
dl.min.io answers 410 since 09/2026, so on an instance without mc that
line saved the error page as the binary, and `which mc` then found it
forever. Production has such an instance today (ct 301).

ensureMcCommand() tests `mc --version` instead, downloads from
TIDE_MC_URL with -f, checks sha256, runs --version, and only then moves
the file into place. With no mirror configured it fails naming the
variables, and no credential is issued.

Also adds scripts/ops/tide-minio-mirror.sh --conferir, a read-only check
of whether production can provision a new Tide instance.

- linha do tempo (abertura, vereditos, espera e resultado da aprovação).

Tudo lido do que a conta já tem (execução, esteira, política). Cada painel
carrega sozinho e some se não puder ser lido — o caso nunca fica bloqueado.

feat(code-portal): mais de uma pessoa por conta; a Mesa do Decision assina com a pessoa

Com um login por conta, um veredito acima do limite de alçada nunca podia
ser aprovado pela tela: o quatro-olhos pede uma segunda pessoa, e ela não
tinha como existir (decisão 4 do dono, 10/10).

- `CodeAccountMember` (migration aditiva): e-mail próprio, papel
  ADMIN/ANALYST, convite por link de escolher senha (7 dias, uso único).
- Login tenta o membro quando o e-mail não é de titular; mesma resposta
  genérica e mesmo custo de bcrypt. O token do membro leva `member`.
- `CodePortalGuard`: token de membro só passa em rota marcada com
  `@PortalMembers`, e o membro é conferido no banco a cada pedido. As
  outras verticais continuam fechadas para membros.
- Um e-mail entra em um lugar só; ninguém é apagado (REMOVED mantém o nome
  atrás do que a pessoa assinou).

Decision:
- O console inteiro abre para membros; plano, cartão, chaves, lista de
  pessoas e as regras das filas da Mesa ficam com titular e administradores.
- A Mesa assina com a pessoa: titular = código da conta (como antes),
  membro = `<código>/<id>`. O painel devolve os nomes (`people`) e a tela
  mostra nome, não código.
- Rotas e tela "Pessoas" (convidar, papel, novo link, remover) e o aceite

title: fix(baas): simulated provider grant publishes before it writes; nothing is ever undone
body:
fix(baas): simulated provider grant publishes before it writes; nothing is ever undone

Final review round for #600: the "undo" made revocation fail open and let a
grant be visible before it was confirmed.

One rule: the trail may have one record too many, never one too few, and
state never goes back.

- Grant: the id is generated first, the event is published with it, and the
  row is inserted only after the publication is confirmed. No confirmation
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_TRAIL_UNAVAILABLE with the table untouched, so
  isAllowed never sees an unconfirmed grant. Insert failing after the event
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_NOT_RECORDED. Idempotent PUT publishes nothing.
- Revocation: active grant ids are read, the event is published with them,
  and only then revokedAt/revokedBy are written (loop and 409 STILL_GRANTED
  kept). No confirmation -> 503 with no row touched; the organization stays
  granted and the caller is told so.
- undoGrant, undoRevoke and the deleteMany are gone: the grant table never
  loses a row and no row is reactivated. "My rows" are no longer recognised
  by revokedAt + revokedBy.
- Emergency path: DELETE ...?force=true (platform operator only) writes the
  revocation without a confirmed publication, logs at error level with
  operator, organization and grant ids, and answers trail: 'unconfirmed'.
- Tests cover the reviewer's sequences (slow-trail revoke vs a second DELETE,
  revoke/grant/revoke interleaving, grant with the trail down never allowed,
  concurrent PUT during the wait) and both force outcomes. README updated.

title: fix(baas): simulated provider grant — revoke every active grant, no act without a trail event, operator events never reach client webhooks
body:
fix(baas): simulated provider grant — revoke every active grant, no act without a trail event, operator events never reach client webhooks

Review follow-up for #600.

- Revocation revokes ALL active grants of the organization and only answers
  204 when none is left (409 if one was granted again meanwhile). The code no
  longer relies on the partial unique index: scripts/launch/2-verificar.sh
  checks the table and the index, and prisma/pre-db-push.sql records that the
  index must not be dropped there (db push keeps it — measured in the
  integration test).
- Grant and revocation only confirm when the trail publication confirms.
  There is no outbox in this repo, so on failure or timeout the act is undone
  (the grant row is removed / the revocation is reverted) and the answer is
  503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_TRAIL_UNAVAILABLE, with an error log. The gate
  refusal stays best effort for the event and no longer holds the 403.
- webhooks-engine: explicit operator-only prefix list
  (baas.simulated-provider.) that is never delivered to client subscriptions;
  the audit trail still receives it. No other event changes delivery.
- audit-trail: `revoked` maps to UPDATE only for
  baas_simulated_provider_grant; device and mandate revocations are unchanged.
- auditHoldRoute takes a scope label so platform routes log "operação de
  plataforma"; hold routes keep their text.
- Tests: platform router in the refusal-audit turnstile, API key case with the
  real requirePermission, two active grants, publication failure/timeout.
- README: what is guaranteed for the trail, where each refusal lands (401 is
  log only), and the known limits (credentials.sandbox on real providers; no
  check for an active real provider on grant).

title: fix(webhooks): platform operator events never reach a client webhook
body:
fix(webhooks): platform operator events never reach a client webhook

Measured on staging (2026-10-11): `baas.simulated-provider.grant.*` reached a
client webhook (`baas.*` subscription) with `actorId`, `grantedBy` and
`operatorOrganizationId` in the payload. An orphan webhooks-engine replica on

* fix(baas): simulated provider grant publishes before it writes; nothing is ever undone

Final review round for #600: the "undo" made revocation fail open and let a
grant be visible before it was confirmed.

One rule: the trail may have one record too many, never one too few, and
state never goes back.

- Grant: the id is generated first, the event is published with it, and the
  row is inserted only after the publication is confirmed. No confirmation
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_TRAIL_UNAVAILABLE with the table untouched, so
  isAllowed never sees an unconfirmed grant. Insert failing after the event
  -> 503 SIMULATED_PROVIDER_NOT_RECORDED. Idempotent PUT publishes nothing.
- Revocation: active grant ids are read, the event is published with them,
  and only then revokedAt/revokedBy are written (loop and 409 STILL_GRANTED
  kept). No confirmation -> 503 with no row touched; the organization stays
  granted and the caller is told so.
- undoGrant, undoRevoke and the deleteMany are gone: the grant table never
  loses a row and no row is reactivated. "My rows" are no longer recognised
  by revokedAt + revokedBy.
- Emergency path: DELETE ...?force=true (platform operator only) writes the
  revocation without a confirmed publication, logs at error level with
  operator, organization and grant ids, and answers trail: 'unconfirmed'.
- Tests cover the reviewer's sequences (slow-trail revoke vs a second DELETE,
  revoke/grant/revoke interleaving, grant with the trail down never allowed,
  concurrent PUT during the wait) and both force outcomes. README updated.

Review of #1863. The package declared a factory "1.3.0" derived from the 1.2.1
in the code, so installing it replaced a table the desk had edited with the
default one, in silence.

  publish a declared version under a newer published one, stops on a published
  version whose name is not a number, and answers the snapshot of the version
  the engine runs — read from the engine, or null with the reason — never one
  of a table it does not execute. This changes every package with creditBlocks;

  declared version that never reached the tenant becomes a pendência;

feat(packages): feature flags of a package — registered with the tenant key, turned on with the installer's token (slice 3)

A package now declares the feature flags it needs (`featureFlags`: key, state, name, description and
the house prerequisites it waits for), one declaration per key over the closure, and the installer
registers and turns them on in the tenant's organization as its LAST step.

Read in the blocks repo: `banking` evaluates `products.receivables` and `credit.contract` as
capabilities and treats "not registered" as off; a flag is born off; turning it on is publishing, which
the tenant's key is refused on purpose (403) and the account's main user carries in the token. So:
- register, list and read back: the tenant's machine key (a sub-user and a script register too);
- turn on: the token of who installs, and only that.

Rules:
- order: after the credit blocks and the policy pointers; when an earlier step failed or the pointers
  are not in the policy yet the step is `skipped` (new status) and no flag is touched;
- prerequisite: the showcase flag is turned on at installation; the CONTRACTING flag declares
  `requires: ['house-policy']` and is turned on only when the policy was read and has creditor, market
  place and the disbursement account — the reinstall after the house fills them turns it on;
- what the house decided is not undone: the block keeps no readable history, so a flag the installer
  created and has not turned on carries a sentence in its description, removed when it is turned on;
  off WITHOUT it is the house's and is never turned on;
- who cannot turn on (script without a token, sub-user, 403): `needs-input` with its own code and who
  can — never a failure; block down: `failed` in a strict package (409), `degraded` in a default one;
- what should be on is read back as a consumer reads it.

Also: the `feature-flags` block joins the tenant-key probe, and the dead routes are fixed — the
workflow actions and the assistant's tools called `/api/v1/feature-flags/...`, which matches no route
of the block (`/feature-flags/api/v1/flags/...`, `/feature-flags/api/v1/evaluate/:key`). One contract
(routes, module prefix recomposed when the base lacks it, answer parsing) is now shared by the
installer's client, the three actions and the three tools, with a ratchet against the old path.

`receivables-banking-channel` declares both flags. Nothing here ran against the real block.

  confirmation, one outcome per block (APPLIED | ALREADY | CONFLICT | REFUSED | UNAVAILABLE |
  NOT_REQUESTED) written on the row; a refusal never leaves as a success. Revoking only records it.
- `GET /workflow-templates/packages/:slug/operator-grant` for the tenant: the host and what is missing,
  never the reason nor who granted.
- A minimal form on the client's admin page.

  THIS organization, answers, and serves THIS tenant (each with its own code and who acts). The fact in
  the block decides, not the panel's row: an organization whose host already works passes without one.

  credential.

  is on is ever turned off.

Adversarial review of PR #1871: one blocker, two important, four minor.

   answered, and the attempt's outcome went over the previous one. A `PANEL_ADMIN` who is not an
   operator, repeating a grant that stood, became "who granted" with a 403; a refused attempt undid a
   recorded revocation; and a repetition with the block down turned APPLIED into UNAVAILABLE, which let a
   SECOND host be bound. Now the row keeps three different things apart:

   cannot; a revocation recorded on the panel changes nothing there.

title: fix(packages): only what is provably the same flow is switched off as a copy — review of #1865
body:
fix(packages): only what is provably the same flow is switched off as a copy — review of #1865

The first version of the new copy rule (same triggers + same action names) switched off things that
were not copies. Two blockers found by the adversarial review, both fixed here:

1. Reinstalling a template switched off the INSTALLED workflow of another template of the catalogue
   with the same triggers and action names (vehicle × property release deadline, the three
   appointment reminders): only the last one installed kept working.
2. A duplicate the house reconfigured (a second WhatsApp number, another text) was switched off by an
   ordinary reinstall, and the new copy could be born without the number.

The rule now:
(a) a workflow with an installation record of ANY template is never a stray copy;
(b) switched off: (i) the installer's name ("X" / "X (importado)") on the same triggers, exactly as
    before this PR — it is what cleans a tenant restored with an earlier version of the template —
    and (ii) an EXACT duplicate of the installed copy (same triggers and actions with the same
    configuration, device, credentials, agents; a webhook with its own slug is not one);
(c) same structure with another configuration is never switched off: reported on named `event`
    triggers as `OTHER_ACTIVE_COPY_ON_SAME_EVENT` — `needs-input` in a default package, `failed`
    (409) in a strict one;
(d) a structure shared by more than one template of the catalogue is not attributed to any;
(e) a reinstall nobody asked for (another active copy, no `force`) inherits device, credentials,
    agents and the on/off state of the installed workflow;
(f) catalogue ratchet: the three groups of look-alike templates are a declared list.

Also: the same-event warning only for triggers of type `event` that name their event; the request's
references are checked on the single-template route too, only for what will be used, with a message
for platform staff that says how to install on behalf of a customer; copy candidates are read once
per installation; the credit policy field of a house pendência goes in the step (`field`, one code
per pendência) instead of vanishing.

Copy rules are specified on the real catalogue and the real service over an in-memory tenant
(`workflow-templates.copies.spec.ts`). Plan updated: the rule, the pre-existing sub-user defect, the
feature-flag routes the panel calls and the block does not serve, and the slice 3 decision (turn
flags on with the installer's JWT).

    installing reads (they stay in the step key/code, the probes and the log); testing the
    `credit-blocks-bb` credential uses the real probe of the three credit blocks and answers in

A6. The pending key-request marker is left out of `GET /credentials` unless the Credentials screen

feat(packages): o pacote registra e liga as flags do app; corrige rotas mortas de feature flag (fatia 3) (#1866)

* feat(packages): feature flags of a package — registered with the tenant key, turned on with the installer's token (slice 3)

A package now declares the feature flags it needs (`featureFlags`: key, state, name, description and
the house prerequisites it waits for), one declaration per key over the closure, and the installer
registers and turns them on in the tenant's organization as its LAST step.

Read in the blocks repo: `banking` evaluates `products.receivables` and `credit.contract` as
capabilities and treats "not registered" as off; a flag is born off; turning it on is publishing, which
the tenant's key is refused on purpose (403) and the account's main user carries in the token. So:
- register, list and read back: the tenant's machine key (a sub-user and a script register too);
- turn on: the token of who installs, and only that.

Rules:
- order: after the credit blocks and the policy pointers; when an earlier step failed or the pointers
  are not in the policy yet the step is `skipped` (new status) and no flag is touched;
- prerequisite: the showcase flag is turned on at installation; the CONTRACTING flag declares
  `requires: ['house-policy']` and is turned on only when the policy was read and has creditor, market
  place and the disbursement account — the reinstall after the house fills them turns it on;
- what the house decided is not undone: the block keeps no readable history, so a flag the installer
  created and has not turned on carries a sentence in its description, removed when it is turned on;
  off WITHOUT it is the house's and is never turned on;
- who cannot turn on (script without a token, sub-user, 403): `needs-input` with its own code and who
  can — never a failure; block down: `failed` in a strict package (409), `degraded` in a default one;
- what should be on is read back as a consumer reads it.

Also: the `feature-flags` block joins the tenant-key probe, and the dead routes are fixed — the
workflow actions and the assistant's tools called `/api/v1/feature-flags/...`, which matches no route
of the block (`/feature-flags/api/v1/flags/...`, `/feature-flags/api/v1/evaluate/:key`). One contract
(routes, module prefix recomposed when the base lacks it, answer parsing) is now shared by the
installer's client, the three actions and the three tools, with a ratchet against the old path.

`receivables-banking-channel` declares both flags. Nothing here ran against the real block.

* feat(packages): the installer publishes the app's terms and configures the app's profile; contracting waits for the app being able to open an account (slice 6)

`cmsContent` and `bankingProfile`, generic fields of a package, with the session of the person installing
(the tenant key does not reach `cms` or `banking`, on purpose):

- `cms-content`: the space and the legal documents the app asks the customer to accept. The channel package
  brings ONLY the three demonstration notices the staging script publishes, word for word, marked in the
  version (`demo-2026.10`), and they are written and published only while the organization's bank is the
  simulated one, as the BaaS step resolved it. With a real bank nothing is published in the house's name:
  the step waits for the house's terms, or only checks the ones it already published. The installer only
  writes a document that does not exist; anything different is kept and reported. A release is only
  published over a space nobody else published (publishing a release publishes the whole draft).
- `banking-profile`: the app is pointed at the content space when it points at none, and the channel of the
  verification code comes from the house as inputs (`otpSenderId`, `otpTemplateName`, `otpLanguageCode`).
  The `banking` block has no platform default for it; without a channel the step is `needs-input`. A channel
  the profile already has is only replaced with a confirmation per field.
- `banking-onboarding`, a new generic prerequisite: required terms published in the space the profile points
  at, and a channel for the code. `credit.contract` waits for it; the showcase does not.
- `tenant-block:cms` / `tenant-block:banking`: the preflight checks the address only (public health route).
- `banking` and `cms` in `bb-endpoints.ts` (`BANKING_BB_BASE_URL`, `CMS_BB_BASE_URL`), added to the versioned
  env files.

Four corrections from the staging smoke of slice 5:

- an account informed in the request is only written with a confirmation by field (the BaaS does not say who
  the holder is), and any sign of a customer's account refuses it;
- the "account kept after the creditor changed" warning persists across installations: the panel keeps the
  creditor the account was opened or confirmed for;
- `packageInputs.applied` lists `fundAccountId` when the informed account is written;
- `BAAS_FUND_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` says the two ways out.

Nothing changes for packages that declare neither field (catalogue ratchet).

Not proven against the real blocks: local tests over a `cms` and a `banking` in memory that follow the rules
read in building-blocks-v2 a88aeca7. Two decisions are left for the owner and recorded in the plan: the model
texts of the terms, and a shared sender for the verification code.

* fix(packages): review of slice 6 — demo notices never count as the house's terms, the app's keys, the code channel checked where it sends, and the installer's organization

Adversarial review of PR #1869 (one blocking, five important):

1. A demonstration notice is never read as "the house's terms". With a bank that is not the simulated one,
   a required document the installer published (in the record, or with the package's key and version, or the
   package's very text) makes the step `needs-input` (`CMS_DEMO_TERMS_ON_REAL_BANK`) and does not count for
   `banking-onboarding`. Nothing is unpublished.
2. A release is only published over a space the installer created (this call, or an earlier one by the
   record) or over the release it published. A space that was already there, published or not, gets the
   documents as a draft (`CMS_RELEASE_NEEDS_THE_HOUSE`).
3. "Terms published" means the keys the app asks for: every document of the package required in the current
   release and no other required one (`CMS_APP_TERMS_KEYS_MISMATCH` says what is missing and what is extra).
4. The verification code's channel is checked in `wpp-business` with the installer's token before it is
   written, and the one already in the profile too: the number is the organization's and active; the
   template exists in that number's account, is an authentication one, approved, in that language. One code
   per reason; not checked is not met. New client `shared/wpp-business/wpp-business-channel.client.ts`.
5. The organization of the token is compared with the organization of the tenant's key before any call with
   the token: the provider configuration the key resolved is read with the token in the BaaS (404 = another
   organization). Different: `BANKING_ONBOARDING_INSTALLER_NOT_OF_THIS_ACCOUNT`, no block called, nothing
   written. Without a resolved bank the app steps wait; a closure that declares `cmsContent` or
   `bankingProfile` without `baasProvision` is a catalogue defect.
6. Plan and handoff: the two new variables are a mandatory step before the deploy, staging first, and
   `BB_WPP_BUSINESS_BASE_URL` has to be present.

Minor: the profile is read again right before the write (the block has no conditional write); a fund-account
record without creditor says "not known" instead of nothing; the two app steps say the same thing about
where the house acts; limits recorded in the plan.

Also, from the slice-5 smoke: a reinstall with nothing to change no longer writes the policy document (the
pointers were rewritten every time because of the "seeded at" stamps: 4 -> 16 versions in six reinstalls).

body:
feat(banking-channel): first request of a not-enabled assignor goes to the desk; approving enables (slice 8, channel part)

The account holder created by the bank app is born without the fund manager's
enablement, and the channel refused NOT_HABILITATED before the analysis, so the
decision table's "not enabled -> desk" rule was unreachable from the app.

- A product may declare `enablement: 'desk-on-first-request'` (read from the
  catalog, never by slug). With it, and only on the product declared for the
  bank channel, the request is analysed as "not enabled" and lands on the desk.
  Without it the refusal stays exactly as it was.
- The desk's decision route (`decideQueueItem`) enables the assignor when it
  APPROVES a proposal the engine held (ANALISE_MANUAL) with the recorded input
  `decisaoInput.habilitado === false`, in a product that declares the
  parameter. Refusing does not enable; a proposal the engine refused never
  does (A20 untouched); A17 still runs first. No installed workflow changes.
- While not enabled, one request under review at a time: a second one is
  refused with APPLICATION_UNDER_REVIEW and no analysis is enqueued (atomic
  slot in the ledger + the proposal waiting for the desk).
- Trail events and logs for the forwarded request, the refusal and the
  enablement.
- Package `receivables-banking-channel`: the product declares the parameter
  and version 1.1.0 for new tenants. An existing tenant keeps 1.0.0 (the seed
  only publishes when there is no version) and gets the key on the product's
  live parameters when the package is reinstalled; the channel reads it there.

Jest (local, container): credit-desk, credit-catalog, credit-identity, the
package and the receivables/credito-base custom actions: 69 suites, 851 tests.
tsc -p tsconfig.build.json and check:di clean. Not exercised in any
environment.

title: fix(packages): the unsettled-host lock is only armed and lifted by what the block says about the host; reserved platform labels (review of #1871, round 2)
body:
fix(packages): the unsettled-host lock is only armed and lifted by what the block says about the host; reserved platform labels (review of #1871, round 2)

1. The lock that keeps a second host out while a first attempt got no answer was armed by anybody
   (the attempt was written before the block answered) and lifted by a 401/403, which says nothing about
   the host. It now lives in its own column (`unsettledHost`): only no-answer (5xx, timeout) arms it,
   only an answer of the block ABOUT the host settles it (200, 409, 400/404), and a 401/403 puts it back
   as it was. Since, with the block down, anybody through the panel's door can leave a host pending,
   the operator has an explicit way out that does not bind it: `discardUnsettledHost`, typed, recorded
   (`discarded*`) and said for what it is — the discarded host may have stayed bound in the block. The
   409 no longer tells anybody to bind the pending host: it offers both ways out.
2. In the Launch the panel's `*_URL` variables are mesh addresses, so the computed list held no public
   host: `banking-product-portfolio`, `banking-console` and `banking-desktop` went through, and the
   screen SUGGESTED `banking-console…` for an organization whose slug is `console`. An explicit list of
   reserved labels is added to the computed one, the service name is derived from mesh hosts
   (`bb-<name>` → `<name>`), and the suggestion is never a reserved host (`-app` is appended).
Also: the screen no longer shows "granted by" when nothing stands any more; the plan records the
follow-ups (history table, the migration changed after its first version — check the table does not
exist before applying).

body:
fix(bureaus): mask the subject in the MOCK raw payload; grant reason goes to the operator event (bureaus and baas) (#606)

* fix(bureaus): mask the subject in the MOCK raw payload; grant reason goes to the operator event (bureaus and baas)

Two findings, same area.

1. The simulated bureau provider (`MOCK`) returned `raw.subject` with the whole
   document. `raw` is persisted as-is in `bureau_queries.raw` and
   `bureau_cache.raw` and is returned by default (`includeRaw: true`), so the
   block that "never stores the document in clear" stored it, and so did
   whoever kept the envelope. `raw.subject` is now the mask (same as
   `subject.masked`), on FOUND and NOT_FOUND. `profile`/`forced`/`kind`/
   `generatedFrom` are unchanged. The `includeRaw` default does NOT change:
   the panel reads the raw BigDataCorp envelope.

2. The reason of a simulated-provider grant never reached the audit trail:
   `<block>.simulated-provider.grant.created` carried `grantId`, `grantedBy`,
   `grantedAt` but not `reason`, and after a revoke the `GET` no longer shows
   it. The event now carries `reason` in `bureaus` and in `baas`. This reverses
   the earlier "reason stays in the row only" choice, with the guards that
   make it safe: the event is a platform-operator event (own stream, only the
   audit trail reads it, never a customer webhook), the text is capped at 500
   and the SAME trimmed/capped text goes to the event and the row, it is not
   logged, and a reason carrying something CPF/CNPJ-shaped is refused with
   400 `SIMULATED_PROVIDER_REASON_HAS_DOCUMENT` (route and service) before
   anything is published or written.

`@shared/utils/free-text-document` holds the document-shape check.

Not changed: rows already written keep the old `raw.subject` until retention
or cache expiry; the canonical `person.basic`/`company.basic` still carry
`taxId` (type contract); the revoke event does not repeat the reason.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(bureaus,baas): grant reason stays out of the target organization's trail; MOCK raw drops the seed; document check covers spaces, hyphens and alphanumeric CNPJ

Review follow-up on #606.

- MOCK `raw` no longer carries `generatedFrom`: it is a 32-bit seed derived
  from the document, and next to the masked subject it gives the document
  back by brute force in seconds. Profiles and data are unchanged.
- The grant `reason` is free text written by the platform operator, and the
  audit trail has no read-time redaction (masking happens on write, and the
  chain covers what was written): whatever is stored under the target
  organization is readable by that tenant through `GET /audit-trail/api/v1/logs`.
  So `…simulated-provider.grant.created` (target organization) no longer
  carries it. The reason goes in its own event,
  `…simulated-provider.grant.reason.recorded`, stored under the OPERATOR's
  organization, with `grantId` and `targetOrganizationId`. Both events are
  confirmed before the grant row is written (503 and nothing recorded
  otherwise). Without an operator organization the reason stays on the grant
  row only, with a warning in the log. Same change in `bureaus` and `baas`.
- `containsDocumentNumber` accepts space and hyphen as separators in the
  document grouping and recognises the alphanumeric CNPJ (uppercase, letters
  and digits mixed). Phone numbers in a phone shape pass; a bare 11-digit
  number is still refused — verifying check digits would let mistyped
  documents through.
- READMEs (bureaus, baas, audit-trail) say where the reason lives and who can
  read it.

title: fix(bureaus): baseUrl de fornecedor real só em host oficial em produção (lista de hosts, falha fechada) (#607)
body:
fix(bureaus): baseUrl de fornecedor real só em host oficial em produção (lista de hosts, falha fechada) (#607)

* fix(bureaus): provider baseUrl must be an official host in production (allowlist, fail closed)

`settings.baseUrl` of a BIGDATACORP config accepted any public URL from the
tenant. An organization in production could point the "real provider" at its
own server and get invented credit data stamped as BIGDATACORP, with no MOCK
config and no operator grant (bypassing the simulated-provider gate of #602),
and it made the service an outbound request vector to a tenant-chosen host.

With NODE_ENV=production the effective provider URL must now be https, carry
no userinfo, query or fragment, and have a host (and non-default port) that
matches EXACTLY one of the provider's hosts: the official ones, fixed in
`providers/base-url-policy.ts` (BIGDATACORP -> plataforma.bigdatacorp.com.br),
plus the ones added through the new optional `BUREAUS_PROVIDER_EXTRA_HOSTS`
(`PROVIDER=host[:port]` pairs; no wildcard; malformed entries are ignored and
never release anything). Outside production the rule does not apply, same cut
as the simulated-provider gate. MOCK makes no network call and is unaffected.

Where it applies:
- create: 400 before the connection test, so the credential is never sent to
  the informed host; nothing is stored
- update: 400 when the settings sent are off the list (even on an inactive
  config), or when the config stays active with stored settings off the list;
  deactivating and fixing the URL pass
- test-connection: 403, no network call
- query (and batch): 403, fail closed and BEFORE the cache — an existing config
  off the list answers nothing, not even what it cached; the attempt is
  recorded in bureau_queries as ERROR with errorCode
  PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NOT_ALLOWED and `bureaus.query.failed` is published
- the driver repeats the check before each request (last barrier)

Every refusal has the stable `details.code` PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NOT_ALLOWED and
a `details.reason`, a `warn` log and the new `bureaus.provider_config.refused`
event carrying organization, config, action, reason and only the host (never
path, query or credential). The shared SSRF guard (`secureFetch`) stays in
place behind it; the repo has no shared host allowlist to reuse.

Deploy stacks gain the variable (catalog). Staging runs with
NODE_ENV=production: a BIGDATACORP config there pointing at an external mock
stops answering unless its host is written to `BUREAUS_PROVIDER_EXTRA_HOSTS`
on bb-bureaus before this version goes up. The README has the SQL to find
such configs.
