Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(bureaus): provider call refuses redirects; refusal notice deduplicated per config; document what the allowlist does not undo

Review follow-ups on the provider baseUrl allowlist.

- driver: the BigDataCorp call passes `redirect: 'error'`. The allowlist checks
  the host of the request; `fetch` would follow a 30x to a destination nobody
  checked, and on 307/308 the credential headers go along. Proven against two
  local servers: without the option the credential reaches the redirect target,
  with it the query fails and nothing reaches the target.
- refusal notice: a batch over one irregular config still refuses every query
  and records each one as ERROR, but the `warn` log and the
  `bureaus.provider_config.refused` event are emitted once per config, action,
  reason and host every 5 minutes; the next notice carries
  `repeatsSinceLastNotice`. In-process on purpose (up to one notice per replica
  per window, no Redis dependency). Create/update refusals are not deduplicated.
- README: FOUND queries already recorded by an irregular config stay readable
  (SQL to list them by `config_id`), the rule depends on `NODE_ENV=production`
  being set on the service, and the two behaviours above.

`secureFetch` itself is unchanged: making redirects an error for every caller
would break customer webhook endpoints that redirect. Callers that send
credentials or secrets and still follow redirects are listed in the PR.

title: fix(audit-trail): bound the wait for the chain lock; a locked organization no longer stops the trail of all
body:
fix(audit-trail): bound the wait for the chain lock; a locked organization no longer stops the trail of all

A lock held on ONE organization's chain (a transaction left open, a long
prune) made AuditChainRepository.append wait for as long as the lock lasted:
Prisma's 20 s transaction timeout does not cancel a statement that is waiting.
The consumer writes one message at a time, so the trail of every organization
on that stream stopped, with no error and no dead letter.

- The first statement of the append and of the prune transaction is
  set_config('lock_timeout', <ms>, true): transaction-local, it covers the
  advisory lock and the FOR UPDATE on the head row. Configurable through
  AUDIT_CHAIN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS (100..9000, default 5000).
- Running out is a classified failure (CHAIN_LOCK_TIMEOUT / 55P03), not
  retried inside the write: it counts as an attempt, the 4th delivery goes to
  the dead letter, the other organizations go on, the replay recovers it.
- Replay: the lookup of the already-written row is bounded by
  created_at >= deadLetteredAt - 10 min, an index range scan on
  (organization_id, created_at).
- scripts/audit-trail/append-contention.ts: the measurement behind the default.
- README: the `_audit` metadata prefix is reserved in POST /events;
  idle_in_transaction_session_timeout recommended; who waits for the lock.

title: fix(audit-trail): host refusals reach the trail; non-UUID ids go to metadata; real dead letter (#611)
body:
fix(audit-trail): host refusals reach the trail; non-UUID ids go to metadata; real dead letter (#611)

* fix(audit-trail): host refusals reach the trail; non-UUID ids go to metadata and the dead letter is real

Every banking.host.(map|unmap).refused was dropped: the mapper put the HOST in
resource_id, a UUID column, the INSERT failed with P2023 and the consumer
acknowledged the message after four deliveries while logging "moving to dead
letter" (it only did XACK).

- event-mapper: banking_app_host carries no resource id (the host stays in
  metadata.host); banking.host.mapped|unmapped map to the same resource type
  instead of the raw `banking` namespace with the organization as resource.
- AuditLogService.logEvent (the single write path): actor_id / resource_id only
  keep UUIDs; any other id is stored as metadata.actorRef / metadata.resourceRef
  and the row is always written.
- AuditConsumer: a message that exceeds the retries is copied to the
  `audit-trail:dead-letter` stream before the XACK, logged at error level.
- Integration test with real Redis and real Postgres through the real consumer
  and service; the existing ones replaced the service with a stub and asserted
  resourceId = '<host>'.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(audit-trail): replay dead letters straight into the trail; canonical UUIDs; outage is not an attempt

Review of #611.

- Dead letters are replayed by AuditDeadLetterService (scripts/audit-trail/
  dead-letter.ts): same mapping, same logEvent, NEVER republished — an event
  put back on iam-events reaches every consumer group (webhook delivered
  twice, analytics counted twice). The README recipe that did XADD is gone.
- UUID columns are stored in canonical form (lowercase 8-4-4-4-12): the row
  hash covers the text and Postgres stores lowercase, so an uppercase id made
  /verify answer hash_mismatch. `{uuid}`, 32 hex and `urn:uuid:` are
  normalised instead of diverted. organization_id included.
- Non-UUID actor/resource ids go to RESERVED metadata keys
  (_auditResourceRef / _auditActorRef): a producer's own resourceRef is never
  overwritten. An empty id leaves no reference.
- An organization that is not a UUID is refused by name on the first delivery
  (INVALID_ORGANIZATION_ID) and kept in the dead letter as evidence.
- Database unavailable is not an attempt: the message stays pending, whatever
  its delivery count, and the stream loop backs off. Only a rejected row

title: feat(banking): idempotent credit application by Idempotency-Key
body:
feat(banking): idempotent credit application by Idempotency-Key

`POST /v1/credit/applications` generated `applicationId = randomUUID()` on
every call. When the response was lost and the customer tapped again, the
credit service saw a NEW request: a holder not yet enabled got
`APPLICATION_UNDER_REVIEW` without the id to follow, and an enabled holder
had the paid analysis run twice.

The route now accepts an idempotency key, in the `Idempotency-Key` header or
in the body (same mold as Pix and desktop operations; both present must be
equal):

- the key is bound to an `applicationId` BEFORE the credit service is called,
  in the new `banking.credit_application_requests` (the row id IS the
  `applicationId`); unique per (organization, account, key), so two taps or
  two replicas share one row and the loser reads the winner
- same key -> same `applicationId` sent to the channel, which deduplicates by
  it and returns the usual answer
- same key with other notes -> 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH (the block's
  existing code and status), nothing reaches the service; the comparison is a
  SHA-256 of the sorted note ids, the notes themselves are not stored
- the gate comes before the key; a malformed key is 400 BAD_REQUEST
- `banking.credit.application.requested` carries `repeated`: false only for
  whoever flipped `answered_at` (conditional updateMany), true on replays;
  refusals carry the key to the refusal trail
- no key -> legacy behaviour, unchanged and documented as legacy

analytics: `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH` joins the credit refusal code list (the
hand-versioned entries to version 3.

Migration `20261012150000_banking_credit_application_requests` is additive
and idempotent (one table, two indexes). It does not reach an environment by
itself: run scripts/launch phases 0 -> 1 -> 2 before deploying `banking`.

fix(calculations-engine): rate solvers always terminate and never return an unconverged rate (#609)

* fix(calculations-engine): rate solvers always terminate and never return an unconverged rate

`calculateReceivablesDiscount` with `dayCount: 'ACTUAL_365'` never returned for
short titles with face values in the millions and a deep discount (e.g.
`advanceRate` 0.531 over 3- and 7-day titles). formulajs' XIRR is Newton with
no iteration cap and ABSOLUTE 1e-10 tolerances on both the step and the
residual: with sums in the millions the residual cannot go below one ulp
(~1e-9) and, once the root is large, neither can the step, so it cycles between
neighbouring doubles forever. It is a public route: one request pinned the
process.

All rate searches now go through `calculators/rate-solver.ts`: bounded work
(iteration caps, plus a repeated-iterate exit), a bracketed bisection fallback,
and an explicit "no rate" (`null`) instead of the last iterate. A value is only
returned after its residual is checked against the equation.

- receivables discount, ACTUAL_365: Newton with XIRR's own arithmetic, guess
  and stopping rule (same double for every input that converged), then
  bisection on ln(1 + rate) in [0, 709]; no representable root -> `cet.*` null
  with the existing `EFFECTIVE_RATE_NOT_SOLVABLE` warning
- receivables discount, COMMERCIAL_30: the [0, 1] bisection is kept step for
  step; above 100% a month it used to answer exactly `1` with no warning and
  now keeps searching; a yearly rate that overflows is reported as not solvable
- loan-cet-rate / loan-interest-rate (and portability, which composes them):
  formulajs' RATE gives up after 100 steps by returning the last iterate; its
  answer is kept only when it solves the equation, otherwise the positive root
  is found by bisection, otherwise the existing domain error is raised
- service logs a warning (numbers only) when no effective rate exists
- README: the solver contract, what changed and what did not

Measured against main on generated inputs: 38,915 of 40,000 receivables
portfolios byte-identical; the other 1,085 are the 503 that hang on main and the
582 COMMERCIAL_30 answers that were pinned at 1. Same split under TZ=UTC and
TZ=Asia/Tokyo (8,000 each). Annuities: 17,845 of 30,000 identical; 17 were a
silently wrong rate on main (e.g. 16.1% where the rate is 12.1%); 12,138 raised
an error on main although a rate exists.

body:
feat(banking): unmap an application host only from its expected owner

`DELETE /admin/platform/hosts/:host` took the host from whoever had it: the
route receives no organization. A caller acting for ONE client (the panel's
revocation of an operator grant) had no safe way to use it — checking the owner
first with the idempotent `PUT` is not atomic (the host can change owner
between the two calls, taking ANOTHER bank's app down with a success on record)
and binds the host to the very organization being revoked.

`?organizationId=<uuid>` is now the EXPECTED OWNER: the host is released only
if it is that organization's, in one statement (`release(organizationId, host)`
already deletes by host AND owner). Another organization's: 409, nothing
changes, and the answer never says whose it is. Nobody's: 404. Both carry
`details.code` (`BANKING_HOST_OF_ANOTHER_ORGANIZATION`,

a gateway or of an older block. An `organizationId` that is not a uuid is 400 —
it never falls back to "whoever has it". Without the parameter the behaviour is
unchanged.

The README also says what unmapping does and does not do: the routes scoped by
host stop (manifest, capabilities, onboarding, terms, attestation nonce, desktop
access); whoever already has a bound device keeps a session — those routes find
the organization by the session.

feat(banking): pedido de crédito idempotente por Idempotency-Key (#608)

* feat(banking): idempotent credit application by Idempotency-Key

`POST /v1/credit/applications` generated `applicationId = randomUUID()` on
every call. When the response was lost and the customer tapped again, the
credit service saw a NEW request: a holder not yet enabled got
`APPLICATION_UNDER_REVIEW` without the id to follow, and an enabled holder
had the paid analysis run twice.

The route now accepts an idempotency key, in the `Idempotency-Key` header or
in the body (same mold as Pix and desktop operations; both present must be
equal):

- the key is bound to an `applicationId` BEFORE the credit service is called,
  in the new `banking.credit_application_requests` (the row id IS the
  `applicationId`); unique per (organization, account, key), so two taps or
  two replicas share one row and the loser reads the winner
- same key -> same `applicationId` sent to the channel, which deduplicates by
  it and returns the usual answer
- same key with other notes -> 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH (the block's
  existing code and status), nothing reaches the service; the comparison is a
  SHA-256 of the sorted note ids, the notes themselves are not stored
- the gate comes before the key; a malformed key is 400 BAD_REQUEST
- `banking.credit.application.requested` carries `repeated`: false only for
  whoever flipped `answered_at` (conditional updateMany), true on replays;
  refusals carry the key to the refusal trail
- no key -> legacy behaviour, unchanged and documented as legacy

analytics: `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH` joins the credit refusal code list (the
hand-versioned entries to version 3.

Migration `20261012150000_banking_credit_application_requests` is additive
and idempotent (one table, two indexes). It does not reach an environment by
itself: run scripts/launch phases 0 -> 1 -> 2 before deploying `banking`.

  _auditSourceId) and the database is asked before writing; a short Redis lock
  keeps two runs apart. It walks the list by cursor, passes over the entries
  no replay can write without spending the limit, and reports
  written / skippedAlreadyWritten / stillFailing / impossible.
  `discard <id>` and `discard --reason <R>` remove without writing, logged at
  error level without the body.
- Everything under the `_audit` metadata prefix is the trail's: dropped from
  what a producer sends.

body:
fix(calculations-engine): rate solvers always terminate and never return an unconverged rate

`calculateReceivablesDiscount` with `dayCount: 'ACTUAL_365'` never returned for
short titles with face values in the millions and a deep discount (e.g.
`advanceRate` 0.531 over 3- and 7-day titles). formulajs' XIRR is Newton with
no iteration cap and ABSOLUTE 1e-10 tolerances on both the step and the
residual: with sums in the millions the residual cannot go below one ulp
(~1e-9) and, once the root is large, neither can the step, so it cycles between
neighbouring doubles forever. It is a public route: one request pinned the
process.

All rate searches now go through `calculators/rate-solver.ts`: bounded work
(iteration caps, plus a repeated-iterate exit), a bracketed bisection fallback,
and an explicit "no rate" (`null`) instead of the last iterate. A value is only
returned after its residual is checked against the equation.

- receivables discount, ACTUAL_365: Newton with XIRR's own arithmetic, guess
  and stopping rule (same double for every input that converged), then
  bisection on ln(1 + rate) in [0, 709]; no representable root -> `cet.*` null
  with the existing `EFFECTIVE_RATE_NOT_SOLVABLE` warning
- receivables discount, COMMERCIAL_30: the [0, 1] bisection is kept step for
  step; above 100% a month it used to answer exactly `1` with no warning and
  now keeps searching; a yearly rate that overflows is reported as not solvable
- loan-cet-rate / loan-interest-rate (and portability, which composes them):
  formulajs' RATE gives up after 100 steps by returning the last iterate; its
  answer is kept only when it solves the equation, otherwise the positive root
  is found by bisection, otherwise the existing domain error is raised
- service logs a warning (numbers only) when no effective rate exists
- README: the solver contract, what changed and what did not

Measured against main on generated inputs: 38,915 of 40,000 receivables
portfolios byte-identical; the other 1,085 are the 503 that hang on main and the
582 COMMERCIAL_30 answers that were pinned at 1. Same split under TZ=UTC and
TZ=Asia/Tokyo (8,000 each). Annuities: 17,845 of 30,000 identical; 17 were a

title: fix(audit-trail): bound the wait for the chain lock — a locked organization no longer stops the trail of all (#613)
body:
fix(audit-trail): bound the wait for the chain lock — a locked organization no longer stops the trail of all (#613)

* fix(audit-trail): bound the wait for the chain lock; a locked organization no longer stops the trail of all

A lock held on ONE organization's chain (a transaction left open, a long
prune) made AuditChainRepository.append wait for as long as the lock lasted:
Prisma's 20 s transaction timeout does not cancel a statement that is waiting.
The consumer writes one message at a time, so the trail of every organization
on that stream stopped, with no error and no dead letter.

- The first statement of the append and of the prune transaction is
  set_config('lock_timeout', <ms>, true): transaction-local, it covers the
  advisory lock and the FOR UPDATE on the head row. Configurable through
  AUDIT_CHAIN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS (100..9000, default 5000).
- Running out is a classified failure (CHAIN_LOCK_TIMEOUT / 55P03), not
  retried inside the write: it counts as an attempt, the 4th delivery goes to
  the dead letter, the other organizations go on, the replay recovers it.
- Replay: the lookup of the already-written row is bounded by
  created_at >= deadLetteredAt - 10 min, an index range scan on
  (organization_id, created_at).
- scripts/audit-trail/append-contention.ts: the measurement behind the default.
- README: the `_audit` metadata prefix is reserved in POST /events;
  idle_in_transaction_session_timeout recommended; who waits for the lock.

title: fix(bureaus): provider baseUrl must be an official host in production (allowlist, fail closed)
body:
fix(bureaus): provider baseUrl must be an official host in production (allowlist, fail closed)

`settings.baseUrl` of a BIGDATACORP config accepted any public URL from the
tenant. An organization in production could point the "real provider" at its
own server and get invented credit data stamped as BIGDATACORP, with no MOCK
config and no operator grant (bypassing the simulated-provider gate of #602),
and it made the service an outbound request vector to a tenant-chosen host.

With NODE_ENV=production the effective provider URL must now be https, carry
no userinfo, query or fragment, and have a host (and non-default port) that
matches EXACTLY one of the provider's hosts: the official ones, fixed in
`providers/base-url-policy.ts` (BIGDATACORP -> plataforma.bigdatacorp.com.br),
plus the ones added through the new optional `BUREAUS_PROVIDER_EXTRA_HOSTS`
(`PROVIDER=host[:port]` pairs; no wildcard; malformed entries are ignored and
never release anything). Outside production the rule does not apply, same cut
as the simulated-provider gate. MOCK makes no network call and is unaffected.

Where it applies:
- create: 400 before the connection test, so the credential is never sent to
  the informed host; nothing is stored
- update: 400 when the settings sent are off the list (even on an inactive
  config), or when the config stays active with stored settings off the list;
  deactivating and fixing the URL pass
- test-connection: 403, no network call
- query (and batch): 403, fail closed and BEFORE the cache — an existing config
  off the list answers nothing, not even what it cached; the attempt is
  recorded in bureau_queries as ERROR with errorCode
  PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NOT_ALLOWED and `bureaus.query.failed` is published
- the driver repeats the check before each request (last barrier)

Every refusal has the stable `details.code` PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NOT_ALLOWED and
a `details.reason`, a `warn` log and the new `bureaus.provider_config.refused`
event carrying organization, config, action, reason and only the host (never
path, query or credential). The shared SSRF guard (`secureFetch`) stays in
place behind it; the repo has no shared host allowlist to reuse.

Deploy stacks gain the variable (catalog). Staging runs with
NODE_ENV=production: a BIGDATACORP config there pointing at an external mock
stops answering unless its host is written to `BUREAUS_PROVIDER_EXTRA_HOSTS`
on bb-bureaus before this version goes up. The README has the SQL to find
such configs.

title: feat(admin): revoking an operator grant takes the simulated provider back in the baas block
body:
feat(admin): revoking an operator grant takes the simulated provider back in the baas block

Slice 7d, part 1. The revocation of an operator grant only recorded the end of
the grant: the simulated provider stayed released in `baas`. Now
`DELETE /admin/clients/:userId/provisioning-grants/:packageSlug` with
`simulatedProvider: true` revokes the grant in the block, with the operator's
own session. The app's HOST is NOT unbound by this route: it stays bound and
the answer says so.

Rules, from the adversarial review of the first version (#1884):
- a 404 never means "there was no grant" on its own: only the block's code
  (`SIMULATED_PROVIDER_GRANT_NOT_FOUND`) or the state read again saying
  `granted: false`. A bare 404 (older block, gateway) is UNAVAILABLE / 503 and
  the row is left exactly as it was;
- revoking always needs a PERSON's session, also when no block is called;

title: fix(credit): an operation is only disbursed when the Pix is settled (#1881)
body:
fix(credit): an operation is only disbursed when the Pix is settled (#1881)

Staging smoke, 12/10/2026 (operation 33728c44…): the disbursement sent a fixed
idempotency key per operation and recorded `desembolsada` for ANY answer of the
baas block that carried a transfer id. A first attempt refused for balance,
re-authorized after the deposit, got the block's replay of the refused
transaction (HTTP 200, status FAILED, with an id) and was recorded as paid:
no Pix, fund untouched, event emitted, the bank app showing "paid". A pending
Pix was recorded as paid the same way and "try again" could never work.

This is the minimum that stops it. The first version of this change was
rejected in review: walking the keys paid twice when the Pix was split by the
account limit. The split is OFF under settlement and what was cut is listed in
the PR as work of its own.

Handlers (reach every tenant on deploy):
- INITIATE_PIX_TRANSFER gains a settlement mode (pix-settlement.ts):
  `transferId` only when SETTLED, at most one Pix per business reference. A new
  key (`<reference>:<n>`) is only sent after the block, answering HTTP 200 in
  that very call, showed the previous key's transaction FAILED/CANCELLED.
  401/403, a gateway 404, 408/429, 5xx, a non-JSON page, no answer and a 4xx
  of the call itself never move the key. After any non-answer the transactions
  under the attempt's mark (businessId) decide: one still open is "in
  processing", never "refused". No split by the Pix limit: refused for the
  limit is a failure with its own reason and the key stays.
- `settlement` present and unresolved (a `{{…}}` left as text, null, empty, an
  unknown word) throws; it never falls back to paying. Absent, the reference
  production already sends (`disbursement:<op>`) is settled, so installed
  templates are fixed before any reinstall.
- A 403 for blocked balance (refused before any reservation) is reported as
  lack of available balance, not as an authentication error.
- Outside settlement, a replayed FAILED/CANCELLED transaction no longer carries
  `transferId`.
- DATASTORE_UPDATE_DOCUMENT: a lost claim (409 with `expectedVersion`) keeps
  its old default — the action goes on — now with one structured warning
  (`datastore.update.claim_lost`). `failOnConflict: true` fails the action;
  `conflictAsData: true` hands the 409 to the flow. No global change.
- reverseBoleta refuses while a Pix may still arrive (in processing, claimed,
  partial, or the `falhou` an older flow writes for a pending Pix).
- The banking channel, the desk screens, the timeline, the hotsite desk and
  the assistant stop reading "the Pix step ran" as "paid".
- DisbursementSettlementJob is born OFF (DISBURSEMENT_SWEEP_ENABLED=true): its
  own event `antecipacao.desembolso.conferir`, a gate on every active flow AND
  on the installed validator action, a global lock per run and a lock per
  tenant held until they expire, nothing without Redis.

Templates (reach a tenant when its credit package is reinstalled):
- antecipacao-validar-desembolso: `registrar` writes the OUTCOME — settled →
  desembolsada; pending/no answer → desembolso_autorizado with
  desembolso.status em_processamento; refused → falhou with a sentence for the
  desk and the bank's text in erroBruto. `validar` decides pay vs check and
  refuses a second authorization right after a claim. `encerrar` fails the
  execution on a refused Pix. An operation recorded as paid is not re-opened.
- W6 (1.8): versioned claim before the bank, Pix in settlement mode, one
  announcement gated on "paid for the first time AND written", a trail event
  for every attempt and outcome (no Pix key, no document), the WhatsApp notice
  behind the same app-channel branch as the analysis (#1874), and a second
  trigger for the sweep's event.
- Commission (1.1): a failed replay with an id is not a paid commission; both
  claims fail on conflict.

audits production offline by default; `--consultar-banco` asks the bank and
says that doing so makes the block sync with the provider.

body:
fix(workflows): a failed source stops its dependents in graph mode — behind WORKFLOW_GRAPH_FAILED_SOURCE_MODE (default shadow) (#1877)

* fix(workflows): a failed source stops its dependents in graph mode too

Every workflow installed from a template runs in graph mode (the installer
regenerates layout.edges, and edges win over dependsOn). The graph join counts
a failed source as "resolved" so nothing waits forever — but nothing then
failed the dependent, so an action joining a failed source with any healthy
one ran anyway, reading an output that did not exist. Whether it ran also
depended on the position of the failed source inside the wave.

Measured with the real executor on antecipacao-analise-e-proposta (35
actions): with buscarLead failing, 32 of the other 34 actions ran — dossier
built without the assignor, proposal recorded, WhatsApp sent — and only then
was the execution marked failed. DAG mode stops at the 11 independent reads
and fails 23 actions by dependency.

propagateDependencyFailures runs at the end of each wave, before the ready
queue is used: any incoming edge whose source FAILED fails the target with
"Dependency failed: <name>", transitively — the rule executeDAG already
applies. Unchanged: onDependencyFailure: 'continue' on the target still runs
it; a tolerated failure (continueOnError) never enters `failed`; a skipped
source (branch not taken) still counts as resolved at a join.

Two pre-existing differences between the modes are left alone and pinned in
the new spec: a single-input opt-in dependent after a hard failure (DAG runs
it, graph does not), and a non-opt-in dependent of a tolerated failure (DAG
fails it, graph leaves it unrun and the execution green).

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE for every graph-mode workflow: 118 join actions in 61 of the
142 graph-mode templates stop running when one of their sources fails.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(workflows): gate the graph failed-source rule behind WORKFLOW_GRAPH_FAILED_SOURCE_MODE (default shadow)

Review of the previous commit: the rule is right, shipping it unconditionally
is not. Merging this no longer changes how any workflow executes.

WORKFLOW_GRAPH_FAILED_SOURCE_MODE = off | shadow | on, read once when the
executor is built. Default and fallback for an invalid value: shadow (with a
boot warning) — a bad value never becomes `on`.
- off: legacy behaviour, nothing computed.
- shadow: legacy behaviour plus ONE structured log per execution with what
  `on` would have failed ({action, failedSource, ranAnyway}), which opted-in
  actions `on` would have run, and whether the final status would change.
  Ids and action names only.
- on: a failed source fails its dependents, and:
  - an opted-in dependent (onDependencyFailure: 'continue') is handed the
    baton when its source fails — by execution or by dependency — so the
    remedy no longer depends on the failed source being processed before the
    healthy one; a single-input opt-in runs too, as in DAG mode;
  - a graceful halt (_halt, e.g. BUFFER_MESSAGES) is not a failure and
    propagates nothing;
  - propagation happens before a suspension leaves the wave;
  - on resume, an action that already produced an output is never failed by
    dependency.

off and shadow were compared against the master executor over 24 scenarios:
no difference in what runs, what is logged, or how the call ends.

No template is changed here. The guide (§25) carries the table, the 15
send/agent joins that would go silent under `on`, and what has to happen
before `on` in production.

   acts were all refused is no longer recorded as a revocation. Additive
   migration with the attempt and what a block confirmed as undone. The panel
   shows the outcome per item and what stays in effect.

   account's four-eyes rule (iam `access-policy`) on as the LAST step, with the

  that very call, showed the previous key's transaction FAILED/CANCELLED.
  401/403, a gateway 404, 408/429, 5xx, a non-JSON page, no answer and a 4xx
  of the call itself never move the key. After any non-answer the transactions
  under the attempt's mark (businessId) decide: one still open is "in
  processing", never "refused". No split by the Pix limit: refused for the
  limit is a failure with its own reason and the key stays.

  unknown word) throws; it never falls back to paying. Absent, the reference
  production already sends (`disbursement:<op>`) is settled, so installed
  templates are fixed before any reinstall.

  lack of available balance, not as an authentication error.
- Outside settlement, a replayed FAILED/CANCELLED transaction no longer carries
  `transferId`.

  its old default — the action goes on — now with one structured warning

  `conflictAsData: true` hands the 409 to the flow. No global change.
- reverseBoleta refuses while a Pix may still arrive (in processing, claimed,
  partial, or the `falhou` an older flow writes for a pending Pix).
- The banking channel, the desk screens, the timeline, the hotsite desk and
  the assistant stop reading "the Pix step ran" as "paid".
- DisbursementSettlementJob is born OFF (DISBURSEMENT_SWEEP_ENABLED=true): its

title: fix(workflows): a failed source stops its dependents in graph mode too
body:
fix(workflows): a failed source stops its dependents in graph mode too

Every workflow installed from a template runs in graph mode (the installer
regenerates layout.edges, and edges win over dependsOn). The graph join counts
a failed source as "resolved" so nothing waits forever — but nothing then
failed the dependent, so an action joining a failed source with any healthy
one ran anyway, reading an output that did not exist. Whether it ran also
depended on the position of the failed source inside the wave.

Measured with the real executor on antecipacao-analise-e-proposta (35
actions): with buscarLead failing, 32 of the other 34 actions ran — dossier
built without the assignor, proposal recorded, WhatsApp sent — and only then
was the execution marked failed. DAG mode stops at the 11 independent reads
and fails 23 actions by dependency.

propagateDependencyFailures runs at the end of each wave, before the ready
queue is used: any incoming edge whose source FAILED fails the target with
"Dependency failed: <name>", transitively — the rule executeDAG already
applies. Unchanged: onDependencyFailure: 'continue' on the target still runs
it; a tolerated failure (continueOnError) never enters `failed`; a skipped
source (branch not taken) still counts as resolved at a join.

Two pre-existing differences between the modes are left alone and pinned in
the new spec: a single-input opt-in dependent after a hard failure (DAG runs
it, graph does not), and a non-opt-in dependent of a tolerated failure (DAG
fails it, graph leaves it unrun and the execution green).

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE for every graph-mode workflow: 118 join actions in 61 of the
142 graph-mode templates stop running when one of their sources fails.

feat(credit): BUREAU_QUERY consults as the tenant when it has its own bureau supplier; bureauProvision in the installer

Split out of the first version of this PR after its review: this half changes
nobody's credit decision. The dossier adapter that reads the block's credit
signals is a separate draft PR.

Identity (BUREAU_QUERY, eight actions in seven packages): a tenant whose own
organization has a default, active bureau supplier is consulted in its own
name (machine key `credit-blocks-bb`); everybody else stays exactly as before,
on the platform's identity, with the same request byte for byte.
- the discovery is ONE read (`GET /providers`, first page), never charged;
  concurrent discoveries of a tenant share it;
- "has none" is remembered for 60 s and reads nothing while it holds (not even
  the tenant's credential); "has one" for 5 min, bound to a mark of the key;
- a read that fails for a tenant known to have its own supplier keeps the
  tenant's identity for up to 30 min (it must not fall silently onto the
  platform's paid supplier); with nothing known it is the platform, with a
  `warn` and `identityWarning` in the action's output;
- once the tenant's query has been attempted there is no second query;
- one address builder (`bureausUrl`) for the query, the discovery and the
  installer: the configured base plus the route, no guessed prefix;
- the output says who consulted (`identity`, `identityReason`) and, per batch
  item, which supplier answered (`provider`); never a key;
- a batch the block did not answer item by item (400/429/500) is `ERROR`, no
  longer `NOT_FOUND` with no results.
`identidade-declarada.spec.ts` moves the action from `plataforma-nao-revisado`
to the reviewed, conditional `tenant-se-tem-fornecedor`; ceiling 40 -> 39.

Installer: generic `bureauProvision` with the idempotent step
`bureau-provider` (checks the default supplier with a read; creates the
simulated one only when the request asks for it and the organization has
none; the block's `SIMULATED_PROVIDER_NOT_GRANTED` is `needs-input`). The step
has NO `failed` outcome, not even in a strict package: a bureau block that is
down, 404, refusing the key or without an address is `degraded`, the
installation answers 201 and contracting is turned on. Declared by
`receivables-banking-channel`, with its own `bureauProvider` input. Packages
without the field get no step and no field in the answer.

Notes, the UI gap (the install screen sends no `inputs` at all) and a
pre-existing defect found in five verticals' dossiers:

body:
fix(workflows): gate the graph failed-source rule behind WORKFLOW_GRAPH_FAILED_SOURCE_MODE (default shadow)

Review of the previous commit: the rule is right, shipping it unconditionally
is not. Merging this no longer changes how any workflow executes.

WORKFLOW_GRAPH_FAILED_SOURCE_MODE = off | shadow | on, read once when the
executor is built. Default and fallback for an invalid value: shadow (with a
boot warning) — a bad value never becomes `on`.
- off: legacy behaviour, nothing computed.
- shadow: legacy behaviour plus ONE structured log per execution with what
  `on` would have failed ({action, failedSource, ranAnyway}), which opted-in
  actions `on` would have run, and whether the final status would change.
  Ids and action names only.
- on: a failed source fails its dependents, and:
  - an opted-in dependent (onDependencyFailure: 'continue') is handed the
    baton when its source fails — by execution or by dependency — so the
    remedy no longer depends on the failed source being processed before the
    healthy one; a single-input opt-in runs too, as in DAG mode;
  - a graceful halt (_halt, e.g. BUFFER_MESSAGES) is not a failure and
    propagates nothing;
  - propagation happens before a suspension leaves the wave;
  - on resume, an action that already produced an output is never failed by
    dependency.

off and shadow were compared against the master executor over 24 scenarios:
no difference in what runs, what is logged, or how the call ends.

No template is changed here. The guide (§25) carries the table, the 15
send/agent joins that would go silent under `on`, and what has to happen
before `on` in production.

fix(decision-platform): async consumer on its own connection, exits on SIGTERM, runs each row once

Review of #615 found that starting the consumer as it was would hurt:
- XREADGROUP BLOCK ran on the SHARED Redis client, queueing the XADD of the
  async call, the event publisher, the rate limiter and the /health PING

  connection and quits it on stop.

  never exit and every deploy would end in SIGKILL. The handler now stops the
  server, waits for the entry in hand and exits; SIGINT too.

  reclaimed message whose row already moved on is acked and skipped.
- Entries left pending by a dead consumer are reclaimed with XAUTOCLAIM
  every minute (min idle 2 min).
- A message queued more than 24 h ago fails instead of running late against
  today's policy, re-querying the bureau and firing a stale callback.
- A malformed message fails its execution and is acked instead of escaping
  to the loop with the rest of the batch.
- Consumer name: os.hostname() + random suffix (HOSTNAME is not exported
  under systemd/LXC). Stream capped with MAXLEN ~ 100000. README updated.

title: fix(credit): package reinstall is atomic for whoever executes (P-C) (#1897)
body:
fix(credit): package reinstall is atomic for whoever executes (P-C) (#1897)

* fix(credit): package reinstall is atomic for whoever executes

A reinstall rewrote the custom action ~0.9 s before the new workflow existed and switched the new
flow on ~30 ms before the old one went off (staging smoke 12/10, log-C0). Steps resolve their
action by slug when they run, so executions could see "old flow + new action", "new flow + old
action" (never pays: the operation stays authorized) or two flows on one event.

- custom_action_revisions: executable content of an action (type, config, schemas) kept by
  sha256, append-only. A CUSTOM_ACTION step pinned with config.customActionRevision runs exactly
  that content (live row when it matches, stored revision otherwise, refusal when missing).
- Template installer: actions are prepared (new content kept, live row untouched), the new copy
  is born off with every step pinned, ONE transaction pins the old copy to what it runs, turns it
  off and turns the new one on; only then the live actions are rewritten. The package installer
  defers every rewrite until all copies of the closure switched.
- Executor: unpinned steps are bound at the start of an execution to the live hash, read in the
  same REPEATABLE READ snapshot as the workflow's actions; the map lives in the execution context
  and is restored on resume. In-flight executions end with the versions they started with.
- Editing an action's code keeps the replaced content and re-pins the account's ACTIVE flows in
  the same transaction. Export/import drop pins (only the installer keeps them).

Proven on a real Postgres with the real installer and executor (integration spec gated by
TEST_DATABASE_URL): 0 mixed executions, always exactly one active flow, money once, nothing
stuck, idempotent over 3 more reinstalls; mutation 35/35 killed.

title: fix(credit): package reinstall is atomic for whoever executes
body:
fix(credit): package reinstall is atomic for whoever executes

A reinstall rewrote the custom action ~0.9 s before the new workflow existed and switched the new
flow on ~30 ms before the old one went off (staging smoke 12/10, log-C0). Steps resolve their
action by slug when they run, so executions could see "old flow + new action", "new flow + old
action" (never pays: the operation stays authorized) or two flows on one event.

- custom_action_revisions: executable content of an action (type, config, schemas) kept by
  sha256, append-only. A CUSTOM_ACTION step pinned with config.customActionRevision runs exactly
  that content (live row when it matches, stored revision otherwise, refusal when missing).
- Template installer: actions are prepared (new content kept, live row untouched), the new copy
  is born off with every step pinned, ONE transaction pins the old copy to what it runs, turns it
  off and turns the new one on; only then the live actions are rewritten. The package installer
  defers every rewrite until all copies of the closure switched.
- Executor: unpinned steps are bound at the start of an execution to the live hash, read in the
  same REPEATABLE READ snapshot as the workflow's actions; the map lives in the execution context
  and is restored on resume. In-flight executions end with the versions they started with.
- Editing an action's code keeps the replaced content and re-pins the account's ACTIVE flows in
  the same transaction. Export/import drop pins (only the installer keeps them).

Proven on a real Postgres with the real installer and executor (integration spec gated by
TEST_DATABASE_URL): 0 mixed executions, always exactly one active flow, money once, nothing
stuck, idempotent over 3 more reinstalls; mutation 35/35 killed.

body:
fix(credit): an unanswered bureau or a newly read finding goes to the desk in the five loan dossiers — never a clean record, never a refusal on its own (#1889)

* fix(credit): an unanswered bureau is not a clean record in the five loan dossiers; read the bureaus contract by structure

personal-loan, payroll-loan, rural-loan, vehicle-collateral and property-collateral shared a
copied bureau block with two defects, both generous with credit:

1. An error scored as a clean record. `results: []` is truthy, so a refused batch (4xx/5xx), an
   empty batch, a batch with every item in error and a document NOT_FOUND all read as "consulted,
   nothing against the borrower": full points (200/200). A bureau that was down approved better
   than one that answered.
2. Only the sanction was seen. The signals were searched as substrings under names the bureaus
   block never emits (hasCollections, hasProtests, negativado, hasLawsuits, pep). An active
   collection, lawsuits and a politically exposed person went unread.

Now one shared reader (`_shared/bureau-reading.ts`, same mold as note-reading.ts: one source text,
interpolated into each sandboxed action and evaluated for the API/specs):

- "Clean" only when the answer is whole: batch not in error, every item of the borrower's document
  FOUND, and the three signals the scorecards weigh each covered by a readable answer
  (collections or restrictions; lawsuits; compliance). Anything else — batch ERROR, no results,
  item ERROR/DENIED/NOT_SUPPORTED, NOT_FOUND, partial, FOUND with a null field, a score outside
  0–1000, a company (no kind answers compliance for a CNPJ) — scores half the block (the weight
  "unavailable" already had) and sets `bureauDisponivel: false`.
- The decision tables of personal, payroll, rural and property (1.0.0 → 1.1.0) gain the rule the
  vehicle table already had: `bureauDisponivel = false → MESA`. The catalog simulator sends the
  new input.
- Findings are read by structure and keep the weight each scorecard already gave them:
  isCurrentlyOnCollection / restrictions → the old hasCollections|hasProtests|negativado (blocker);
  lawsuits totalCount/asDefendantCount → the old hasLawsuits (reduced block);
  politicallyExposed / sanctioned → the old sanctioned|pep (blocker).
  The legacy flags and the raw BigDataCorp envelope still count AGAINST the borrower, never for.
- The bureau's own credit score is validated and reported; no scorecard weighs it, so no points.

This CHANGES CREDIT DECISIONS in the five verticals, always to the conservative side, and only
reaches a tenant when the package is reinstalled (custom actions are text installed per tenant;
the five dossiers go to version 2). A tenant that kept its own newer table is not republished by
the installer: there the block stops scoring as clean, but no rule sends the proposal to the desk.

ever read (active collection, restriction/protest, politically exposed person) into blockers,
because that was the weight the scorecards declared — switching on, at once, an automatic refusal
policy that never ran in production. The owner's rule is "in doubt, the desk".

- What was ALREADY read decides exactly as it did: the legacy flags, searched as the same
  substrings in the same shapes (`results|subjects|data`) — which is also how a sanction in the
  block's answer was and is caught. Blockers are byte-for-byte the master's.
- What NOBODY read before is a finding (`achados`) that only sends the proposal to the desk, with
  one reason each: "cobrança ativa no bureau", "restrição ou protesto no bureau", "ações judiciais
  no bureau", "pessoa exposta politicamente", and the findings of the raw BigDataCorp envelope.

title: fix(credit): an unanswered bureau is not a clean record in the five loan dossiers; read the bureaus contract by structure
body:
fix(credit): an unanswered bureau is not a clean record in the five loan dossiers; read the bureaus contract by structure

personal-loan, payroll-loan, rural-loan, vehicle-collateral and property-collateral shared a
copied bureau block with two defects, both generous with credit:

1. An error scored as a clean record. `results: []` is truthy, so a refused batch (4xx/5xx), an
   empty batch, a batch with every item in error and a document NOT_FOUND all read as "consulted,
   nothing against the borrower": full points (200/200). A bureau that was down approved better
   than one that answered.
2. Only the sanction was seen. The signals were searched as substrings under names the bureaus
   block never emits (hasCollections, hasProtests, negativado, hasLawsuits, pep). An active
   collection, lawsuits and a politically exposed person went unread.

Now one shared reader (`_shared/bureau-reading.ts`, same mold as note-reading.ts: one source text,
interpolated into each sandboxed action and evaluated for the API/specs):

- "Clean" only when the answer is whole: batch not in error, every item of the borrower's document
  FOUND, and the three signals the scorecards weigh each covered by a readable answer
  (collections or restrictions; lawsuits; compliance). Anything else — batch ERROR, no results,
  item ERROR/DENIED/NOT_SUPPORTED, NOT_FOUND, partial, FOUND with a null field, a score outside
  0–1000, a company (no kind answers compliance for a CNPJ) — scores half the block (the weight
  "unavailable" already had) and sets `bureauDisponivel: false`.
- The decision tables of personal, payroll, rural and property (1.0.0 → 1.1.0) gain the rule the
  vehicle table already had: `bureauDisponivel = false → MESA`. The catalog simulator sends the
  new input.
- Findings are read by structure and keep the weight each scorecard already gave them:
  isCurrentlyOnCollection / restrictions → the old hasCollections|hasProtests|negativado (blocker);
  lawsuits totalCount/asDefendantCount → the old hasLawsuits (reduced block);
  politicallyExposed / sanctioned → the old sanctioned|pep (blocker).
  The legacy flags and the raw BigDataCorp envelope still count AGAINST the borrower, never for.
- The bureau's own credit score is validated and reported; no scorecard weighs it, so no points.

This CHANGES CREDIT DECISIONS in the five verticals, always to the conservative side, and only
reaches a tenant when the package is reinstalled (custom actions are text installed per tenant;
the five dossiers go to version 2). A tenant that kept its own newer table is not republished by
the installer: there the block stops scoring as clean, but no rule sends the proposal to the desk.

fix(credit): newly read bureau findings go to the desk, never refuse on their own; desk rule before the score cut

Follow-up on the same PR, after review of its first cut. That cut turned the signals nobody had
ever read (active collection, restriction/protest, politically exposed person) into blockers,
because that was the weight the scorecards declared — switching on, at once, an automatic refusal
policy that never ran in production. The owner's rule is "in doubt, the desk".

- What was ALREADY read decides exactly as it did: the legacy flags, searched as the same
  substrings in the same shapes (`results|subjects|data`) — which is also how a sanction in the
  block's answer was and is caught. Blockers are byte-for-byte the master's.
- What NOBODY read before is a finding (`achados`) that only sends the proposal to the desk, with
  one reason each: "cobrança ativa no bureau", "restrição ou protesto no bureau", "ações judiciais
  no bureau", "pessoa exposta politicamente", and the findings of the raw BigDataCorp envelope.
- One table input, `bureauRequerMesa` = the answer is not whole OR there is a finding. The rule
  `true → MESA|bureau: conferencia manual (motivos no dossie)` sits BEFORE the score cut and after
  every refusal that does not hang on the score, so an unanswered bureau never becomes a refusal
  by score and nobody refused for another reason is rescued. personal/payroll/rural/property
  1.0.0 → 1.1.0; vehicle 2.0.3 → 2.0.4 (its rule guarded by `gravameOrdem <= 2`: the third
  creditor is still refused by its own rule).
- Points: a blocker → 0 (as before); `bureauRequerMesa` → half the block; otherwise full.
- A company borrower goes to the desk and the reason says the bureau does not answer for a company.
- Installer: when the account's own table is the one in effect and does not read
  `bureauRequerMesa`, the step `decision-table-bureau-desk-rule:<key>` is `needs-input` with code
  DECISION_TABLE_WITHOUT_BUREAU_DESK_RULE (`blocos.preservedTables[].missingInputs`). No lock
  outside the table.

approved → desk (6,385); 0 new refusals; 3,103 whole clean answers identical.

GET /api/devices?groupId= (a 6.15.3 ignora o filtro e devolve a frota, ~10 MB) e
GET /api/positions (~9 MB) por lote e por operação, em paralelo; a resposta inteira ia para a

- smoke.py confere o resumo de cada lote contra o manifesto, 401 sem credencial/senha errada, 404

feat(credit): owner's decisions on #1889 — a house table without the bureau rule still sends to the desk; approving without a bureau answer only by a recorded, revocable acceptance

Owner, 14/10/2026:

(a) A house that kept its OWN decision table (no `bureauRequerMesa` rule): the proposal goes to the
    desk anyway. `vehicle_compose_proposal` (version 2) overrides an approval while the dossier says
    `bureauRequerMesa: true`; the engine's verdict stays recorded as the engine's (`decisaoMotor`),
    the proposal carries `salvaguarda` and a pt-BR reason, and the installer's step
    DECISION_TABLE_WITHOUT_BUREAU_DESK_RULE (now classified as the house's) says so.
(b) A house WITHOUT a bureau: the desk by default. It may let the automatic decision go on without
    any bureau answer only by a person reading `BUREAU_WAIVER` (versioned text, sha256) and accepting
    it: `GET/POST/DELETE /credit-desk/bureau-waiver` (BureauWaiverService). Who is the authenticated
    user (never the body); the trail event (`auditoria_eventos`: bureau.waiver.accepted / revoked) is
    written BEFORE the policy (`bureau.aprovacaoSemBureau` + append-only history, claimed by
    expectedVersion); revocable; an acceptance of an older text does not count.
    The dossiers honour it only when the bureau said NOTHING about a CPF borrower (no answer, failed
    batch, every item in error) — never an incomplete answer, a document not found, a finding, a
    legacy/raw shape, a company or a proposal without a CPF — and the block still scores half.
    Vehicle table 2.0.5: the old `bureauDisponivel = false → MESA` rule goes (bureauRequerMesa covers
    it and honours the acceptance).
    Screen: Política › Regras da casa › "Bureau na análise" (BureauWaiverCard): the default, the text
    in full, a box to tick, accept / revoke, who and when, history.

Differential master × PR (14,120 cases, final decision through the real compose): package table and
house's own table — only approved → desk, 0 new refusals, 0 more generous; with the acceptance —
0 new refusals, more generous than master only where the bureau said nothing (52, vehicle, where

title: fix(workflows): execução manual ancora no gatilho que escuta o evento pedido (#1921)
body:
fix(workflows): execução manual ancora no gatilho que escuta o evento pedido (#1921)

* fix(workflows): anchor a manual run on the trigger that listens to the requested event

The desk authorizes a disbursement through POST /credit-desk/workflows/:id/execute
with the authorization event and no triggerId. resolveManualTrigger then took
"the oldest" trigger, but the disbursement flow's two triggers (authorize and
check) are created in one transaction with the same createdAt, so the order was
the database's: in the staging smoke of #1892, 9 of 9 authorizations were
anchored on the CHECK trigger, payloadForTrigger injected somenteConferir and
the flow answered NADA_A_CONFERIR. The desk never paid.

- resolveManualTrigger(workflowId, triggerId?, eventType?): without a triggerId,
  a check-only event goes to resolveCheckOnlyTrigger; any other event anchors on
  the trigger that listens to it (eventName/fullEventName/event, plain or
  workflow.<id>.<name>) and NEVER on a check-only trigger; with no listener the
  oldest non-check trigger anchors; a flow with only check triggers is refused
  (409 MANUAL_RUN_ONLY_CHECK_TRIGGERS) before anything runs.
- Deterministic order everywhere a trigger is anchored by creation:
  [{ createdAt: 'asc' }, { id: 'asc' }], also re-sorted in memory.
- dispatchManualEvent and POST /workflows/:id/execute/start pass the eventType.
- Tests: the inverse door "an authorization never becomes a check" with the real
  executor (graph and DAG) in both trigger orders — red without the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* fix(workflows): refuse a manual run whose named event no trigger hears on a flow with a check

Review of #1921:
- Without a triggerId, a NAMED event that no trigger listens to, sent to a flow
  that has a check-only trigger (e.g. `antecipacao.desembolso.Conferir`,
  `antecipacao.qualquer` on the disbursement flow), used to fall back to the
  oldest trigger — the authorization — and run as a payment. It is now refused
  (409 MANUAL_RUN_EVENT_NOT_HEARD) before anything is emitted or run. Generic
  runs (`manual` / no event) keep the fallback, minus check triggers.
- `requireListener`: the credit desk's generic execute route requires a trigger
  that listens to the event it names — no fallback at all.
- Removed the unreachable check-event branch of resolveManualTrigger
  (dispatchManualEvent already routes checks to resolveCheckOnlyTrigger; a check
  event reaching it now ends in the same refusal) and the no-op eventType at
  POST /workflows/:id/execute/start (that call only runs with a triggerId).
- Tests: two ordinary triggers of real templates (credit-commission-payout, the
  vehicle lien flow) — the second event anchors on the second trigger and, in
  graph mode, reaches only its branch; unheard named events refused through the
  desk and the manual run with the real executor (graph and DAG).

    - scripts/credito/diag/decision-tables-bureau-desk-rule.mjs (read-only): per tenant, the version

    committed test now compares the WHOLE dossier with the master's (fixture generated from
    origin/master) for a whole clean answer, in the five verticals.

Generous side, closed:
- a bare list at the top (or under another name) is not an answer: not conclusive (it read as
  whole; in vehicle, desk → approved);
- a whole answer carrying the legacy `hasLawsuits` flag keeps the reduced block it always had

body:
fix(credit): seed — an unreadable version is not "the package table", and two DMNs are compared by what they decide

Second review of #1889, two reservations on `CreditBlocksSeedService`:

R1. `catch { existing = null }` read "could not read the version in the engine" as "it is the
    package's table": an account with its own table under the declared label, a listing without
    content and a failing read came back `preserved: null`, no warning, the package snapshot in the
    policy. Now a read that fails, or comes back without content, is `preserved { published: false }`
    with the snapshot (and its reason) taken from the engine: "I do not know" never claims the table.
R2. "Same label, another DMN" was a byte comparison: an engine handing the same document back with
    other whitespace made a reinstall warn about an "own version" in an account running the package
    table. `sameDecisionTable` compares what decides — hit policy, inputs, each rule's cells and
    output, as the DMN reader interprets them — and, outside what the reader represents, the XML
    without the whitespace between tags.

The installer's message for a same-label table no longer asserts "another content" when the cause
may be an unreadable version.

feat(security): convite com aceite — o login por e-mail nunca coloca ninguém numa conta (#1938)

* fix(security): only masters create users; e-mail link never adopts a member-squatted row

POST /users, /users/me/sub-users and /users/:id/sub-users had no role check.
Any PANEL_MEMBER could create a PANEL_MASTER under itself and pre-register
someone else's e-mail; the first IAM login links by e-mail (IamJwtAuthStrategy
and AuthService.findOrCreateLocalUser), dropping the victim under the
attacker's hierarchy.

- assertCanCreateUser: only PANEL_MASTER (incl. legacy PANEL_COMERCIAL) and
  staff create users; masters create only PANEL_MEMBER inside their own
  hierarchy (parent defaults to the caller); staff may create masters.
- isAdoptableByEmail: a pre-registered row (no iamUserId) is adopted only if
  it has no parent or its parent is a master/staff; otherwise 403 and no link.
  Adoptions are logged with parent and IAM org.
- USER_MANAGER_ROLES includes PANEL_COMERCIAL (legacy master) for role/parent
  changes too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DxYmqJFshaWue1ZNJ1oy3v

* feat(security): user invites with acceptance; e-mail login never joins an account

Creating a user (POST /users, /users/me/sub-users, /users/:id/sub-users) now
issues a UserInvite: single-use token (only its SHA-256 stored), 7-day expiry,
e-mail with the acceptance link. Nobody joins an account until the owner of
the e-mail accepts, authenticated with that e-mail (logged in, or on login via
inviteToken).

- iam-identity-link: one resolution for the strategy (every API call) and
  AuthService (login/me). Never adopts a pre-registration with a parent (R1),
  refuses a row bound to another IAM identity (R2), service tokens resolve by
  id and never link.
- Invitees without an accepted invite get an account of their own; a notice
  points them to the link. Role resync never lifts a joined sub-user to master.
- Legacy pre-registrations (12 in prod) migrate to PENDING, expired invites
  tied to the existing row; the parent account resends from the Users screen.
- Users screen: invites with status, resend (old link dies), cancel; PANEL_MASTER
  only offered to staff. Public /convite-usuario/:token page, throttled preview.
- R4: managing users is self + descendants (no siblings), also in bulk.

Review of #1892.

beside "Conferir pagamento", whatever is installed. With W6 1.8 + validator v1 the check
never records "nothing found", and with the old flow + validator v2 the check is refused:
both left only a button that could never move the operation. Authorizing again restarts
the walk at the first key, so a Pix that was paid or is still at the bank is not sent twice.

B2 — a manual run labelled with the check event is anchored on the trigger that LISTENS
to it; a flow with no such trigger is refused (409 CHECK_ONLY_NOT_SUPPORTED, logged,
nothing emitted or run). POST /workflows/:id/execute with the check event against the old
W6 used to pay: the flag was added, the old flow ignored it, and the oldest trigger (the
authorization) anchored the run.

`payloadForTrigger`) forces the restriction from the configuration of the trigger that
fired: the Pub/Sub listener, the queue, RUN_WORKFLOW and future doors hand the payload raw.
(b) ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED no longer blocks the reversal of the boleta (all keys seen FAILED,
nothing paid; the desk has no button for it).
(c) "Nothing found" can be false for a transaction older than the marks: the sentence now
says what is true in both cases.
(d) The provider's text in the operator's hover is masked (e-mail, CPF/CNPJ, phone, random
key, long digit runs).
(e) Guide: an operation paid outside the flow stays `falhou/PIX_LIMIT`; the future safe
split must check the support ticket first.
(f) The flow specs got a 60 s per-test limit: under a parallel suite the default 5 s cut
cases with no assertion failing. No assertion changed.

with the authorization event and no triggerId. resolveManualTrigger then took

body:
fix(credit): 2nd review of #1889 — a revoked bureau waiver cannot come back; one write rule for every path; accepting is a person's act

- R1: the server keeps the waiver state in Postgres (credit_bureau_waiver_state:
  monotonic epoch, active, policy document, trail event; additive migration). The
  seal now covers the epoch; a record decides only while the state names it, so a
  sealed record pasted back after a revocation is without effect. Revocation is
  durable first (state inactive before the policy is touched). The workflow policy
  readers drop any record not in force (no state = none). One write rule
  (guardPolicyWrite) for the data-store proxy, the assistant's data-store tools,
  the DATASTORE_UPDATE/INSERT/ENSURE handlers and the installer: server-owned keys
  stay as stored, snapshots and ensure never carry a copy, a failed read refuses.
  The waiver routes never return the seal.
- R2: the text says it counts from the next analysis, and only after a reinstall
  when the account's package does not read it yet; the API says which
  (pacoteLeAceite) and the screen shows the right sentence (text version bumped).
- R4: accepting requires an interactive IAM access token; API tokens are refused
  (revoking stays open to them). A policy recreated as a new document, a key change
  or a stale record shows "o aceite anterior não vale mais; aceite de novo".

feat(workflows): retain workflow execution history (36 months, credit 60), configurable (#1925)

* feat(workflows): retain workflow execution history for 36 months, configurable

Hourly sweep (WorkflowExecutionRetentionService) deletes only terminal
executions (completed/failed) started and finished before the cutoff and
with no wait state still waiting, in batches of 200 ids (max 25 per sweep).
Action logs and wait states go with them via onDelete: Cascade.

WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_RETENTION_MONTHS (default 36); 0, negative or
non-integer turns it off and logs a warning. One replica per tick via a
Redis lock; Redis down = run anyway (delete by id is idempotent).

  teto WORKFLOW_HTTP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (padrão 5 MB);
- passou do limite, a ação FALHA com mensagem em português; nada é truncado;
- o corte é do próprio axios (`maxContentLength`), que aborta a conexão sem

Vale para todos os herdeiros de BaseHttpHandler: WEB_REQUEST, a família
BaseCatalisaHandler (blocos BB) e o REST de custom action.
`makeCatalisaRequest` deixa o erro de tamanho passar intacto, em vez de
reescrevê-lo como "não foi possível conectar".

DATASTORE_QUERY_DOCUMENTS declara o teto (5 MB) como padrão próprio: os
templates de crédito pedem pageSize 200 de coleções com arrays aninhados.

`maxBodyLength` (corpo ENVIADO) fica de fora de propósito: já está em
memória e limitá-lo quebraria uploads legítimos (EXTRACT_DATA, biometria).

body:
fix(credit): a disbursement check never pays, and the desk never shows the bank's raw text (#1892)

* fix(credit): a disbursement check never pays, and the desk never shows the bank's raw text

Follow-up of #1881, from its adversarial review and its staging smoke of 12/10/2026.

Desk (reaches every tenant on deploy, whatever flow wrote the record):
- A record of the flow of before 12/10 carries the provider's words in `desembolso.erro`
  and no `codigo`. The desk showed them ("Amount exceeds PIX limit of 100000"). It now
  shows the sentence the action wrote for it (only with a code) or one of its own; the
  raw text stays on hover in the operation sheet. Same rule for the toast, the sheet and
  the timeline.
- A refusal no new authorization can pay (PIX_LIMIT, ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED — one list,
  compared with the action's by a contract spec) has no "Tentar de novo".
- "Conferir pagamento" goes to POST /credit-desk/operations/:id/disbursement/check.
  The server writes the request (`somenteConferir: true`), picks the tenant's own flow
  and refuses (409, nothing runs) an installation that cannot be trusted to only
  check. It used to send the AUTHORIZATION event: on an operation in processing with no
  id of the bank it would have sent the first Pix under the label of a check.

Server (deploy):
- The event `antecipacao.desembolso.conferir` carries the restriction from its NAME, in
  `EventDispatchService.dispatch` and `dispatchManualEvent`, with or without the field
  (a `false` included), plain or namespaced by DISPATCH_EVENT.
- The desk's generic execute route diverts any request that asks to only check.
- One gate for the sweep and the desk (`installationHonoursCheckOnly`).
- The installer writes a description the edit route accepts (the template's when it
  fits, the short one otherwise): 39 of 177 templates installed an action that
  `PUT /custom-actions/:id` then refused. The limit is one constant, read by the spec
  from the DTOs.

Template (reaches a tenant on REINSTALL): `antecipacao-validar-desembolso` version 2
- a check has its own number on `tentativas[]` (`conferencia`, `tentativa`), no `n`;
- `repetivel: false` on a refusal of the list;

was not a 14-digit CNPJ with a 409.

  creates-or-recognizes the PERSON in `people` (externalRef = lead id, the
  lead's e-mail as contact) and records `identidade.tipo = 'pessoa'` with

  `tipo: 'empresa'`). Anything else is a 409 in plain pt-BR. A 409 from the
  block (same lead, another CPF) becomes a human sentence.
- statusForLead: an individual shows name + CPF, no company/representative;
  the only pending item is the e-mail the term goes to.
- CessionSignatureService.request: an individual signs in her own name —
  no `companies.evaluate`; the record says why (`reason
  CEDENTE_PESSOA_FISICA`, `modo proprio`, role `titular`). The envelope,
  W8's event and the per-line are the same code as for a company.
- gerar-termo (model 2): the assignor line of a CPF reads "pessoa física,
  CPF 000.000.000-00"; a company's line is unchanged (same text and hash).
- Desk: register form takes CPF or CNPJ, the PF badge is no longer red and
  an individual can be enabled; the identity card shows the individual.

D1 - every receivables product accepts an individual by default
(exigeCedentePJ: false in the catalog and in the policy seed). Requiring a
legal entity is the house's call and a floor: the policy's true wins over
the product (ladder FLOORS only-on), a product may only tighten it. The
decision table 1.4.0 drops the general PF refusal (the score turns the
requirement into an impediment, which the table refuses); the bank channel
extension is dispensed on a table without that refusal (whenAnchorAbsent:

D2 - term model 3: the assignor fully qualified (PF: name, CPF,
nationality, marital status, profession, address; PJ: corporate name, CNPJ,
seat) and the place of the deed. Anything missing means no term
(SEM_QUALIFICACAO_DO_CEDENTE with semTermo.faltando, or
SEM_LUGAR_DA_CELEBRACAO). Stored model-2 terms keep their text and hash.

analysis).

^\d{11}$ of the unmasked document; an alphanumeric CNPJ is a company.
B2 - exigencias[act].pessoa ('declared' | 'verified'); verified requires an
e-mail whose possession people proved (POST /people/contacts/resolve).
R1 - identidade is compared through the real deepMergeJson; null only to
delete a key the record has; an individual record has no company keys.
R3/R7 - the envelope goes to the LEAD's e-mail, checked against people;
a different proven e-mail is a pending item, nothing is sent.

synchronous outcome follows the outcomeOf rule too.

fluxos.flow.spec.ts (renamed from resultado.flow.spec.ts) runs each of the

body:
feat(opensign): mutual TLS on the engine's port — the docker runtime hides the origin

Owner's decision (16/10): "Fazer o mTLS antes de prod". Measured in staging: inside the Launch
docker runtime every connection reaches the container from 172.17.0.1 (docker-proxy), from outside
and from the e-signature LXC alike, so an origin allowlist cannot work here.

- Caddy on 8090 is TLS only, client_auth require_and_verify against OUR CA; the gate header stays
  (defense in depth). Material comes from the service env (base64 PEM) and the entrypoint writes it
  0600; SERVER_URL must be https.
- scripts/opensign/emitir-tls.sh: EC P-256 CA (key never leaves the operator's machine) + server cert
  (SAN = mesh host) + client cert CN=bb-e-signature (clientAuth). Idempotent.
- deploy-opensign.sh: no HTTP health (healthPath empty → liveness by the container, no public route
  or name), --recriar, mTLS material into the service env and into opensign-local-<env>.env, the locks
  checked over mTLS (gate token via a 0600 header file, not argv), 1 h wait for the image pull.
- prova-assinatura.mjs over node:https with the client cert and the CA pinned.

Proof against the built image: PROVA OK 15/15 — plain HTTP 400 without reaching Parse; no client cert →
ERR_SSL_TLSV13_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED; cert without gate 403; cert + gate 200 over TLSv1.3; signPdf →
COMPLETED with hash, certificate and the signer's ip. Also refused: a client cert from another CA
(curl 56), the server cert used as client (56), and a client that does not pin our CA (60).

title: fix(workflows): an execution never starts inside the rewrite in place (P6, CBP review)
body:
fix(workflows): an execution never starts inside the rewrite in place (P6, CBP review)

The check for executions in flight and the rewrite run in one transaction,
but an execution could start between them: its running row did not exist
when the check counted, and it read the old steps. Both sides now take one
advisory lock per workflow (definition-lock.ts): the rewrite takes it
exclusive before counting; an execution takes it shared to write its running
row, and reads the layout again under it. The check also counts a wait state
just resolved whose execution is still suspended (the resolver flips the wait
state before it marks the execution running).

Integration spec (real Postgres, 20/20): an authorization dispatched while the
rewrite holds its transaction starts only after the commit and runs the new
steps (without the lock it starts in the window, on the old steps); a resolved
wait not yet resumed leads to a new copy; the acceptance flow rewritten in
place keeps its id and trigger, the event matcher finds that one flow, and the
real AcceptanceGateService still refuses an unsigned acceptance on it.

title: fix(antecipacao): trava de recebíveis no handshake do banking (BB #629) — proposta declara, aceite leva o lienId
body:
fix(antecipacao): trava de recebíveis no handshake do banking (BB #629) — proposta declara, aceite leva o lienId

The banking block creates the lien BEFORE calling the acceptance, so the CCP side follows its handshake:

- GET proposal answers `repaymentLock { amountCents, destinationAccountId, sourceDocuments, externalReference,
  expiresAt, payerName? }` — exactly `CreditRepaymentLock`, deterministic, reference `credit-proposal:<id>`.
  A lock that cannot be formed (no fund account UUID, payers without document, >20 payers) is not offered.
- POST acceptance takes `repaymentLock { lienId, externalReference }` (declared in the DTO: the whitelist pipe
  would drop it). A lock proposal without it, or with another reference, is refused 409 with a neutral sentence
  (the bank undoes the lien); a lien sent for a non-lock proposal is refused too. No echo in the answer.
- The lien is stamped on the proposal (`travaBanco`) before W8; validar-aceite refuses without it
  (TRAVA_AUSENTE) and copies it to the operation (`trava`, no `trava_pendente`) and every title
  (`lienId`, `lienExternalReference`).
- antecipacao-trava-baas resolves the proposal reference to the operation (by propostaId); `created` before the
  operation is a no-op; NEW `baas.lien.capture.failed` (holdLeftActive) stamps `trava.alertaMesa` and audits
  `trava.captura.falhou`; events without an operation alert. W10 subscribes the new event in its own
  subscription (no double delivery for tenants that already have the lien one). W7 untouched.
- Contract test copies the banking types and shape check (credit.facade, http-credit.facade, banking-core).

* fix(credit-install): turn counterparties on only with an e-signature provider (Catalisa OpenSign)

The credit package installer turned `contrapartes.ativo` on without any provider
configuration in the e-signature block, so every envelope was refused with 404
("default config not found") and houses were left without acceptance.

- New step `esignature-provider` (before counterparties): keeps a default active
  provider config; otherwise creates the platform's self-hosted OpenSign config in
  the tenant's organization from OPENSIGN_LOCAL_* (baseUrl, apiPrefix, appId,
  masterKey, gateToken); missing env -> degraded. Credentials never logged/returned.
- Counterparties: on only when connected; absent -> switched OFF (not `desligadoEm`,
  nothing linked is deleted); unknown -> left as is; the desk's `desligadoEm` is kept.
- Webhook safety net: pending envelope -> one POST /requests/:id/refresh (5 s)
  before deciding, in CessionSignatureService.refresh and AcceptanceGateService.
- Copilot > Pacotes shows "Assinatura eletrônica: Catalisa (conectada)" /
  "não disponível neste ambiente".

body:
feat(antecipacao): PF by default, fully qualified term (model 3), checked signer e-mail

Owner's decisions (15/10/2026) and the review of #1947.

D1 - every receivables product accepts an individual by default
(exigeCedentePJ: false in the catalog and in the policy seed). Requiring a
legal entity is the house's call and a floor: the policy's true wins over
the product (ladder FLOORS only-on), a product may only tighten it. The
decision table 1.4.0 drops the general PF refusal (the score turns the
requirement into an impediment, which the table refuses); the bank channel
extension is dispensed on a table without that refusal (whenAnchorAbsent:
'not-needed') and still applies to tenants on 1.2.x.

D2 - term model 3: the assignor fully qualified (PF: name, CPF,
nationality, marital status, profession, address; PJ: corporate name, CNPJ,
seat) and the place of the deed. Anything missing means no term
(SEM_QUALIFICACAO_DO_CEDENTE with semTermo.faltando, or
SEM_LUGAR_DA_CELEBRACAO). Stored model-2 terms keep their text and hash.
The desk form and the bank channel ask for the fields (GET/PUT
/credit-channel/v1/assignor-profile, ASSIGNOR_PROFILE_INCOMPLETE before the
analysis).

B1 - the term classifies the assignor like assignorDocumentOf: PF only on
^\d{11}$ of the unmasked document; an alphanumeric CNPJ is a company.
B2 - exigencias[act].pessoa ('declared' | 'verified'); verified requires an
e-mail whose possession people proved (POST /people/contacts/resolve).
R1 - identidade is compared through the real deepMergeJson; null only to
delete a key the record has; an individual record has no company keys.
R3/R7 - the envelope goes to the LEAD's e-mail, checked against people;
a different proven e-mail is a pending item, nothing is sent.
R5 - the desk offers "Habilitar" to an individual only when the house
policy does not require a legal entity, with matching hints.

body:
feat(opensign): motor OpenSign local no Launch, atrás de um portão (#1975)

* feat(opensign): local signing engine image for the Launch, behind a gate

The owner chose the self-hosted OpenSign as the signing engine behind the e-signature block (16/10):
the signer signs on our page; OpenSign signs the PDF, hashes it and issues the certificate by REST.

- docker/opensign: opensign/opensignserver (pinned digest) + MongoDB 7 on loopback + Caddy gate on
  :8090. /api/* needs X-OpenSign-Gate (the Launch mesh is reachable from outside and signPdf
  authenticates nothing with IsEnableOTP=false); masterKeyIps patched to loopback; PDF stamp and
  certificate logo patched to Catalisa; OpenSign SMTP off. Each patch is grep-checked in the build.
- scripts/opensign/deploy-opensign.sh: the docker/traccar recipe — image from the commit, secrets
  generated into ~/.config/catalisa/opensign-local-<env>.env (0600), docker service in the blocks
  project with a volume and no public domain, then the lock and the end-to-end proof.
- scripts/opensign/prova-assinatura.mjs: owner + signer + document → signPdf → completed with a
  signed PDF (/ByteRange), hash, audit trail and certificate; 403 without the gate.

Proved locally against the built image: PROVA OK (12/12).

title: feat(e-signature): OpenSign provider speaks mutual TLS to the engine
body:
feat(e-signature): OpenSign provider speaks mutual TLS to the engine

Owner's decision (16/10): "Fazer o mTLS antes de prod". The engine (panel repo docker/opensign, #1981)
requires a client certificate signed by our CA on its only port; inside the Launch docker runtime
every connection comes from 172.17.0.1, so the lock is WHO, not where.

- engineTlsFromEnv(): OPENSIGN_TLS_CA_PEM_B64, OPENSIGN_TLS_CLIENT_CERT_PEM_B64 and
  OPENSIGN_TLS_CLIENT_KEY_PEM_B64 from the SERVICE env (never a tenant's ProviderConfig); all three or
  none — a partial or broken set throws instead of talking without a certificate.
- Every request to the engine (REST, PDF upload, file download) carries Bun's fetch `tls` option
  {ca, cert, key}: our CA pinned, the client certificate presented.
- With mutual TLS configured an http baseUrl is refused (ENGINE_TLS_REQUIRES_HTTPS), never downgraded;
  material from the env outside Bun fails loud (ENGINE_TLS_RUNTIME: Node would drop `tls` in silence).
- Boot logs whether mutual TLS is on and errors loud on a broken set. README: the three variables.

Tests: tests/unit/e-signature 30 files, 363 passed (7 in opensign.mtls.test.ts; the fake PEM key is
assembled at run time so the secrets scanner does not see a literal header).
Runtime proof (Bun 1.4, the real provider against the engine image with mTLS): with cert + CA →
ensureAccount OK; nothing → refused; CA pinned without client cert → refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Owner's decision (16/10): "Fazer o mTLS antes de prod". Measured in staging: inside the Launch

- deploy-opensign.sh: no HTTP health (healthPath empty → liveness by the container, no public route
